**13.12.8**  Galloping this way and that, afflicted by weariness and thirst, the king beheld a most lovely lake brimming with excellent water; and plunging into the lake, dear son, he let his horse drink.

**13.12.9**  Then, when the horse had drunk, that best of kings tied it to a tree, and entering the water to bathe, the king attained womanhood.

**13.12.10**  Seeing himself turned into a woman, that best of kings was abashed, his whole being given over to anxious thought, his senses and mind confounded.

**13.12.11**  "How shall I mount the horse, how shall I return to the city? I performed the rite called Agniṣṭu, and a hundred sons of my own loins were granted me—

**13.12.12**  sons born of great strength. What shall I now say of them to my wives, and to the people of city and countryside?"

**13.12.13**  Softness, slenderness, and timidity—these the sages, who behold the truth and meaning of dharma, have declared the qualities of woman; while exertion, hardness, and valor are the qualities of man.

**13.12.14**  "My manhood is utterly lost, and womanhood has come upon me by some agency; in this state of womanhood, how can I bring myself to mount the horse again?"

**13.12.15**  Then with great distress that lord of men mounted the horse and, turned into a woman, returned to the city, dear son—that best of kings.

**13.12.16**  His sons and wives and servants, and the folk of city and countryside, perceiving "what then is this?", were struck with the utmost amazement.

**13.12.17**  Then that royal sage, now a woman, best of speakers, said: "I had set out to hunt, firmly surrounded by my forces; but, deluded by fate, I strayed and entered a fearsome wilderness.

**13.12.18**  And in that most terrible wilderness, parched with thirst and bereft of my wits, I beheld a lake of most lovely aspect, thronged with birds.

**13.12.19**  Having plunged therein, I was made a woman—plainly by fate, there is no doubt—as though I had not yet had my fill of sons, of wives, and of wealth."

**13.12.20**  Then that best of kings, now a woman, said to his sons: "In harmony enjoy this kingdom; I shall go to the forest, my dear ones." And having consecrated his hundred sons, the king departed to the forest.

**13.12.21**  In the hermitage, dear son, an ascetic took that woman to wife; and by that ascetic a hundred sons were born to her in the hermitage as well.

**13.12.22**  Then taking these sons, she said to her former sons: "You are my sons begotten in manhood, and these hundred are my sons in womanhood.

**13.12.23**  Enjoy the kingdom together, as brothers, my dear ones." And those brothers, united, then enjoyed the kingdom together.

**13.12.24**  Seeing them enjoy that excellent kingdom in brotherly accord, Indra, lord of the gods, overwhelmed with wrath, reflected: "I have done that royal sage a service, not an injury."

**13.12.25**  Then in the guise of a brāhmaṇa, the king of the gods, lord of a hundred sacrifices, went to the city and sowed dissension among those sons of the king.

**13.12.26**  "There is no brotherhood among brothers, even among the sons of one father: for the sake of the kingdom the gods and demons, sons of Kaśyapa, fell to strife.

**13.12.27**  You are the offspring of Bhaṅgāśvana, while the others are the sons of an ascetic—just as the gods and the demons were the sons of Kaśyapa; yet your paternal kingdom is being enjoyed by the ascetic's sons."

**13.12.28**  Set at variance by Indra, they struck one another down in battle; and hearing this, the ascetic-woman, sore stricken, broke into weeping.

**13.12.29**  Approaching her in the disguise of a brāhmaṇa, Indra then inquired: "With what grief are you tormented, that you weep, O fair-faced one?"

**13.12.30**  Seeing the brāhmaṇa, that woman piteously replied: "My two hundred sons, O brāhmaṇa, have been laid low by time.

**13.12.31**  I was once a king, O brāhmaṇa, and there a hundred sons were begotten by me, handsome and valiant, O best of the twice-born.

**13.12.32**  Once, gone out to the hunt, I strayed in a dense forest and, plunging into a lake, was made a woman, O best of brāhmaṇas; and having established my sons in the kingdom, I then withdrew to the forest.

**13.12.33**  And to me as a woman a hundred sons were begotten by a great-souled ascetic in the hermitage, O brāhmaṇa; these too I brought to the city.

**13.12.34**  And by the working of time enmity arose among them, O brāhmaṇa; this I lament, O best of brāhmaṇas, overwhelmed by fate."

**13.12.35**  Seeing her in her grief, Indra spoke harsh words: "Of old, O lady, you wrought me grief most hard to bear,

**13.12.36**  by performing a sacrifice hateful to Indra, slighting me, O perverse one. I am Indra, O foolish one, and the enmity I have requited upon you."

**13.12.37**  But seeing Indra, the royal sage fell with bowed head at his feet: "Be gracious, O best of the gods; that sacrifice was performed by me in longing for sons, O tiger among the gods; in this you ought to forgive me."

**13.12.38**  Well pleased by her obeisance, Indra granted a boon: "Which of your sons, O king, shall live? Tell me—those born to you as a woman, or those who came to you as a man?"

**13.12.39**  Then the ascetic-woman, with reverently folded hands, said to Śakra: "Let those who were born to me as a woman live, O Vāsava."

**13.12.40**  But Indra, astonished and delighted, questioned that woman again: "How are the sons you begot as a man become hateful to you?

**13.12.41**  How is it that your love is greater for those born when you were a woman? I wish to hear the reason; this you ought to tell me here."

**13.12.42**  The woman said: A woman's love is the greater—not so a man's; therefore, O Śakra, let those live who were born to me when I was made a woman.

**13.12.43**  Bhīṣma said: When she had spoken thus, Indra, well pleased, replied: "Let all your sons live here, O truthful one.

**13.12.44**  And choose a boon, O lord of kings, whatever you desire, O steadfast in vows—manhood or womanhood, whichever you crave from me."

**13.12.45**  The woman said: I choose womanhood itself, O Śakra, since you are gracious, O Vāsava.

**13.12.46**  Thus addressed, Indra, lord of the gods, replied to that woman: "How is it that, forsaking manhood, you prefer womanhood, O mighty one?"

**13.12.47**  Thus addressed, that best of kings, now a woman, replied: "In the union of woman and man, the pleasure of the woman is ever the greater; for this reason, O Śakra, I choose womanhood itself."

**13.12.48**  "And I take greater delight in womanhood—truly, O best of gods; I am content in my woman's state. Go now, O lord of the gods."

**13.12.49**  Saying "So be it," and taking leave of her, Indra departed to heaven. Thus, O great king, is the woman's pleasure declared the greater.

**13.13.1**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: What ought a man to do who seeks the welfare that sustains worldly life? And of what conduct should he be as he carries on the course of the world?

**13.13.2**  Bhīṣma said: Of action by the body there are three kinds, by speech four kinds, and by the mind three; these ten paths of evil action one should renounce.

**13.13.3**  The slaying of living beings, theft, and intercourse with another's wife—these three sins of the body one should utterly shun.

**13.13.4**  Idle babble, harshness, slander, and falsehood likewise—these four sins of speech, O lord of kings, one should neither utter nor even ponder.

**13.13.5**  Freedom from coveting another's goods, good will toward all beings, and the conviction that actions bear fruit—this threefold course one should practice with the mind.

**13.13.6**  Therefore let a man do no evil by speech, body, or mind; for doing deeds good or evil, he tastes the fruit of each in turn.

**13.14.1**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: O mighty one, declare to me the names of the grandsire-lord, of Śambhu, of Babhru, of him who is the māyā of the universe, and his exalted majesty in truth.

**13.14.2**  Bhīṣma said: O preceptor of gods and demons, O divine Viṣṇu, it is you who ought to speak that which Yudhiṣṭhira asks of me concerning Śiva, who has the universe for his form.

**13.14.3**  The thousand names of the god, which were proclaimed of old by Taṇḍin, sprung from Brahmā, and were once set forth before Brahmā in the world of Brahmā.

**13.14.4**  Let these sages too, rich in austerity—Dvaipāyana foremost among them—men of noble vows and self-restraint, listen as you speak.

**13.14.5**  Tell us, O mighty one, of the high glory of him who is the Unmoving, the Giver of joy, the Sacrificer, the Protector, the Creator of all, who is Fire itself—of the Shaven-headed and the Matted-locked one.

**13.14.6**  Vāsudeva said: The course of the Lord's deeds cannot be known in its truth.

**13.14.7**  The gods, led by Hiraṇyagarbha and Indra, and the great sages of subtle vision, do not know his end nor his beginning. How then could he, the goal of the good, be known by a mere man?

**13.14.8**  Yet of that blessed Lord, the slayer of the asuras, the master of all vows, I shall recount to you some of his attributes, as faithfully as I am able.

**13.14.9**  Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, the blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa sipped water, made himself pure, and began to relate the attributes of that great-souled and wise one.

**13.14.10**  Vāsudeva said: Listen, O foremost of brāhmaṇas, and you too, dear Yudhiṣṭhira; and you, son of the River, attend to the names of the Lord of the world.

**13.14.11**  How in time past I gained, for the sake of Sāmba, that which is most hard to win, and how the blessed Lord was once beheld by me through deep meditation—

**13.14.12**  After Śambara had been slain of old by the wise son of Rukmiṇī, when the twelfth year had passed, Jāmbavatī said to me—

**13.14.13**  Beholding the little sons of Rukmiṇī—Pradyumna, Cārudeṣṇa and the rest—and herself longing for a son, she came to me and spoke, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

**13.14.14**  "Grant me without delay, O Acyuta, a son who is valiant, foremost among the strong, lovely in form, free of all blemish, the equal of yourself."

**13.14.15**  "For there is nothing in the three worlds beyond your reach; should you wish it, you could create other worlds, O upholder of the Yadu line."

**13.14.16**  "Living on air and wasting away for twelve years, by propitiating the Lord of creatures, you begot upon Rukmiṇī her sons."

**13.14.17**  "Cārudeṣṇa and Sucāru, Cāruveṣa and Yaśodhara, Cāruśravas and Cāruyaśas, Pradyumna, and Śaṃbhu as well—"

**13.14.18**  "Even as those sons of fair prowess were begotten of Rukmiṇī, so grant to me also a son endowed with strength."

**13.14.19**  Urged in this way by the lady, I said to the fair-waisted one: "Give me leave, O queen; I shall do as you ask." And she said to me: "Go, for victory and for blessing."

**13.14.20**  "May Brahmā, Śiva, and Kāśyapa, the rivers, the gods who follow the mind, the fields and the herbs, the bearers of the sacrifice, the sacred metres, the hosts of sages, and the Earth—"

**13.14.21**  "the oceans, the sacrificial fees, the chants, the constellations, the ancestors, the planets, the wives of the gods, the daughters of the gods, and the mothers of the gods—"

**13.14.22**  "the cosmic ages of the Manus, the cattle, the Moon, Savitṛ, Hari, Sāvitrī and the knowledge of Brahman, the seasons, the years, the nights—"

**13.14.23**  "the moments, the instants, the hours, the wink-spans of time, and the turning of the ages—may they guard you wherever you go, O Yādava, bringer of joy. Go your way unharmed and watchful, O sinless one."

**13.14.24**  Thus blessed by her with rites of well-being, having taken leave of that daughter of the lord of the apes, I went to her father, that best of men, to her mother, and to King Āhuka—

**13.14.25**  and laid before them what the deeply grieving daughter of the lord of the Vidyādharas had asked of me; then, sore at heart, I took leave of them, and of Gada and of mighty Rāma as well.

**13.14.26**  Having obtained the leave of my elders, I called to mind Tārkṣya; he bore me to Himavat, and upon reaching it I dismissed him.

**13.14.27**  There upon that noblest of mountains I beheld wondrous sights, and I saw a holy ground supreme among the seats of austerity, a most excellent hermitage—

**13.14.28**  the divine hermitage of the great-souled Upamanyu, son of Vyāghrapad, honoured by gods and gandharvas, endowed with a sacred and Brahmic splendour.

**13.14.29**  It was rich with dhava, kakubha, kadamba and coconut trees; with kurabaka, ketaka, jambu and pāṭala; with banyan, varuṇaka, vatsanābha and bilva; with sarala, kapittha, priyāla, sāla and palm;

**13.14.30**  with jujube, kunda and punnāga, with aśoka, mango and atimukta, with bhallātaka, madhūka, campaka and breadfruit;

**13.14.31**  graced with woodland trees of many kinds bearing fruit and flower, strewn with blossoming shrubs and creepers, made lovely with thickets of plantain.

**13.14.32**  It was adorned with trees whose fruits gave food to birds of many sorts, and beautified with rows of woodland set each in its fitting place.

**13.14.33**  It teemed with deer, elephants, tigers, lions and panthers; was thronged with antelope and peacocks, beset with wildcats and serpents, frequented by herds of beasts of many breeds, by buffaloes and bears.

**13.14.34**  There a pleasant breeze blew, laden with the pollen of many flowers, perfumed with the ichor of elephants, and filled with the songs of celestial women.

**13.14.35**  With the murmur of cascades and the cries of birds, with the auspicious trumpeting of elephants, with the lofty songs of the kiṃnaras, and the holy sounds of those who chant the Sāman, O hero—

**13.14.36**  —it was such as others could not so much as conceive in the mind; adorned with lakes, beautified with broad fire-shelters, and carpeted with kuśa grass.

**13.14.37**  Adorned, O king, by the daughter of Jahnu with her holy and purifying waters, ever-frequented by her, it was graced by great-souled seers, foremost among upholders of dharma, who blazed like fire.

**13.14.38**  It was adorned all around by foremost brāhmaṇas—ascetics who lived on air, who drank only water, who were ever at their muttered prayers, who scoured their vessels clean, who were ever in meditation, who fed on smoke, who drank only warmth, and who lived upon milk alone.

**13.14.39**  There were those who grazed like cattle, those who ground their grain on stones, those whose mortar was their own teeth, those who lived on the sun's rays, those who drank only foam, and those who roamed like the wild deer.

**13.14.40**  Beholding these men who upheld their grievous vows in the rigour of austerity, with wide-open eyes I set myself to enter in.

**13.14.41**  Well honoured by the hosts of gods, the great-souled ones, Śiva and the rest, doers of holy deeds, O Bhārata, that circle of hermitage ever shone, O king, like the orb of the sun in the heavens.

**13.14.42**  There the mongooses sported with the serpents, and the tigers with the deer, as friends—through the power and the virtue of nearness to those whose austerity blazed forth.

**13.14.43**  In that supreme hermitage, delightful to all beings, frequented by tigers among the twice-born who had mastered the Vedas and their auxiliaries—

**13.14.44**  —and by great-souled sages renowned for their manifold vows, even as I entered I beheld the Lord, wearing matted locks and bark-cloth garments.

**13.14.45**  Blazing like fire with splendour and with austerity, seated amid his pupils, serene, youthful, a bull among brāhmaṇas—Upamanyu spoke to me as I bowed my head before him.

**13.14.46**  "Welcome, O lotus-eyed one. Our austerities have borne their fruit, since you who are worthy of worship pay us honour, and you who are worthy to be beheld desire to behold us."

**13.14.47**  Then, with palms joined together, I asked after the welfare of his beasts and birds, of his sacred fires, of his observance of dharma, and of the band of his pupils.

**13.14.48**  Then the blessed sage said to me with words most gentle and kind: "You shall surely obtain, O Kṛṣṇa, a son who is your own equal—of this there is no doubt."

**13.14.49**  "Undertaking a most mighty austerity, propitiate the Lord, the Ruler; for here, O Adhokṣaja, the god disports himself together with his consort."

**13.14.50**  "In this very place, O Janārdana, the gods together with the hosts of sages, in days of old, having gratified that best of deities by austerity, by chastity, by truth and by self-restraint, obtained their fair desires."

**13.14.51**  "That blessed Lord, the treasure-house of all splendours and austerities, dwells here together with the Goddess—he, the inconceivable one, who sends forth and withdraws all states of being, both fair and foul—the very one whom you entreat, O slayer of foes."

**13.14.52**  "Hiraṇyakaśipu, the dānava who once shook Mount Meru, obtained from Śarva the lordship over all the immortals for a full ten million years."

**13.14.53**  "His foremost son, renowned as Mandara, by a boon of Mahādeva did battle with Śakra for ten million years."

**13.14.54**  "Even the dread discus of Viṣṇu and the thunderbolt of Ākhaṇḍala, O dear Keśava, were of old shattered upon the limbs of that demon Graha."

**13.14.55**  "And the gods, sorely oppressed by that mighty Graha, slew in their turn many a lord of the asuras who had been granted boons by Śiva."

**13.14.56**  "Well pleased with Vidyutprabha too, he gave him the sovereignty of the three worlds; for a hundred thousand years he became the lord of all worlds, and the god said: 'You shall ever be my attendant.'"

**13.14.57**  "Likewise the Lord granted him ten thousand sons, and the blessed Unborn one gave him the island of Kuśa to rule as a kingdom."

**13.14.58**  "So too there was a great asura named Śatamukha, fashioned by the Creator, who for a full hundred years offered up the fire with his own flesh; and the blessed Śaṃkara, well pleased, said to him: 'What shall I do for you?'"

**13.14.59**  "And Śatamukha answered him: 'Let mine be a wondrous power of yoga, and grant me, O best of the gods, strength that endures forever.'"

**13.14.60**  "And Kratu, son of the Self-existent, of old, longing for offspring, entered into himself through yoga for three hundred years."

**13.14.61**  "To him the god granted a thousand sons, each the equal of Kratu himself. You know, O Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of yoga who is sung of by the gods—of this there is no doubt."

**13.14.62**  "The Vālakhilyas, it is said, were once slighted by Maghavat; and they in their wrath gratified the blessed Rudra by their austerities."

**13.14.63**  "And to them the best of gods, the Lord of the world, well pleased, declared: 'By your austerity you shall bring forth Suparṇa, the carrier-off of the soma.'"

**13.14.64**  "Through the wrath of Mahādeva the waters of old were destroyed, and the gods brought other waters into being by means of the seven-skulled rite."

**13.14.65**  "The wife of Atri too, a speaker of sacred truth, forsook her husband, saying: 'Never again shall I be subject to the will of that sage'; and so saying she went, it is said, for refuge to Mahādeva."

**13.14.66**  "Taking no food, in fear of Atri, she lay even upon pestles for three hundred years, to win the grace of Bhava."

**13.14.67**  "To her the god said, smiling: 'A son shall surely be born to you, and in your own line he shall attain the renown you desire, bearing your name.'"

**13.14.68**  "Śākalya, a man of disciplined soul, propitiated Bhava for nine hundred years with the sacrifice of the mind, O Keśava."

**13.14.69**  "And the blessed Lord, well pleased, said to him: 'You shall become an author of treatises, my child; your fame shall be imperishable throughout the three worlds, and let your lineage be undying, adorned with great sages.'"

**13.14.70**  "There was too a renowned sage named Sāvarṇi in the Kṛta age; here he practised austerity for six thousand years."

**13.14.71**  "To him the blessed Rudra appeared in person and said: 'I am pleased with you, O sinless one. You shall become a maker of treatises, renowned throughout the world, free of age and death.'"

**13.14.72**  "And how I too of old beheld in person the God of gods, the all-pervading Lord, Paśupati himself, of that also hear, dear Mādhava."

**13.14.73**  "And for what purpose I once, with strenuous effort, propitiated the mighty Mahādeva of great splendour—that too hear in full."

**13.14.74**  "And whatever I formerly gained from the God of gods, from Maheśvara, all of that, entire and without omission, I shall now relate to you, O sinless one."

**13.14.75**  "Long ago, in the Kṛta age, my dear one, there lived a sage of great renown, known as Vyāghrapad, master of the Vedas and their auxiliaries. I was his son, and Dhaumya was my younger brother."

**13.14.76**  "Now once upon a time, O Mādhava, I came at play, together with Dhaumya, to the hermitage of sages whose souls were purified."

**13.14.77**  "And there I saw a milk-cow being milked, and I marked that its milk was sweet to the taste, like the very nectar of immortality."

**13.14.78**  "Now flour, O Mādhava, stirred together with water, used to be brought to the two of us to drink, under the name of 'milk.'"

**13.14.79**  "Then once, my dear one, I tasted the milk of a cow, and thereafter the flour-water, O dear one, no longer gave me any pleasure."

**13.14.80**  "Then in my childish way I said to my own mother: 'Give me food made with milk-porridge to eat.'"

**13.14.81**  "Then my mother, filled with grief and sorrow, embracing me out of a mother's love and kissing me upon the head, O Mādhava, said to me:"

**13.14.82**  "'Whence is milk-porridge to come, my child, for sages of purified souls who dwell ever in the forest and feed upon roots, bulbs and fruits?'"

**13.14.83**  "'Without first winning the grace of the three-eyed Virūpākṣa, the giver of boons, the unmoving and undecaying Sthāṇu—whence, my child, is milk-porridge to come, or comforts, or fine raiment?'"

**13.14.84**  Take refuge always in Śaṃkara, my child, with your whole being; by his grace, little son, you shall win from your desires their fruit.

**13.14.85**  Having heard those words of my mother, O slayer of foes, from that day onward an unwavering devotion to Mahādeva took root in me.

**13.14.86**  Then, undertaking austerity, I set myself to please Śaṃkara, standing for a thousand divine years poised upon the tips of my toes.

**13.14.87**  For one hundred years I lived then on fruit alone; for a second hundred I ate withered leaves; for a third I subsisted on water; and for seven hundred years more I fed upon air alone.

**13.14.88**  Then Mahādeva, the Lord and Master of all worlds, was pleased; assuming the form of Śakra and encircled by all the hosts of the gods, he became the thousand-eyed one, thunderbolt-handed and of great renown.

**13.14.89**  He mounted a mighty elephant, white as nectar, with red eyes, ears held stiffly erect, fierce in its rut, its trunk coiled, terrible to behold, and armed with four tusks.

**13.14.90**  Mounted upon it, the Lord came on, blazing with his own splendour, crowned with a diadem and adorned with necklaces and armlets.

**13.14.91**  A white parasol was held above his head, the Apsarases waited upon him, and the music of celestial Gandharvas resounded around him.

**13.14.92**  Then the lord of the gods spoke to me: 'I am pleased with you, O best of the twice-born; choose from me whatever boon dwells in your heart.'

**13.14.93**  But hearing Śakra's words, O Kṛṣṇa, my heart was not gladdened, and I then spoke to the king of the gods these words.

**13.14.94**  'I desire no boon from you, nor from any other deity save Mahādeva, O gentle one; this truth I tell you.'

**13.14.95**  'At a word from Paśupati I would gladly become at once a worm, or a tree with countless branches; but the sovereignty and splendour even of the three worlds, if not born of Paśupati's gracious boon, is unwelcome to me.'

**13.14.96**  'Even an insect or a moth I would gladly become at Śaṃkara's command; but the dominion over the three worlds, were it given by you, O Śakra, I do not desire.'

**13.14.97**  'So long as Paśupati, my Lord and God, whose locks are bound with the pure crescent fragment of the moon, is not pleased with me, so long shall I bear the sorrows ordained for the body, smitten by a hundred old ages, deaths, and births.'

**13.14.98**  'Without winning the favour of Rudra—radiant as sun, moon, and fire, the essence of the three worlds, boundless, primordial, unique, unaging, undying—what man in this world could ever attain peace?'

**13.14.99**  Śakra said: 'And what is your reason concerning the Lord, the Cause of all causes, that you should seek favour from no god other than him?'

**13.14.100**  Upamanyu said: 'What need have you of other reasons? The Lord is the Cause of all causes. We have never heard that the emblem of any other is worshipped by the gods.'

**13.14.101**  'Whose emblem, save that of Maheśvara, is worshipped by all the gods, or has been worshipped of old? Tell me, if you have heard of any such.'

**13.14.102**  'He whose emblem Brahmā and Viṣṇu, and you too together with the gods, forever worship—he therefore is the most supreme of all.'

**13.14.103**  'From him alone do I desire a boon, or even death itself, O Kauśika. Go or stay as you please, O Śakra, slayer of Bala.'

**13.14.104**  'Let it be, then—whether a boon be mine from Maheśvara, or even a curse; I desire no other deity, not though it bring me the fruit of all my wishes.'

**13.14.105**  Having thus spoken to the lord of the gods, my senses troubled with grief and brooding, 'Why is it that Rudra is not gracious to me?'—in that very instant I beheld once again that same Airāvata.

**13.14.106**  It had taken the form of a bull, like a swan, like jasmine, like the moon, gleaming as the lotus-stalk and the white water-lily, vast as the very Ocean of Milk before my eyes.

**13.14.107**  Huge of body, with a black tail and eyes tawny as honey, adorned on every side with a girth of pure gold.

**13.14.108**  Red-eyed, with a great muzzle, fine ears, fine flanks at the haunch, well-formed sides, broad shoulders—shapely and lovely to behold.

**13.14.109**  Its hump shone, rising full upon its shoulder, like the peak of a snow-clad mountain, like the crest of a white cloud.

**13.14.110**  Mounted upon it together with Umā, the Lord, God of gods, the great Mahādeva, shone like the lord of the stars on the night of the full moon.

**13.14.111**  The fire born of his radiance, charged with clouds and thunder, stood enveloping all things like a thousand suns at once.

**13.14.112**  The Lord, of vast and mighty splendour, was like the all-consuming fire, poised as if to burn up every being at the ending of an age.

**13.14.113**  When that splendour, hard to gaze upon, had spread on every side, my heart was troubled once more, and I pondered, 'What is this?'

**13.14.114**  That splendour, having filled all the ten directions for but a moment, was in an instant stilled again by the power of the God of gods.

**13.14.115**  Then I beheld the Lord Maheśvara, the Steadfast One, standing there—gentle, seated upon the bull, like a smokeless flame—the Supreme Lord together with Pārvatī, fair in every limb.

**13.14.116**  The blue-throated, great-souled, unattached one, treasury of all splendours, the Steadfast, with eighteen arms, adorned with every ornament.

**13.14.117**  The God clad in white garments, garlanded and anointed in white, bearing a white banner, unassailable, wearing the white sacred thread.

**13.14.118**  He was surrounded by his celestial attendants—singing, dancing, leaping here and there—each equal to himself in valour.

**13.14.119**  Crowned with the crescent moon, pale-bright as the autumn moon newly risen, blazing with his three eyes like three suns risen at once.

**13.14.120**  And upon the God's body, fair of hue, there shone a garland woven of golden lotuses and set with jewels.

**13.14.121**  And the weapons of Bhava, of measureless splendour—embodied and wholly made of radiance—these I beheld, O Govinda.

**13.14.122**  The bow of that great-souled one, gleaming like a thousand rainbows, renowned by the name of Pināka—and that bow was itself a mighty serpent.

**13.14.123**  Seven-headed, vast of body, with sharp fangs and abounding in venom, its great neck wound about as the bowstring, it stood there in the shape of a man.

**13.14.124**  And the arrow, resembling the sun, of a brilliance like the fire of doom—that great and most terrible divine weapon, the mighty Pāśupata.

**13.14.125**  Without a peer, beyond all describing, striking terror into every being, huge of frame and scattering sparks, as though shedding forth fire.

**13.14.126**  One-footed, with great fangs, with a thousand heads and bellies, with a thousand arms, tongues, and eyes, as though belching forth fire.

**13.14.127**  Surpassing the weapons of Brahmā, of Nārāyaṇa, of Indra, of Agni, and of Varuṇa, O mighty-armed one, and the destroyer of every other weapon.

**13.14.128**  By which, in days of old, Mahādeva burned Tripura and reduced it to ashes in an instant, with a single arrow and as if in sport, O Govinda.

**13.14.129**  Loosed from Maheśvara's arm, it would consume the whole universe, the three worlds with all that moves and is unmoving, in half the blink of an eye—of this there is no doubt.

**13.14.130**  In this world there is none it cannot slay, not even among Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the gods. That weapon, supremely wondrous and marvellous, did I behold, my friend.

**13.14.131**  And another supreme and secret weapon, equal to it or even greater—that which is renowned throughout all the worlds as the trident of the Trident-bearer.

**13.14.132**  Hurled by the Trident-handed one, it could cleave the whole earth asunder, or dry up the great ocean, or destroy the entire universe.

**13.14.133**  By it, in olden times, was Māndhātṛ slain, the son of Yuvanāśva, together with his army—a sovereign emperor of vast splendour, the king who had conquered the three worlds.

**13.14.134**  Mighty in strength and valour, in prowess the equal of Śakra, he was slain, O Govinda, by that trident here held in the hand of the demon Lavaṇa.

**13.14.135**  That trident, exceedingly sharp of point, most dreadful and hair-raising, stood as though it had drawn its three prongs into a frown and was threatening all before it.

**13.14.136**  Smokeless yet flaming, dark, risen like the sun of doom, serpent in hand, beyond describing, like Death with his noose in hand—that weapon I beheld, O Govinda, in the presence of Rudra.

**13.14.137**  And the keen-edged axe that of old was given to Rāma by the well-pleased Mahādeva, bringer of destruction to the Kṣatriyas—by which, in a mighty battle, the emperor Kārtavīrya was slain.

**13.14.138**  By which the earth was made bereft of Kṣatriyas thrice seven times over, O Govinda, by Rāma the son of Jamadagni, of unwearied deeds.

**13.14.139**  With blazing edge and most fearsome face, wound about at the throat and tip with serpents, it stood beside the Trident-bearer like a tongue of flaming fire.

**13.14.140**  Numberless are the divine weapons of that wise one; these, the chief among them, have I recounted to you, O sinless one.

**13.14.141**  On the God's left side stood Brahmā, the Grandsire of the worlds, mounted upon a celestial car yoked with swans and swift as thought.

**13.14.142**  And likewise Nārāyaṇa stood upon his left flank, mounted upon the son of Vinatā, bearing conch, discus, and mace.

**13.14.143**  Skanda, mounted upon his peacock, stood near the Goddess, his spear held aslant his shoulder, like a second fire.

**13.14.144**  And before the God I saw Nandin stationed, standing braced upon his trident, like a second Śaṃkara.

**13.14.145**  The Manus, beginning with Svāyaṃbhuva, the sages, beginning with Bhṛgu, and the gods, beginning with Śakra—all alike drew near.

**13.14.146**  Saluting the great-souled one and encircling him on every side, the gods then praised Mahādeva with hymns of many kinds.

**13.14.147**  Brahmā, praising Bhava, intoned the Rathantara hymn; and Nārāyaṇa then sang to the Lord of gods with the Jyeṣṭha Sāman; while Śakra chanted the supreme Brahman, the excellent Śatarudrīya.

**13.14.148**  Brahmā and Nārāyaṇa and Kauśika the king of the gods—those three great-souled ones shone like three sacred fires.

**13.14.149**  In their midst the Lord God Śiva shone resplendent, like the sun freed from the autumn clouds yet still wreathed in a halo. Then I too praised that God of holy vows with this hymn.

**13.14.150**  Homage to the God of gods, homage indeed to Mahādeva; to Śakra, to him whose form is Śakra's, to him who wore the garb of Śakra.

**13.14.151**  Homage to you, thunderbolt in hand, tawny and ruddy of hue; to the Pināka-bearer evermore, to him who bears the sword and the trident.

**13.14.152**  Homage to you, clad in black, with dark curling locks, mantled in a black antelope hide, and delighting in the eighth of the dark fortnight.

**13.14.153**  To the white of hue, to the white one, to him clad in white garments, smeared with white ashes, and delighting in pure deeds.

**13.14.154**  You are Brahmā among all the gods, the blue-and-red Nīlalohita among the Rudras, the Self of all beings, and in the Sāṃkhya you are called the Puruṣa.

**13.14.155**  You are the bull among holy things, the partless and auspicious one among the Yogins; among the stages of life you are the householder, among lords you are Maheśvara, among all the Yakṣas you are Kubera, and among sacrifices you are called Viṣṇu.

**13.14.156**  Among mountains you are the great Meru, among the lunar mansions the Moon; among the sages you are Vasiṣṭha, and among the planets you are called the Sun.

**13.14.157**  Among the beasts of the forest you are the lion, O Supreme Lord; among the beasts of the village you are the bull, O Lord, worshipped by all the world.

**13.14.158**  Among the Ādityas you are Viṣṇu, among the Vasus the Fire-god, among birds the son of Vinatā, and among serpents you are Ananta.

**13.14.159**  Among the Vedas you are the Sāmaveda, among the Yajus formulas the Śatarudrīya, among the Yogins Sanatkumāra, and among the followers of Sāṃkhya you are Kapila.

**13.14.160**  Among the Maruts you are Śakra, O God; among the ancestral fathers you are the king of dharma; among the worlds you are the world of Brahmā, and among the goals you are called liberation.

**13.14.161**  Among the oceans you are the Ocean of Milk, among mountains the Himavat; among the social orders you are the Brāhmaṇa, and among the learned the consecrated twice-born. You are the beginning of the worlds, and you are likewise their destroyer, even Time itself.

**13.14.162**  And whatever other being in the worlds is held to surpass the rest in splendour—all that is the Lord himself: such is my settled conviction.

**13.14.163**  Homage to you, O Lord and God; homage to you, tender to your devotees; homage be to you, O Lord of Yoga; homage to you, O source of the universe.

**13.14.164**  Be gracious to me, your devotee, wretched and forlorn, beset by helplessness; be my refuge, O eternal one.

**13.14.165**  Whatever offense I have committed in ignorance, O supreme lord, deign to forgive it all, O lord of gods, for I am your devotee.

**13.14.166**  I was deluded, O lord of gods, by the disguise of your form, and so I offered you neither the welcome-water nor the water for your feet, O lord of the celestials.

**13.14.167**  Having thus praised Īśāna, with hands folded in reverence I offered him in devotion the water for his feet, the water of welcome, and all the rites.

**13.14.168**  Then, O dear one, a gracious shower of flowers, cool with water and fragrant with celestial scents, fell upon my head.

**13.14.169**  Then a celestial kettledrum was sounded by the servants of the gods, and a holy breeze blew, pure-scented and bringing delight.

**13.14.170**  Then Mahādeva, the bull-bannered one, well pleased and accompanied by his consort, spoke to the gods, gladdening me as it were.

**13.14.171**  Behold, all you gods, the supreme and celestial devotion of the great-souled Upamanyu toward me, established in singleness of heart.

**13.14.172**  Thus addressed by the trident-bearer, O Kṛṣṇa, all those gods, with folded hands and bowing to the bull-bannered one, replied:

**13.14.173**  O lord, O god of gods and ruler of gods, O protector of worlds, master of the universe, let this best of the twice-born obtain from you the fruit of all his desires.

**13.14.174**  Thus addressed by the gods led by Brahmā, Śarva—the lord, Śaṃkara—spoke to me as though smiling:

**13.14.175**  My child Upamanyu, I am pleased; behold me, O bull among sages. You are firm in devotion, O brahmin seer, and I have tested you.

**13.14.176**  By this devotion of yours I am exceedingly delighted; therefore I grant you this day all the desires you wish for.

**13.14.177**  When Mahādeva had thus spoken to me, O mighty one, tears flowed from joy, and my hair stood on end.

**13.14.178**  And then, touching the earth with my knees and bowing again and again, I addressed the god in a voice faltering with joy:

**13.14.179**  Today indeed am I born, O god; today my austerity has borne fruit, in that Mahādeva himself stands graciously before me.

**13.14.180**  That god of boundless might, whom even the gods cannot behold for all their worship, I have now beheld; who is more blessed than I?

**13.14.181**  Thus do the wise meditate upon him as the supreme eternal principle, known as the twenty-sixth, the imperishable, higher than the highest.

**13.14.182**  This same lord, the imperishable god, is the source of all principles, knower of the ordering of all principles, the master of Primal Nature and Spirit.

**13.14.183**  It was the lord who created from his right side Brahmā, the origin of the worlds, and from his left side Viṣṇu for the protection of the worlds; and when the age's end arrives, the master brings forth Rudra from his body.

**13.14.184**  That Rudra, of great splendor, withdrawing the whole world of things moving and unmoving, becomes Time itself, like the all-consuming fire of dissolution.

**13.14.185**  This god, Mahādeva, having created the world of things moving and unmoving, at the end of the aeon withdraws the consciousness of all and abides alone.

**13.14.186**  All-pervading, the self of all beings, the source from which all beings arise, he abides forever present everywhere, unseen even by all the gods.

**13.14.187**  If a boon is to be granted to me, and if my lord is pleased with me, then let my devotion to you, O Śaṃkara, be everlasting and eternal.

**13.14.188**  And that I may know what is past, what is to come, and what is present, O mighty one—such is my wish—by your grace, O best of the gods.

**13.14.189**  And that I may eat of inexhaustible milk-rice together with my kinsmen, and that your supreme presence may ever abide for me in my hermitage.

**13.14.190**  Thus addressed, the lord—Maheśvara, worshiped by all the worlds, of great splendor, the master and teacher of all things moving and unmoving—said to me:

**13.14.191**  Be free from age and free from death, released from sorrow, virtuous, endowed with every excellence, all-knowing, and fair to look upon.

**13.14.192**  Let your youth be unfading and your splendor like fire, and let the ocean of milk be present wherever you wish, O sage.

**13.14.193**  There the presence of the ocean of milk shall be yours at will, and you shall eat milk-rice mingled with the nectar of immortality.

**13.14.194**  Together with your kinsmen you shall live through the aeon and then come to me; and I will make my presence abide forever in your hermitage, O best of the twice-born.

**13.14.195**  Abide as you wish, my child; you need not grieve. Whenever you remember me, O brahmin, I will ever grant you my sight.

**13.14.196**  Having spoken thus, that lord Īśāna, radiant as ten million suns, granted me the boon and vanished on the spot.

**13.14.197**  Thus, O Kṛṣṇa, did I behold the god of gods through deep contemplation, and all that was promised by that wise one came to pass for me.

**13.14.198**  And behold here before your very eyes, O Kṛṣṇa, the perfected ones gathered—seers, vidyādharas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and apsarases.

**13.14.199**  Behold these enchanting trees, ever laden with flowers and fruit, bearing the blossoms of every season, with glossy leaves and fair branches—all this, O mighty-armed one, is filled with a celestial presence.

**13.15.1**  Upamanyu said: These and thousands of others Hara has favored with his thought; why then, O Mādhava, should the lord not show his grace to you?

**13.15.2**  For communion with the gods is praiseworthy through one like you—devoted to brahmins, free of cruelty, and full of faith; and I will impart to you the prayer by which you shall behold Śaṃkara.

**13.15.3**  Kṛṣṇa said: I answered him, O brahmin, great sage: By your grace I shall behold the lord of the gods, the crusher of the hosts of Diti's sons.

**13.15.4**  And on the eighth day I was duly consecrated by the brahmin—bearing a staff, with shaven head, holding kuśa grass, clad in rags, anointed with ghee, and girded with a sash.

**13.15.5**  For one month I lived on fruit, for the second on water alone, and through the third, the fourth, and the fifth I subsisted on air.

**13.15.6**  Standing on one foot, with arms upraised and never slackening, I beheld in the sky, O Bhārata, a radiance like that of a thousand suns.

**13.15.7**  And in the midst of that radiance, O son of Pāṇḍu, I saw a cloud-mass like a heap of dark mountains, its form wreathed with rainbows, its lattice-windows of lightning-garlands, adorned with cranes.

**13.15.8**  And upon it stood the lord of great brilliance, together with the goddess, his consort, blazing with austerity, splendor, and radiant beauty.

**13.15.9**  There Maheśvara, the lord, shone forth with the goddess, even as the sun joined with the moon shines when resting amid the clouds.

**13.15.10**  With my hair bristling, O son of Kuntī, and my eyes wide with wonder, I beheld Hara, the refuge of the hosts of gods, the remover of distress.

**13.15.11**  Crowned, mace-bearing, trident in hand, clothed in a tiger's skin, with matted locks and staff in hand, wielder of the Pināka bow and the thunderbolt, with sharp tusks, fair-armleted, wearing a serpent for his sacred thread—

**13.15.12**  bearing upon his breast a celestial garland of many hues, hanging down to his ankles—him I beheld like the moon ringed with a twilit halo at the passing of the rains.

**13.15.13**  He was surrounded on every side by the troops of the pramathas, hard to gaze upon, like the sun ringed with a halo in autumn.

**13.15.14**  And the eleven Rudras, self-controlled, praised him, the bull-riding one, of auspicious deeds, with their rites.

**13.15.15**  The Ādityas, the Vasus, the Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas, and the two Aśvins praised the god, the god of all, with hymns of every kind.

**13.15.16**  And the lord of a hundred sacrifices and Viṣṇu, both sons of Aditi, and Brahmā chanted the Rathantara sāman in the presence of Bhava.

**13.15.17**  Many lords of yoga praised him, the giver of yoga, the father and teacher, as did the brahmin seers with their sons and the divine seers.

**13.15.18**  The earth and the firmament, the constellations and the planets, the months and fortnights, the seasons, the nights, the years, and the moments—

**13.15.19**  the hours and the instants, and likewise the revolutions of the ages—all these, O king, made obeisance, as did the celestial sciences and all the quarters of space.

**13.15.20**  Sanatkumāra, the Vedas, and the ancient legends as well; Marīci, Aṅgiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu—

**13.15.21**  the Manus, Soma, Atharvan with Bṛhaspati, Bhṛgu, Dakṣa, Kaśyapa, Vasiṣṭha, and Kāśya as well—

**13.15.22**  the metres, the consecration, the sacrifices and their priestly fees, the fire and the oblation, and all the materials that go to a sacrifice, embodied in form, O Yudhiṣṭhira—

**13.15.23**  all the lords of creatures, the rivers, the serpents and the mountains, all the mothers of the gods, and the wives of the gods together with their maidens—

**13.15.24**  sages by the thousands, by the tens of thousands and the millions, made obeisance to the serene lord, as did the mountains, the oceans, and the quarters of space.

**13.15.25**  And the gandharvas and apsarases, skilled in song and instrument, singing in celestial measures, praised the wondrous Bhava, as did the vidyādharas, the dānavas, the guhyakas, and the rākṣasas.

**13.15.26**  And all beings, unmoving and moving, made obeisance, O great king, to the all-pervading lord with word, mind, and deed; and Śarva, the lord of the gods, stood before me.

**13.15.27**  And when the whole world, with the Lords of Creatures and Śakra, saw my Īśāna standing before me, O Bhārata, it gazed up at me.

**13.15.28**  And I had then no power to look upon Mahādeva; thereupon the god said to me: Behold, Kṛṣṇa, and speak.

**13.15.29**  When I had bowed my head to the god, the goddess Umā was well pleased; then I praised Sthāṇu, who is praised by the gods led by Brahmā:

**13.15.30**  Homage to you, O eternal one, source of all; the seers call you the sovereign of Brahmā; and the holy ones declare that austerity, and goodness, passion, and darkness, and truth itself are none but you.

**13.15.31**  You indeed are Brahmā and Rudra, Varuṇa, Agni, Manu, and Bhava; you are Dhātṛ, Tvaṣṭṛ, and Vidhātṛ; you are the lord whose faces are turned in every direction.

**13.15.32**  From you are born all beings, unmoving and moving; you are the origin of all beings, and you alone are their dissolution.

**13.15.33**  The objects of the senses and the whole of the mind, the seven winds and the fire, and the deities that dwell in heaven among men—beyond all these the seers declare you to be.

**13.15.34**  The Vedas and the sacrifices, the soma and the priestly fee, the fire and the oblation, and whatever else pertains to the sacrifice—all that, O lord, are you, beyond doubt.

**13.15.35**  Sacrifice offered, gifts bestowed, scripture studied, and the vows and observances; modesty, renown, prosperity, splendor, contentment, and attainment—all are offered up to you.

**13.15.36**  Desire, anger, fear, greed, pride, arrogance, and envy, and afflictions of mind and body—these too, O lord, are your offspring.

**13.15.37**  Creation, transformation, dissolution, Primal Nature, the imperishable source; the supreme womb of the mind and inherent nature, eternal; the unmanifest, O purifier, O all-pervading one of a thousand rays and golden hue.

**13.15.38**  You are the origin of all the qualities, the refuge of life; the Great Self, intelligence, Brahmā, the Universe, Śaṃbhu, the self-existent one.

**13.15.39**  Intellect, wisdom, perception, awareness, fame, steadfastness, and memory—by these synonymous words you, the Great Self, are conceived.

**13.15.40**  Having known you, the learned brahmin falls into no delusion; you are the heart of all beings, the Knower of the Field, praised by the seers.

**13.15.41**  With hands and feet on every side, with eyes, heads, and faces on every side, with ears on every side, you abide in the world, enveloping all.

**13.15.42**  You are the fruit of every act, from the blink of an eye onward, O fierce-rayed one; you are the radiant-flamed Spirit seated in the heart of all; you are minuteness, lightness, and attainment, the lord, the imperishable light.

**13.15.43**  In you abide intellect, thought, and the worlds; and those who take refuge and rely upon you are the meditators, the ever-yoked, the true to their word, the conquerors of the senses.

**13.15.44**  He who knows you as the changeless one, dwelling in the cave of the heart—the lord, the ancient Spirit, the all-formed, the golden one, the supreme goal of the wise—he, the wise one, transcends the intellect and abides.

**13.15.45**  Having known the seven subtle principles and you who are six-membered in your embodied form, the wise one, established in the discipline of the ordering of primal matter, enters into you alone.

**13.15.46**  When I had spoken thus, O Pārtha, to Bhava the destroyer of affliction, the whole world, moving and unmoving, raised up a lion's roar.

**13.15.47**  The hosts of brāhmaṇas, the gods and the asuras, the nāgas, the piśācas, the ancestral fathers and the birds, the throngs of rākṣasas and all the bands of spirits, and the great seers as well, then bowed down in reverence.

**13.15.48**  Upon my head heaps of fragrant celestial flowers came showering down, and a most pleasant breeze blew.

**13.15.49**  The Lord, the benefactor of the world, having looked upon the goddess Umā and upon me, and having gazed at Śatakratu, Śaṃkara himself spoke to me.

**13.15.50**  We know, O Kṛṣṇa, your supreme devotion to us, O slayer of foes; let your own welfare be secured, for our love for you is supreme.

**13.15.51**  Choose eight boons, O Kṛṣṇa; I shall grant them to you, O most excellent one. Speak, O tiger among the Yādavas, of whatever boons, however hard to obtain, you desire.

**13.16.1**  Kṛṣṇa said: Falling down with my head upon that mass of splendor, self-controlled, and then attaining the highest joy, I addressed the Lord.

**13.16.2**  Firmness in dharma, the slaying of foes in battle, foremost renown and supreme strength, devotion to yoga, nearness to you, and a hundred times a hundred sons — these I choose.

**13.16.3**  "So be it" — these words Śaṃkara spoke, having been addressed by me.

**13.16.4**  Then the mother of the world, Umā the all-purifying Earth, intent and composed — Śarvāṇī, the treasury of austerities — spoke to me.

**13.16.5**  "A son named Sāmba has been granted to you by the Lord, O sinless one; from me too receive eight cherished boons, which I give to you." And bowing my head, I addressed her, O delight of Pāṇḍu's line.

**13.16.6**  Freedom from anger toward the twice-born, my father's favor, a hundred sons and the highest enjoyment, affection within my kindred and my mother's grace, the attainment of peace, and skillfulness too — these I chose.

**13.16.7**  The goddess said: "So shall it be, O you of immortal majesty; never at any time do I speak falsely. Sixteen thousand wives shall be yours, and beloved standing among them, and likewise undecaying vigor."

**13.16.8**  "Foremost affection from your kinsmen I grant you, and the loveliness of your form; and seven hundred guests shall ever feast in your house."

**13.16.9**  Vāsudeva said: Having thus granted me boons, the god and the goddess, O Bhārata, vanished in that instant together with their attendant hosts, O elder brother of Bhīma.

**13.16.10**  All this exceedingly wondrous matter I recounted in full to the brāhmaṇa Upamanyu of surpassing splendor, O best of the Kurus.

**13.16.11**  And having made obeisance to the god of gods, he of firm vows declared: "There is none equal to Śarva in giving, none equal to Śarva in battle, no god equal to Śarva, no refuge equal to Śarva."

**13.16.12**  There was a seer in the Kṛta age, my son, renowned by the name of Taṇḍi; for ten thousand years the god was worshipped by him, devoted, with deep meditation. Hear now the outcome that came to him.

**13.16.13**  He beheld Mahādeva and praised the Lord with hymns: "You are the purifier of the pure, the goal of those who seek a goal, O most excellent one; the fiercely blazing splendor of splendors, the supreme austerity of austerities."

**13.16.14**  "O you to whom Viśvāvasu, Hiraṇyākṣa, and Puruhūta bow down, bestower of abundant blessings, O all-pervading Lord, O ancient truth — homage be to you!"

**13.16.15**  "For the ascetics striving in their endeavor, who dread birth and death, O all-pervading Lord, you are the giver of nirvāṇa, O thousand-rayed one; homage be to you, O abode of bliss!"

**13.16.16**  "Brahmā, Śatakratu, Viṣṇu, the Viśvedevas, and the great seers do not know you in your true essence; how then shall we come to know you?"

**13.16.17**  "From you time proceeds, and in you time dissolves; you alone are that which is called Time, that which is called Puruṣa, and that which is called Brahman."

**13.16.18**  "Three forms of yours are recounted by the divine seers learned in ancient lore: that pertaining to the cosmic Person, to the self, and to beings and deities; and pertaining to the worlds, to higher knowledge, and to sacrifice — you alone are all these."

**13.16.19**  "Having known you, who dwell within the body of the self, hard to know even by the gods, the wise, set free, attain the supreme, disease-free state."

**13.16.20**  "For you, O all-pervading Lord, who desire it not, there is no birth or death in any manifold way; you are the gateway to heaven and to liberation — you both withhold and bestow."

**13.16.21**  "You alone are liberation and heaven; you indeed are desire and wrath; you alone are sattva, rajas, and tamas, and the below and the above."

**13.16.22**  "Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra, Skanda and Indra, Savitṛ, Yama, Varuṇa and the Moon, Manu, Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ — you are the lord of wealth, Kubera."

**13.16.23**  "Earth, wind, light, and the waters, speech, intellect — you are thought and mind, action, and both truth and untruth; you alone are being and non-being."

**13.16.24**  "The senses and the objects of the senses, and that abiding reality beyond primal nature — you alone are the existence transcending both the manifest and the unmanifest universe, the thinkable and the unthinkable."

**13.16.25**  "That which is the supreme Brahman, that which is the supreme abode, and the goal of the followers of Sāṃkhya and Yoga — that are you, O Lord; herein there is no doubt."

**13.16.26**  "Surely this day we have achieved our purpose; surely we have attained the goal of the good — that goal which here is reached by those whose minds are made pure through knowledge."

**13.16.27**  "Alas, for a very long time we have been deluded, devoid of understanding, in that we knew not the supreme, eternal God whom the wise know."

**13.16.28**  "This very god, the bestower of grace upon his devotees, has now been reached by me in person through many births — the god whom, once known, one tastes immortality."

**13.16.29**  "That which is the eternal secret of gods, asuras, and men — the Brahman hidden in the cave of the heart, hard to be known even by the gods —"

**13.16.30**  "This very one is the blessed God, the maker of all, facing in every direction, the Self of all, the all-seeing, the all-pervading, the knower of all."

**13.16.31**  "Maker of breath, sustainer of breath, the breathing one, giver of breath, the goal of all that breathe; maker of bodies, sustainer of bodies, the embodied one, enjoyer of bodies, the goal of all the embodied."

**13.16.32**  "For those steadfast in the path of the inner self, for meditators and knowers of the Self, for those who desire no second death — the goal that is theirs, that is this Lord."

**13.16.33**  "And this one bestows upon all beings their auspicious or inauspicious destinies; and this one ordains the birth and death of all creatures."

**13.16.34**  "And this Lord is the giver of perfection to the seers who desire perfection; and this Lord is the giver of liberation to the twice-born who desire liberation."

**13.16.35**  "Having brought forth all the worlds beginning with the earth, along with the dwellers in heaven, the god sustains them with his eight bodily forms, and grants their boons."

**13.16.36**  "From him everything proceeds; in him everything is established; and in him it goes to dissolution — he is the one eternal."

**13.16.37**  "This is the supreme world of truth for the good who desire truth; he is the final release of the liberated and the absolute solitude of those who proclaim the Self."

**13.16.38**  "This Lord is kept hidden in the cave of the heart by the perfected beings beginning with Brahmā, so that he might not be manifest to gods, asuras, and men."

**13.16.39**  "You, that Bhava, the gods, asuras, and men do not truly know, deluded indeed and led astray by this very one who dwells within the heart."

**13.16.40**  "But to those who take refuge in him through the discipline of devotion, O Bhārata, this dweller in the heart reveals the Self to them by the Self."

**13.16.41**  "Whom having known, there is no birth nor death again; whom having understood as the supreme object of knowledge, nothing further remains to be known."

**13.16.42**  "Whom having gained as the supreme gain, one deems nothing greater thereafter; one comes to that highest attainment, subtle as the breath of life, which brings the undecaying."

**13.16.43**  "Whom the followers of Sāṃkhya, knowers of the truth of the guṇas, versed in the Sāṃkhya teaching, delighting in subtle knowledge, having first known, are freed from their bonds."

**13.16.44**  "Whom the knowers of the Veda know as the object of knowledge, established in the Vedānta, and whom those ever intent on breath-control enter into and ceaselessly recite."

**13.16.45**  "He, as the Sun, is called the gateway of those who travel the path of the gods; and he, as the Moon, is called the gateway of those who travel the path of the fathers."

**13.16.46**  "He is the varied course of time in years, ages, and the rest, and presence and absence in the present moment, and the southern and northern courses of the sun."

**13.16.47**  "Thus did Prajāpati of old, having worshipped him with many hymns, choose for his son the one named the Blue-and-Red."

**13.16.48**  "Whom the reciters of many ṛc-verses extol with the Ṛg verses in the ritual act, and whom, threefold to be known, the adhvaryu priests offer oblation to with the Yajus formulas in the sacrifice."

**13.16.49**  "And whom the singers of the Sāman, pure of mind, hymn with the Sāman chants — he is remembered as the supreme womb of sacrifice and its supreme lord."

**13.16.50**  "Night and day are his ears and eyes, the fortnights and months his head and arms; the seasons are his potency, austerity his firmness, the year his hidden secret, with thighs and feet of vast measure."

**13.16.51**  "Death, Yama, and the fire-god, Time impetuous in destruction — he is the supreme source of time, and he is this eternal Time itself."

**13.16.52**  "The moon and the sun with the constellations, with the planets and the wind, the Pole Star and the seven seers, and the seven worlds as well —"

**13.16.53**  "Primal matter, the great principle, the unmanifest, ending in the particularized, together with its modifications, all from Brahmā down to a clump of grass, the elements and whatever is being and non-being —"

**13.16.54**  "The eight constituent natures, and that which is beyond the natures — the whole of this revolves as a portion of this god."

**13.16.55**  "This is the supreme bliss, which is also the eternal; this is the goal of the dispassionate, this the highest state of the good."

**13.16.56**  "This is the abode free from agitation, this the eternal Brahman; for those learned in the scriptures, the Vedas, and the Vedāṅgas, this is the supreme object of meditation and the highest abode."

**13.16.57**  "This is that supreme limit, this that supreme part; this is that supreme perfection, this that supreme goal."

**13.16.58**  "This is that supreme peace, this the highest beatitude, attaining which the creators thought, 'We have accomplished all that is to be done.'"

**13.16.59**  "This is contentment, this is perfection, this is revelation, this is tradition; for the wise who are steadfast in the path of the inner self, this is the undecaying attainment."

**13.16.60**  "For those who sacrifice, desiring sacrifice, with rites of abundant priestly fees, the divine goal won together with the gods — that goal are you, O eternal one."

**13.16.61**  "For those who practice austerity through recitation, oblation, vows, penances, restraints, and the mortifying of the body, O god — the goal that lies in the Vairāja world, that goal are you."

**13.16.62**  "For those who have renounced action and the dispassionate, here and there — the goal that lies in the abode of Brahmā, that goal are you, O eternal one."

**13.16.63**  "For those who desire no second death, who abide in the highest dispassion, and for the modifications dissolved back into their source — that goal are you, O eternal one."

**13.16.64**  "For those steadfast in knowledge and discernment, the goal that is indescribable, stainless, the absolute solitude, the supreme — that goal, O god, are you."

**13.16.65**  "These five goals, declared in the Vedas, the śāstras, and the Purāṇas, are recounted; they are won only by your grace, and otherwise are not won, O all-pervading Lord."

**13.16.66**  Thus Taṇḍi, through the power of his austerity, praised the imperishable Lord, and sang the supreme Brahman which the maker of the world had sung of old.

**13.16.67**  "Brahmā, Śatakratu, Viṣṇu, the Viśvedevas, and the great seers know you not" — and at this Śiva, well pleased, then spoke to him.

**13.16.68**  "He shall be undecaying and imperishable, free of sorrow, renowned, endowed with splendor, and possessed of divine knowledge."

**13.16.69**  "Approachable by the seers and a composer of aphorisms, your son shall be, by my grace, O best of the twice-born; of this there is no doubt."

**13.16.70**  "What desire, then, shall I grant you this day? Speak, my child, of what you wish." With folded hands he said this: "Let my devotion to you be firm."

**13.16.71**  Having thus granted the boon, the god, revered by the divine seers and praised by the wise, vanished then and there.

**13.16.72**  When the Lord with his attendants had vanished, O lord of the Yādavas, the seer, having returned to his hermitage, recounted all this to me here.

**13.16.73**  And those names, renowned from the first, which Taṇḍi declared to me, O best of men, hear them now for your perfection.

**13.16.74**  In the Vedas the Grandsire proclaimed ten thousand names of Śarva, and in the scriptures, likewise, a thousand names.

**13.16.75**  These secret names of the Blessed One, O Acyuta, O lord of the gods, the sage Taṇḍi declared of old, by the grace of the deity, to that great-souled one.

**13.17.1**  Vāsudeva said: Then, my dear Yudhiṣṭhira, that brahmin-sage, having purified himself, with palms joined in reverence, recited to me the litany of names from the beginning.

**13.17.2**  Upamanyu said: With names declared by Brahmā, declared by the seers, born of the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences, renowned throughout all the worlds, I shall praise Sthāṇu.

**13.17.3**  With names ordained by the great ones, true, perfected, accomplishing every aim, fashioned in devotion by the sage Taṇḍi, whose self was made one with the god.

**13.17.4**  With names handed down as spoken, famed throughout the world, given by sages who see the truth — supreme, primordial, leading to heaven, the welfare of all beings, auspicious, heard everywhere in the universe, brought down from the world of Brahmā.

**13.17.5**  That supreme mystery, eternal, declared by Brahmā, I shall now speak, O best of the Yadu line; listen to me with full attention.

**13.17.6**  As one devoted, you hold the god Bhava to be the Supreme, the highest Lord; therefore I shall cause you to hear that eternal Absolute.

**13.17.7**  No one is able to tell in full detail the glories of Śarva — not even one wholly absorbed in yoga, not even in a hundred years.

**13.17.8**  He whose beginning, middle, and end not even the gods can reach — who, O Mādhava, could tell his attributes in their entirety?

**13.17.9**  Yet of the mighty god, in words and syllables compressed in meaning, I shall recount his deeds as best I can, and by his grace alone.

**13.17.10**  Without first obtaining his sanction, the Lord cannot here be praised; only when granted leave by him may one ever praise Bhava.

**13.17.11**  Of him without beginning or end, the source of all, the great-souled one whose origin is unmanifest, I shall set forth some portion of his names.

**13.17.12**  Of the giver of boons, the most excellent, the cosmic-formed, the wise one — hear the enumeration of names that was spoken by the Lotus-born.

**13.17.13**  The ten thousand names that the great Grandsire declared — churning these in his mind, he drew them forth as clarified butter is drawn from curds.

**13.17.14**  As gold is the essence of the mountain, as honey is the essence of the flower, as cream is the essence of clarified butter, so this essence was drawn forth.

**13.17.15**  This litany, which removes all sin and is joined with the four Vedas, is to be mastered with effort and held fast by one of disciplined soul — bringing peace, fostering prosperity, slaying demons, purifying, and great.

**13.17.16**  This is to be given to one who is devoted, faithful, and a believer — never to one without faith, to an unbeliever, or to one whose self is unconquered.

**13.17.17**  And whoever reviles the god, the Self of all beings, the wielder of the Pināka bow — he, O Kṛṣṇa, goes to hell together with his forebears and his followers.

**13.17.18**  This is meditation, this is yoga, this is the unsurpassed object of contemplation; this is the prayer to be murmured, this is knowledge, this the supreme mystery; knowing this, even at the hour of death one attains the highest goal.

**13.17.19**  Pure, auspicious, meritorious, blessed, and supreme — this I shall now recite, O mighty-armed one: the highest of all hymns of praise.

**13.17.20**  Brahmā, the Grandsire of all the worlds, having composed this of old, appointed it to sovereignty over all the celestial hymns.

**13.17.21**  From that time onward this hymn of the great-souled Lord has been renowned in the world as the King of Hymns, honored by the immortals; and this King of Hymns was brought down from the world of Brahmā.

**13.17.22**  Because Taṇḍi proclaimed it of old, it came to be called the work of Taṇḍi; and from heaven to this earthly world it was indeed brought down by Taṇḍi.

**13.17.23**  Auspicious among all auspicious things, destroying every sin — this I shall recite, O mighty-armed one: the highest of all hymns.

**13.17.24**  He who is the Absolute even of the absolutes, the supreme even of the supreme, the radiance even of radiances, the austerity even of austerities;

**13.17.25**  The peace even of those at peace, the brilliance even of the brilliant, the self-controlled even among the self-controlled, the wisdom even of the wise;

**13.17.26**  The god even of the gods, the sage even of the sages, the sacrifice even of sacrifices, the auspicious even of auspicious things;

**13.17.27**  The Rudra even of the Rudras, the lord even of the mighty, the yogin even of yogins, and the cause of all causes;

**13.17.28**  From whom the worlds arise and into whom they cease to be — of Hara, who has become the Self of all beings, of measureless splendor.

**13.17.29**  Now hear from me the thousand-and-eight names of Śarva, on hearing which, O best of men, you shall obtain all your desires.

**13.17.30**  The Steadfast, the Pillar, the Lord, the Radiant, the Most Excellent, the Boon-giver, the Best; the Self of all, the All-renowned, the All, the Maker of all, Bhava the Existent.

**13.17.31**  The Matted-haired, the Hide-clad, the Crested; the All-bodied, the Source of all becoming; Hari, the Doe-eyed, the Lord who withdraws all beings.

**13.17.32**  Engagement and Disengagement; the Constant, the Eternal, the Fixed; the Haunter of cremation grounds, the Blessed One, the Sky-rover, the Earth-rover, the Tormentor.

**13.17.33**  The One to be saluted, of mighty deeds, the Ascetic, the Nourisher of beings; Hidden in the guise of a madman, the Lord of all creatures in every world.

**13.17.34**  Of great form, of mighty frame, of every form, of great renown; the Great-souled, the All-pervading, the Misshapen, the Dwarf, the Man.

**13.17.35**  The Guardian of the world, the Hidden-souled, Serene Grace, He of horse and ass; the Pure, the Mighty, Discipline itself, and the Refuge of discipline.

**13.17.36**  The Doer of all deeds, the Self-existent, the Beginning, the First Maker, the Treasure-store; the Thousand-eyed, the Strange-eyed, Soma, the Marshaller of the stars.

**13.17.37**  The Path of moon and sun, the Comet, the Seizing Planet, the Lord of planets, the Excellent; the Mountain, the Mountain-dweller, the Maker, He who loosed the arrow at the deer-form, the Sinless.

**13.17.38**  Of great austerity, of terrible austerity, the Undejected, the Helper of the wretched; the Maker of the year, the Sacred Formula, the Measure, the Supreme Austerity.

**13.17.39**  The Yogin, the One to be united with, the Great Seed, the Great-seeded, of great austerity; He of golden seed, the All-knowing, of goodly seed, the Bull-borne.

**13.17.40**  The Ten-armed, the Unblinking, the Blue-throated, the Husband of Umā; the Cosmic-formed, the Self-supreme, the Mighty Hero, the Strong, the Host.

**13.17.41**  The Maker of hosts, the Lord of hosts, the Sky-clad, and the Desirable; the Pure, the Supreme, the Sacred Formula, Hara who brings every state of being to pass.

**13.17.42**  Bearer of the water-pot, the Bowman, the Arrow-handed, He who holds a skull; armed with the thunderbolt, the śataghnī, the sword, and the spear — the Weaponed, the Great.

**13.17.43**  The Ladle-handed, the Fair-formed, Radiance, the Maker of radiance, the Treasure-store; the Turbaned, the Fair-faced, the Lofty, and likewise the Bowed.

**13.17.44**  The Tall, the Tawny-haired, the Goodly Ford, and the Dark One; the Jackal-formed, the All-purposed, the Shaven-headed, the Ringed, He of the water-pot.

**13.17.45**  The Unborn, the Deer-formed, the Bearer of fragrance, He of the matted braid; of upward-flowing seed, with phallus raised, lying on high, the very vault of heaven.

**13.17.46**  The Triple-braided, the Rag-clad, Rudra, the Army-commander, the All-pervading; the Day-rover and the Night-rover, of fierce wrath, of brilliant splendor.

**13.17.47**  Slayer of the elephant, slayer of demons, the World itself, the Upholder of the world, the Mine of virtues; of the form of lion and tiger, wrapped in a garment of fresh hide.

**13.17.48**  The Yogin of Time, the Great Roar, the Dwelling-place of all, the Crossroads; the Night-rover, the Wanderer among ghosts, the Wanderer among spirits, the Great Lord.

**13.17.49**  Of many forms, of many treasures, the Support of all, of boundless course; Lover of the dance, ever-dancing, the Dancer, the Sporter of all.

**13.17.50**  The Terrible, of great austerity, the Noose, the Eternal, the Mountain-rover, the Sky; the Thousand-handed, the Victorious, Resolve itself, the Blameless.

**13.17.51**  The Unforbearing, the Forbearing-souled, the Destroyer of the sacrifice, the Slayer of desire; the Despoiler of Dakṣa's sacrifice, the All-enduring, and the Mean between extremes.

**13.17.52**  Robber of radiance, slayer of might, the Joyful, the Aim, the Conquered, the Best; of deep voice, the Profound, He whose strength and mount are profound.

**13.17.53**  Of the banyan's form, the Banyan, abiding in the tree's hollow, the All-pervading; of sharp heat, the Tawny-horsed, the Companion, the Knower of the time of action.

**13.17.54**  Propitiated by Viṣṇu, the Sacrifice, the Ocean, the Mare's-mouth fire; the Ally of the fire that eats oblations, the Tranquil-souled, the Oblation-eater himself.

**13.17.55**  Of fierce radiance, of great radiance, the Victory, the Knower of the hour of triumph; the Pathway of the lights, Attainment, Union, and also Strife.

**13.17.56**  The Crested, the Staff-bearer, the Matted-haired, the Flaming; Born of form, Crowning the head, the Strong; the Flute-player, the Drummer, the Cymbalist, Time itself, the Kālakaṭaṃkaṭa.

**13.17.57**  The Ordainer of the array of stars, the Increase of qualities, Dissolution, the Inaccessible; the Lord of creatures, He whose arms are the quarters, the Apportioning, the Face-turned-everywhere.

**13.17.58**  The Liberator, the Host of the gods, Sprung from golden armor; Born of the loins, the Wanderer in strength, the Great Wanderer, and likewise the Praised.

**13.17.59**  Sounding all the trumpets, the Possessor of every instrument; of serpent form, dwelling in caverns, the Gold-garlanded, the Knower of the waves.

**13.17.60**  The Thrice-ten gods, the Holder of the three times, the Looser of every bond of action; yet the Binding of the chiefs of the asuras, the Destroyer of foes in battle.

**13.17.61**  The Grace of Sāṃkhya, the Ill-clad, the Served by all the good; the Onrushing, the Apportioning, the Incomparable, the Knower of the sacrificial share.

**13.17.62**  The Dwelling of all, the Wanderer everywhere, the Ill-clad, the Wealth-giver, the Immortal; the Golden, the Maker of gold, the Sacrifice, the Upholder of all, the Supreme Sustainer.

**13.17.63**  The Red-eyed, the Great-eyed, the Eye of victory, the Skilled; the Gathering-up, the Restraint, the Maker, Clothed in the slough of serpents.

**13.17.64**  The Foremost and the Not-foremost, the Body and the Body's increase, the Granter of every desire; Gracious at all times, of goodly strength, bearing the form of strength.

**13.17.65**  Of the form of the treasure-store that is space, the Down-striker, the Serpent, the Sky-goer; of fierce form, the Ray, the Sun, He whose beams are wealth, of brilliant splendor.

**13.17.66**  Swift as wealth, of mighty speed, swift as thought, the Night-rover; Dwelling in all, dwelling with Fortune, Hara the giver of instruction.

**13.17.67**  The Sage, the Lord of his own self in the world, the One to be feasted, the Thousandfold giver; the Bird and the Bird-formed, the Surpassingly radiant, the Lord of peoples.

**13.17.68**  Frenzy, of the form of passion, the Maker of wealth from wealth, the Hairy one; Vāmadeva and the Lovely, He who faces east and south, the Dwarf.

**13.17.69**  The Withdrawer of perfected yoga, the Perfected, the Accomplisher of every aim; the Mendicant and the Mendicant-formed, the Horned, the Gentle, the Imperishable.

**13.17.70**  The Great-armied, and Viśākha, He of the sixtyfold portion, the Lord of cattle; the Thunderbolt-handed, the Prop, and the Stayer of armies.

**13.17.71**  The Season, the Maker of seasons, Time, the Sweet, the Maker of sweetness, the Unmoving; Sprung from the lord of trees, He of the array of strength, ever honored in the hermitages.

**13.17.72**  The Chaste student, the World-rover, the Wanderer everywhere, the Knower of good conduct; the Ruler, the Lord, Time, the Night-wanderer, the Bearer of the Pināka bow.

**13.17.73**  Nandīśvara and Nandin, the Gladdening, the Increaser of joy; the Slayer of Bhaga's eye, Time, the best of those who know the Absolute.

**13.17.74**  The Four-faced, of mighty emblem, and likewise of fair emblem; the Overseer of the emblem, the Overseer of the gods, the Overseer of the worlds, the Bearer of the yoke of the ages.

**13.17.75**  The Overseer of the seed, the Maker of the seed, He who attends upon the inmost Self, the Strong; the Maker of legend, the Aeon, Gautama, and the Lord of waters.

**13.17.76**  Pride and the Prideless, the Conqueror of pride, the Subdued, the Subduer, the Seer; the Maker of the world, the Lord of beasts, the Great Maker, the Mighty Herb.

**13.17.77**  The Imperishable, the Supreme Absolute, the Mighty, and Śakra himself; Right conduct and Misconduct, the Pure-souled, the Pure, the Honored, the Course of the mind.

**13.17.78**  Abundant in grace, the Dreamer, the Mirror, and the Vanquisher of foes; the Maker of the Vedas, the Maker of the aphorisms, the Learned, the Crusher in battle.

**13.17.79**  He who dwells in the great cloud, the awesome one, the subduer; flame of fire, mighty blaze, the deeply smoke-hued, the oblation offered and the offering itself.

**13.17.80**  The virile one, Śaṃkara the bestower of peace, the eternal, the radiant, he whose banner is smoke; the dark-blue one, eager in his limbs, the resplendent, the unrestrained.

**13.17.81**  Giver of blessing and the very state of blessing; the partaker, the apportioner, the swift; the embrace, the great-limbed, of mighty womb, supreme, ever young.

**13.17.82**  Of dark hue and of golden hue, he who is the senses of all embodied beings; great of foot, great of hand, of mighty frame, of vast renown.

**13.17.83**  Great of head, of great measure, great of eye, whose dwelling is the quarters of space; great of tooth, great of ear, mightily endowed, great of jaw.

**13.17.84**  Great of nose, great-throated as a conch, great of neck, haunter of the cremation-ground; broad of chest, mighty-breasted, the inmost Self, whose abode is among the deer.

**13.17.85**  The pendant one, with hanging lip, master of great illusion, the ocean of waters; great of tooth, great of fang, great of tongue, great of mouth.

**13.17.86**  Great of nail, great of hair, of great locks, with mighty matted braids; without a rival, the gracious one, the ground of all conviction, accomplished upon the mountain.

**13.17.87**  He who shows tenderness and he who is without attachment, the unconquered, the great sage; in form like a tree, whose emblem is the tree, the fire, borne upon the wind.

**13.17.88**  The ringed one, whose seat is Meru, breaker of the pride of gods and Dānavas; he whose head is the Atharva, whose face is the Sāman, whose unbounded gaze is the thousand verses of the Ṛk.

**13.17.89**  He whose feet and arms are the Yajus, the hidden one, the manifest, and likewise the moving; of unfailing purpose, the gracious, the approachable, fair to behold.

**13.17.90**  Lover of offerings, Śarva, the golden, the gold-bright, the steadfast; the navel, maker of joy, he who is to be meditated upon, lord enthroned upon the lotus, the unmoving.

**13.17.91**  The twelvefold, the terrifier, the primal; the sacrifice and he who is composed within the sacrifice; the night, the age of strife, and Time itself, the sea-monster, worshipped through all time.

**13.17.92**  He who is with his hosts and maker of hosts, the charioteer who fosters all beings; couched upon ashes, guardian of ashes, become as ash, the tree, the troop.

**13.17.93**  He without host, and the dissolution, the great-souled, worshipped by all; the stake, the triple-staked, the perfected, the pure, attended by the spirits.

**13.17.94**  Abiding in the hermitage, seated as a dove, maker of the universe, the choicest lord; the Branch and Viśākha, copper-lipped, a net of lotuses, the firmly resolved.

**13.17.95**  The tawny and the non-tawny, the hero, and life itself, the higher and the lower; the Gandharva, indeed Aditi, Tārkṣya, the easily known, the skilled charioteer.

**13.17.96**  He whose weapon is the battle-axe, the god, doer of all purpose, the good kinsman; bearer of the gourd-lute, of mighty wrath, of upward-drawn seed, who couches upon the waters.

**13.17.97**  The fierce, the maker of lineage, the lineage, the sound of the flute, the blameless; whose form is in every limb, the wielder of illusion, the true friend, the wind and the fire.

**13.17.98**  The binder and maker of bonds, and the loosener of the close-drawn fetter; he is the foe of the sacrifice, he the foe of desire, great of fang, mighty in arms.
