**13.17.99**  The arm indeed, the blameless, Śarva, Śaṃkara, the bestower of peace who is without possession; lord of the immortals, the Great God, the All-god, slayer of the foes of the gods.

**13.17.100**  Ahirbudhnya and Nirṛti, Cekitāna, and likewise Hari; Ajaikapād and the bearer of the skull, the triple-staked, the unconquered, the auspicious one, Śiva.

**13.17.101**  Dhanvantari, he whose banner is smoke, Skanda, and likewise Vaiśravaṇa; Dhātṛ and Śakra and Viṣṇu, Mitra, Tvaṣṭṛ, Dhruva, the upholder.

**13.17.102**  The source of power, the all-pervading, the wind, Aryaman, Savitṛ, the sun; the lofty, and Vidhātṛ, Māndhātṛ, the fosterer of beings.

**13.17.103**  The sacred ford of delight and the eloquent, bearer of every desire and quality; lotus-wombed, of mighty womb, moon-faced, the ravisher of the mind.

**13.17.104**  The mighty and the wholly tranquil, the ancient, skilled in what is meritorious; doer of deeds, whose form is Time, become the Kurus, the Great Lord, Maheśvara.

**13.17.105**  The refuge of all, who couches upon darbha grass, lord of all that breathes; foremost among god of gods, the unattached, the existent and the non-existent, knower of every jewel.

**13.17.106**  Dweller on the peak of Kailāsa, who has his refuge on the Himavat mountain; sweeper-away of banks and maker of banks, of manifold lore, giver of much.

**13.17.107**  The merchant, the increaser, the tree, the mongoose, the sandal, the leaf-shelter; firm of neck, of mighty collarbone, the unwavering, and the great healing herb.

**13.17.108**  Accomplisher of true ends and the one whose end is accomplished, supreme in metre and grammar; the lion's roar, lion-fanged, lion-gaited, lion-borne.

**13.17.109**  His own self the source of power, the Time of the world, the rhythm, the good of the worlds, the tree; the dappled one, whose body is the nine wheels, garlanded with banners, the well-disposed.

**13.17.110**  The dwelling of beings, lord of beings, blameless as day and night; the bearer of all beings, their resting-place, the all-pervading, the existent, Bhava.

**13.17.111**  The unerring, the restrained, indeed the horse, the sustenance, the upholder of life-breath; steadfast, wise, skilful, honoured, lord of the aeons.

**13.17.112**  The herder, lord of cattle, the village, clad in a hide of leather, Hara; golden-armed, and likewise the guardian of the cave for those who enter.

**13.17.113**  The well-established, of great joy, conqueror of desire, conqueror of the senses; Gāndhāra and Surāla, who delights in the works of austerity, the bow.

**13.17.114**  Of great song, of mighty dance, attended by the hosts of Apsarases; the great-bannered, the bow, the upholder, follower of many ridges, the ever-moving.

**13.17.115**  He to whom all is to be made known, the indwelling presence, bearer of every fragrance and joy; the gateway, the deliverer, the wind, who courses about from one place alone.

**13.17.116**  The union, the increaser, the aged, the mightily aged, lord of the hosts; the eternal, his own self his only helper, lord of gods and Asuras, the master.

**13.17.117**  The yoked and the strong-armed, the twofold and the well-jointed; Āṣāḍha and Suṣāḍha, the fixed one, slayer of Hari's foes, Hara.

**13.17.118**  The body for those caught in the turning round of birth, best of the Vasus, the great path; bearer of heads, the deliberating one, adorned with every auspicious mark.

**13.17.119**  The axle and he yoked to the chariot, the master of all yoga, of mighty strength; the sacred tradition and what lies beyond tradition, god of the holy fords, the great charioteer.

**13.17.120**  The lifeless and the life-giving, the sacred word, fair of eye, of many a rough place; rich in jewels, red of limb, who knows the drinking-down of the great ocean.

**13.17.121**  The root, the vast, indeed the immortal, the manifest and unmanifest, the treasury of austerity; the ascent and the descent, sweeper-away of mountains, of mighty penance.

**13.17.122**  Marshalled like an army, the great cosmic age, maker of age upon age, Hari; whose form is the aeon, of mighty form, the purifier, the unfathomable, the mountain.

**13.17.123**  He who quenches all by right reasoning, the foot, the learned, indeed like the unmoving mountain; many-garlanded, of great garland, of fair garland, of many eyes.

**13.17.124**  The expanse, the salt, the well, the blossom, whose rising bears fruit; the bull, whose limb is marked with the bull, the bearer of jewel and bilva, wearer of matted locks.

**13.17.125**  The moon, the emanation, fair of face, the god, armed with every weapon, the forbearing; the surrender, born of nectar, of sweet fragrance, the great bow.

**13.17.126**  Garlanded with fragrance, the Blessed One, the rousing of all works; the churner, the abundant, the arm, the whole, the all-seeing.

**13.17.127**  He who beats time swiftly, who beats time with his hand, of upward-knit frame, the bearing one; the parasol, the well-sheltering, the renowned, the refuge of all worlds, the great.

**13.17.128**  The shaven-headed, the formless, the misshapen, the staff-bearing and bald, the transforming one; tawny-eyed, the eminence, the wielder of the thunderbolt, of blazing tongue, thousand-footed.

**13.17.129**  Thousand-headed, lord of the gods, made of all gods, the teacher; thousand-armed, present in every limb, the refuge-giving, maker of all worlds.

**13.17.130**  The pure, the threefold sweetness, the sacred word, the youngest, the dark and tawny; fashioner of the staff of Brahman, the hundred-slayer, holder of a hundred nooses.

**13.17.131**  Lotus-wombed, of mighty womb, womb of the Brahman, sprung from the waters; the ray of light, maker of the sacred word, Brahmā, knower of the Brahman, the Brāhmaṇa, the goal.

**13.17.132**  Of endless forms, not of a single self, of keen splendour, the self-existent; whose self moves ever upward, lord of cattle, swift as the wind, fleet as thought.

**13.17.133**  Sandal-anointed, foremost in his garland of lotuses, who delivers across by fragrance, the Man; great-wreathed with karṇikāra blossoms, blue-crested, bearer of the Pināka bow.

**13.17.134**  Lord of Umā, beloved of Umā, who upholds the Jāhnavī, consort of Umā; the boon, the boar, the giver of boons, lord of boons, of mighty resounding voice.

**13.17.135**  Of great grace, the subduer, slayer of foes, white and tawny; glad of soul, of disciplined soul, of restrained soul, upholder of primal nature.

**13.17.136**  Born at every side, Tārkṣya, the common ground of dharma, the choicest; the self of all that moves and is still, of subtle soul, the good bull, lord of the cattle-bull.

**13.17.137**  Seer of the Sādhyas, the Vasu, the Āditya, Vivasvān, Savitṛ, the gracious; Vyāsa, the gathering-together of all, the expanse, the turning round, the guiding course.

**13.17.138**  The season, the year, the month, the fortnight, the completion of reckoning; the moment-fraction, the instant, the particle, the measure, the muhūrta, the day, the nights, the breaths of time.

**13.17.139**  The field of the universe, the seed of all creatures, the sign, the primal, indeed the blameless; the existent and the non-existent, the manifest and the unmanifest, father, mother, grandsire.

**13.17.140**  The gate of heaven, the gate of creatures, the gate of release, the triple heaven; extinction and gladdening too, the world of Brahman, the supreme goal.

**13.17.141**  Fashioner of gods and Asuras, the refuge of gods and Asuras; teacher of gods and Asuras, the god, saluted by gods and Asuras.

**13.17.142**  The chief minister of gods and Asuras, the resort of the hosts of gods and Asuras; overseer of the hosts of gods and Asuras, foremost leader of the hosts of gods and Asuras.

**13.17.143**  The god beyond the gods, the divine seer, giver of boons to gods and Asuras; lord of gods and Asuras, the god, the Great Lord of gods and Asuras.

**13.17.144**  Made of all gods, the inconceivable, whose self is the deities, self-arisen; the sprouting forth, the thrice-striding, the healer, the stainless, clad in stainless raiment.

**13.17.145**  The praiseworthy, the elephant, the tiger among gods, the lion among gods, the bull among men; foremost and choicest of the wise, the best, the highest of the high among all gods.

**13.17.146**  The well-applied, the resplendent, the thunderbolt, Īśāna the ruler, the lord, the imperishable; the teacher, the beloved, the innate, the creation, the pure, who bears all upon him.

**13.17.147**  The horned, lover of the peak, the tawny, king of kings, the unailing; the delightful, the host of gods, the ceasing, the means of all attainment.

**13.17.148**  Eyed upon the brow, his body the universe, the fawn-hued, possessed of the lustre of the Brahman; and lord too of all things unmoving, increaser of restraint and the senses.

**13.17.149**  He whose aim is accomplished, the welfare of all beings, the inconceivable, true to his vow, the pure; lord of vows, the supreme Brahman, the highest goal of the liberated.

**13.17.150**  The wholly released, of unfettered splendour, the glorious, the increaser of glory, the world itself: thus, as each was foremost, has the Blessed One been hymned by me in devotion.

**13.17.151**  Him whom the gods, with Brahmā at their head, do not know, whom the great seers do not know, that one worthy to be praised, worshipped, and revered, the Lord of the world — who shall hymn him?

**13.17.152**  Setting devotion alone before me, having first obtained his leave, I have hymned the lord of sacrifice, the Vasu, the best of the wise.

**13.17.153**  He who praises Śiva the god with these names that increase well-being, ever steadfast and grown pure, attains the Self by the self.

**13.17.154**  For this is the supreme Brahman, sung by the Self-existent himself; and with it the seers and the gods praise that which is beyond.

**13.17.155**  The Great God, when praised, is gladdened by the names of his own self; the Blessed One, compassionate to his devotees, establishes them within himself.

**13.17.156**  And likewise among men, those who are foremost among men, the faithful and the believing, through many births and many hymns of praise,

**13.17.157**  waking and sleeping, walking or halted upon the road, they praise him and are themselves extolled, and they are content and rejoice, through thousands of millions of births in the manifold wombs of transmigration.

**13.17.158**  In the creature whose sin is wholly cleansed there is born devotion to Bhava; and once arisen, devotion to Bhava becomes undivided, with the whole of one's being.

**13.17.159**  The cause of such devotion has been ordained for him who is wholly liberated in every way; this is hard to attain even among the gods, and is not to be had among men.

**13.17.160**  Unobstructed, unwavering, and unswerving is devotion to Rudra; and it is by his grace alone that such devotion arises in men, by which those whose minds are fixed upon his being attain the supreme perfection.

**13.17.161**  Those men who have come to him with their whole being, taking him as the Supreme, the god who cherishes those who take refuge in him would lift up out of the round of existence.

**13.17.162**  Thus the other gods do not accomplish the release of men from the cycle of birth, not even by the power of austerity, as does Mahādeva.

**13.17.163**  Thus, O Kṛṣṇa, was the Blessed One, lord of the existent and the nonexistent, clad in his hide, praised by Taṇḍi—one like unto Indra and of purified understanding.

**13.17.164**  This hymn to the Blessed One Brahmā himself bore in memory; Brahmā declared it to Śakra, and Śakra declared it to Death.

**13.17.165**  Death declared it to the Rudras, and from the Rudras it came to Taṇḍi; by mighty austerity it was won by Taṇḍi in the abode of Brahmā.

**13.17.166**  Taṇḍi declared it to Śukra; the descendant of Bhṛgu spoke it to Gautama; and Gautama spoke it, O Mādhava, to Manu the son of Vivasvat.

**13.17.167**  Manu spoke it to Nārāyaṇa the Sādhya, his beloved and wise one; and the blessed Sādhya, the imperishable Nārāyaṇa, spoke it to Yama.

**13.17.168**  The blessed Yama, son of Vivasvat, spoke it to Nāciketas; and Nāciketas, O scion of the Vṛṣṇis, spoke it to Mārkaṇḍeya.

**13.17.169**  From Mārkaṇḍeya I received it through self-discipline, O Janārdana; and to you too, O slayer of foes, I now give this renowned hymn—conferring heaven, health, long life, prosperity, and strength as well.

**13.17.170**  No hindrance do the Dānavas work upon him, nor the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, the Piśācas and the demons that devour, the Guhyakas, nor even the serpents.

**13.17.171**  He who, having become pure, chaste, and master of his senses, recites it for a year with unbroken discipline obtains the fruit of the horse sacrifice.

**13.18.1**  Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the great yogin, the sage Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, spoke: "Recite it, my son—blessings upon you; may Maheśvara be pleased with you.

**13.18.2**  Of old, my son, while I performed the highest austerity upon Meru for the sake of offspring, O great king, this hymn was recited by me.

**13.18.3**  I obtained those desires of mine, O delight of Pāṇḍu's line; and you too shall obtain all your desires from Śarva."

**13.18.4**  Then the Four-headed one spoke, the beloved friend of Śakra, renowned by the name Ālambāyana, whose nature was compassion:

**13.18.5**  "Having reached Gokarṇa and performed austerity there for a hundred years, I won—of sons not born of any womb, self-controlled, knowers of dharma, and radiant,

**13.18.6**  of the ageless, the sorrowless, who live a hundred thousand years—a hundred sons from Śarva of old, O son of King Pāṇḍu."

**13.18.7**  The blessed Vālmīki too addressed Yudhiṣṭhira: "In a dispute over a Sāman chant I was told by the sages, 'You are a slayer of a brāhmaṇa,' and in an instant, O Bhārata, I was possessed by that unrighteousness.

**13.18.8**  Then I, taking refuge, praised the sinless Lord Īśāna, and helpless though I was, I was freed from that sin; and he, the destroyer of suffering, the slayer of Tripura, said to me, 'Your glory shall be foremost.'"

**13.18.9**  And the son of Jamadagni, foremost of the upholders of dharma, addressed the son of Kuntī, standing amid the seers like blazing fire, dear child:

**13.18.10**  "Tormented by the slaying of my father and of brāhmaṇas, O eldest of the Pāṇḍavas, having made myself pure, I went for refuge to Mahādeva, O king.

**13.18.11**  With his names I praised the god, and thereupon Bhava was pleased; and the god gave me the axe and divine weapons as well.

**13.18.12**  'No sin shall be yours this day, and you shall be unconquerable; death shall have no power over you, and you shall be full of glory.'"

**13.18.13**  "Thus the Blessed One, the crested one whose very form is Śiva, spoke to me; and all that I have attained is by the grace of that wise god."

**13.18.14**  And Asita Devala addressed the king, the son of Pāṇḍu: "By a curse of Śakra, O son of Kuntī, my accumulated merit was perishing; but Bhava restored to me that merit, my foremost glory, and my life as well."

**13.18.15**  The seer named Gṛtsamada, the beloved friend of Śakra, blessed and radiant as Bṛhaspati, addressed the descendant of Ajamīḍha:

**13.18.16**  "The blessed one named Vasiṣṭha, son of Manu Cākṣuṣa, while the inconceivable Śatakratu's sacrificial session of a thousand years was in progress, spoke these words when a Sāman had been chanted by me:

**13.18.17**  'O best of the twice-born, the Rathantara is not rightly rendered; consider it again with your mind, casting off your excitement, O foremost of the twice-born. You have committed a sin that bears no sacrifice, O most wicked-minded one.'

**13.18.18**  Having spoken thus, in great wrath he angrily uttered these further words: 'Bereft of wisdom, wretched, forever fearful, a wanderer of the woods shall you become—for ten thousand years and ten and eight hundred more,

**13.18.19**  in a region without water or pasture, shunned by deer and other beasts, with no trees fit for sacrifice, haunted by antelope and lion—there you shall become a savage beast beset with great suffering.'

**13.18.20**  At the close of that utterance, O Pārtha, I was indeed born a beast; then, when I had come to him for refuge, the yogin Maheśvara said to me:

**13.18.21**  'Ageless and deathless shall you become, free of sorrow; even and equable shall your happiness be—and may the sacrificial rite of you both prosper.'"

**13.18.22**  "Thus does this Blessed and all-pervading Lord bestow his favors—the supreme Ordainer and Disposer, and ever the giver of pleasure and pain.

**13.18.23**  Inconceivable is this Blessed One in deed, in thought, and in speech; not even one learned in knowledge, dear child, O best of warriors, is his equal."

**13.18.24**  Jaigīṣavya said: "The eightfold lordly power was given to me of old by the mighty Blessed One, with but little effort, at Vārāṇasī, O Yudhiṣṭhira."

**13.18.25**  Gārgya said: "The wondrous knowledge of time, with its sixty-four branches, he gave to me, well pleased by a sacrifice of the mind, upon the bank of the Sarasvatī, O Pāṇḍava.

**13.18.26**  And he gave me a thousand sons, all alike, expounders of the sacred word, and a lifespan—for me together with my sons—of a hundred and ten thousand years."

**13.18.27**  Parāśara said: "Having propitiated Śarva of old, O king, I pondered in my mind—desiring a son of great austerity, great splendor, great yoga, and great fame, a Vedavyāsa, an abode of glory, devoted to brahman, and compassionate of nature:

**13.18.28**  'Might there be granted to me from Maheśvara the son I desire?' Knowing this resolve in my heart, the best of the gods spoke to me:

**13.18.29**  'As the fruit of his being born of me, he shall be Kṛṣṇa, and in the creation of Manu Sāvarṇa he shall be one of the seven seers.

**13.18.30**  He shall be the divider of the Vedas and the continuer of the Kuru line, and the author of the epic history; your son shall be a benefactor of the world.

**13.18.31**  That great sage shall become beloved of Mahendra, ageless and deathless, O Parāśara—he, your son.'

**13.18.32**  Having spoken thus, that Blessed One vanished then and there, O Yudhiṣṭhira—the great yogin, the valiant, the imperishable, the undecaying."

**13.18.33**  Māṇḍavya said: "When, though no thief, on suspicion of theft I was impaled upon the stake, I praised the god while fixed there, and Maheśvara said to me:

**13.18.34**  'You shall be freed from the stake, and you shall live a hundred million years; nor shall the pain caused by the stake be yours, O brāhmaṇa, and free of mental and bodily afflictions shall you be.

**13.18.35**  Since your self, O sage, has come forth from the fourth quarter, you shall be without compare; make your birth bear fruit indeed.

**13.18.36**  The fruitful bathing in sacred fords you shall attain without hindrance, and an imperishable heaven, mighty and exalted, I bestow upon you, O brāhmaṇa.'

**13.18.37**  Having spoken thus, the Blessed One, the most excellent, borne upon the bull, Maheśvara, O great king, clad in his hide and of mighty radiance, foremost of the gods together with his hosts, vanished then and there."

**13.18.38**  Gālava said: "Dismissed with leave by Viśvāmitra, I came to my father; then my mother, sorrowing and weeping bitterly, said to me:

**13.18.39**  'Your father does not behold you, dear child—his son adorned with the Vedas, dismissed with leave by Kauśika, young, self-controlled, and sinless.'

**13.18.40**  Hearing my mother's words, despairing of seeing my father, with self subdued I beheld Mahādeva, and he said to me:

**13.18.41**  'Your father and your mother and you yourself, my son, shall be free of death; enter quickly, and you shall behold your father in his dwelling.'

**13.18.42**  Dismissed with leave by the Blessed One, having gone home, O Yudhiṣṭhira, I beheld my father, dear lord, just come forth from completing his offering.

**13.18.43**  Having touched water and taken up the fuel-sticks and the kuśa grass, and having set down those holy implements within the dwelling, my father, his eyes brimming with tears, said to me—

**13.18.44**  embracing me as I bowed and smelling my head, O Pāṇḍava: 'By good fortune are you seen by me, my son, accomplished in learning and come here at last.'"

**13.18.45**  Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard these most wondrous deeds of the great-souled one recounted by the sages, the Pāṇḍava was filled with amazement.

**13.18.46**  Then Kṛṣṇa, foremost of the wise, spoke again to Yudhiṣṭhira, ever devoted to dharma, as the Lord might speak to Indra of the many invocations:

**13.18.47**  "The sun and moon, the wind and fire, the sky, the earth, the waters, the Vasus, the All-gods, the Ordainer, Aryaman, Śukra and Bṛhaspati, the Rudras together with the Sādhyas, Varuṇa the guardian of wealth,

**13.18.48**  Brahmā, Śakra, the Wind, the sacred word, truth, the Vedas, the sacrifices, the priestly fee, the bearers of the Vedas, Soma, the sacrificer, and whatever is offered and the oblation itself, protection, consecration, and whatever observances there are,

**13.18.49**  the cries Svāhā and Vaṣaṭ, the brāhmaṇas, the offspring of the divine cow, dharma, the wheel and the moving wheel of time, glory, self-restraint, intelligent steadfastness, the auspicious and the inauspicious, and the seven sages—

**13.18.50**  the foremost intellect, perception by mind and sight, attainment in touch, and the attainment that crowns deeds, the hosts of the gods—the drinkers of warm vapor and the drinkers of Soma, the Lekhas, the Suyāmas, the Tuṣitas, the Brahmakāyas,

**13.18.51**  the Ābhāsvaras, the drinkers of fragrance, the sustainers of sight, those opposed in speech and those opposed in mind, the pure gods and those who delight in extinction, those who feed on touch, the beholders, and the drinkers of clarified butter—

**13.18.52**  those who abide in thought and are chief among the gods, and whatever other deities there are, O descendant of Ajamīḍha, the Suparṇas, Gandharvas, Piśācas, and Dānavas, the Yakṣas, the serpents, and the Cāraṇas—

**13.18.53**  the subtle, the gross, the soft, and what is not subtle, pleasure, pain, and what lies between pleasure and pain, Sāṃkhya and Yoga, and what is highest of the high—know all that I have named to be sprung from Śarva.

**13.18.54**  Sprung from him are the makers of beings, the most excellent; all the gods are guardians of this world, who, entering this earth, have protected the ancient creation of that god.

**13.18.55**  Searching with my mind, I would praise some truth for the sake of life; I am bowed down. May that god grant the boons desired here; may the undecaying Lord, ever praised by us, bestow them."

**13.18.56**  That man who, restraining his senses and having become pure, recites this hymn with unbroken discipline, self-controlled, for one year—he would obtain the fruit that lies in the horse sacrifice.

**13.18.57**  A brāhmaṇa would gain all the Vedas, a king would conquer the whole earth, a vaiśya would gain profit and skill, and a śūdra would win a good course after death and happiness as well.

**13.18.58**  Having made this king of hymns, they fixed their minds upon Rudra—the hymn that removes all faults, meritorious, purifying, and glory-bestowing.

**13.18.59**  As many as are the pores of the hair upon his body, O Bhārata, for so many thousands of years does that man dwell in heaven.

**13.19.1**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: "This thing that is called 'shared dharma,' O bull of the Bhāratas—how has it come to be enjoined for women at the time of the taking of the hand in marriage?

**13.19.2**  Is this the law of the seers, or of Prajāpati, or indeed of the asuras—this 'shared dharma' that was declared of old by the great sages?

**13.19.3**  A very great doubt is this, and a contradiction, in my view: the shared dharma that holds here in this life—where, then, is it ordained to hold in the world beyond?

**13.19.4**  Does shared dharma belong to the dead in heaven, O grandsire? Yet one dies first while the other remains—tell me, where then is it?"

**13.19.5**  "When men are many, endowed with the fruits of diverse deeds, dwelling in diverse states of action, ending in diverse hells,

**13.19.6**  and when the author of the aphorisms lays down that 'women are untruthful'—since women are untruthful, dear lord, whence is shared dharma enjoined for them?

**13.19.7**  'Women are untruthful'—even in the Vedas this is so recited. This dharma, this ancient designation, this customary usage, this rule of rites—

**13.19.8**  all this appears to me an impenetrable thicket as I ponder it day and night; make all of this free of doubt for me, O grandsire, as the sacred revelation has it."

**13.19.9**  Of what nature this is, and just how it came to be ordained — let your honored self declare all of it to me in full, O profoundly wise one.

**13.19.10**  Bhīṣma said: On this matter too they recount an ancient tale, the dialogue of Aṣṭāvakra with the Quarter of Space, O descendant of Bharata.

**13.19.11**  In days of old, Aṣṭāvakra of great austerities, wishing to marry, sought the daughter of the high-souled sage Vadānya.

**13.19.12**  Suprabhā she was named, peerless in beauty upon the earth, foremost in virtues, of upright conduct, radiant in character.

**13.19.13**  That fair-eyed maiden, merely by the sight of her, stole away his heart, as a glorious belt of forest does in spring, heaped with blossoms.

**13.19.14**  The sage said to him: My daughter shall be given to you — hear me out. Go first to the holy northern quarter, and there you shall behold a sight.

**13.19.15**  Aṣṭāvakra said: What is it I am to behold there? Be pleased to tell me, sir; and even so shall I act now, just as your honored self shall instruct me.

**13.19.16**  Vadānya said: Passing beyond the realm of Kubera the Wealth-giver, and likewise beyond Himavat, having looked upon the abode of Rudra, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas —

**13.19.17**  thronged by his joyful attendants dancing with manifold faces, by Piśācas anointed with divine unguents, by woodland beings of every kind,

**13.19.18**  and with hand-claps for cymbals and rhythm beaten on wooden bars in even measure — by these, exultant and dancing, is Śarva there attended.

**13.19.19**  That divine abode upon the mountain is beloved of him, so we have heard recounted; ever present there is the god, and with him his auspicious attendants.

**13.19.20**  There the Goddess performed austerity most hard to bear for Śaṃkara's sake; therefore that place is dear to the god and to Umā alike — so runs the tradition.

**13.19.21**  There, on the northern side beside the god, is a great well; and the seasons, and Kālarātri the Night of Doom, both those that are divine and those that are mortal —

**13.19.22**  all of them, taking embodied form, there wait upon the god, so it is told. Passing beyond that dwelling, you must journey on.

**13.19.23**  Then you shall see a tract of dark-blue forest, resembling a rain-cloud, lovely and heart-captivating; and there you shall behold a woman.

**13.19.24**  An ascetic woman, greatly blessed, aged, established in her vows — her you must behold there, and reverence with all care.

**13.19.25**  Having seen her, you shall return, and then take my daughter's hand in marriage. If this compact be acceptable, let it be fulfilled — go thither.

**13.20.1**  Aṣṭāvakra said: So be it; I shall accomplish this. Without doubt I will go there where you bid me, O virtuous one; let your honored self prove true to his word.

**13.20.2**  Bhīṣma said: Then that reverend one set out toward the supreme northern quarter, toward Himavat, best of mountains, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas.

**13.20.3**  That tiger among the twice-born, journeying to the great mountain Himavat, came upon the holy river Bāhudā, bestower of righteousness.

**13.20.4**  At the pure ford of Aśoka he bathed and made offerings to the gods, and there, settling for the night upon a couch of kuśa grass, he rested at ease.

**13.20.5**  Then, when the night had passed, the twice-born one rose at dawn, bathed, kindled the sacred fire, and made oblation according to the rite.

**13.20.6**  Coming to the Well of Rudrāṇī, he refreshed himself in the pool there; and when rested he arose and went on toward Kailāsa.

**13.20.7**  He beheld a golden gateway, blazing as it were with splendor, and the Mandākinī, and the lotus-pond of the high-souled Wealth-giver.

**13.20.8**  Then all those Rākṣasas who guard the lotus-pool rose up before the reverend one, with Maṇibhadra at their head.

**13.20.9**  He greeted those Rākṣasas of fearsome valor in turn, and said: Announce me at once to the Wealth-giver.

**13.20.10**  Then those Rākṣasas, O king, said to the reverend one: Yonder King Vaiśravaṇa comes himself into your presence.

**13.20.11**  The reverend one is known to him, and the purpose of his coming; behold him now, that greatly blessed lord, blazing as if with radiance.

**13.20.12**  Then Vaiśravaṇa, approaching the blameless Aṣṭāvakra and inquiring after his welfare as the rite prescribes, said to that sage among brahmans:

**13.20.13**  Have you come in comfort, sir? And what would you have of me? Speak — whatever you shall ask of me, twice-born one, all that I will do.

**13.20.14**  Enter my dwelling at your pleasure, O best of the twice-born; honored and with your purpose fulfilled, you shall depart unhindered.

**13.20.15**  He entered his own dwelling, having taken that best of the twice-born by the hand, and gave him his own seat, and water for his feet, and the welcome-offering as well.

**13.20.16**  When the two were seated there, Kubera's own folk — Yakṣas, Gandharvas, and Rākṣasas, led by Maṇibhadra — took their places there.

**13.20.17**  Then, when they were seated, the Wealth-giver spoke this word: Learning your honored one's pleasure, let the troops of Apsarases dance.

**13.20.18**  "Supreme hospitality must be shown, and service rendered to you — so let it be," said he. And the sage replied in a sweet voice, "Let it proceed."

**13.20.19**  Then Urvarā and Miśrakeśī, Rambhā and Urvaśī too, Alambusā and Ghṛtācī, Citrā, Citrāṅgadā, Ruci,

**13.20.20**  Manoharā and Sukeśī, Sumukhī, Hāsinī, Prabhā, Vidyutā, Praśamā, Dāntā, Vidyotā, and Rati as well —

**13.20.21**  these and many other fair Apsarases fell to dancing, and the Gandharvas sounded their instruments of every kind.

**13.20.22**  And when the divine Gandharva music had begun, the sage of mighty austerities tarried there, delighting, a full celestial year.

**13.20.23**  Then King Vaiśravaṇa said to the reverend one: A full year and more has passed for you here, O brahman, while you watched.

**13.20.24**  Enchanting is this pleasure, O brahman, Gandharva music by name; let it continue at your pleasure, sir, or as your honored self may bid.

**13.20.25**  You are a guest to be honored, and this house is yours; command all of it at once — we are wholly subject to you.

**13.20.26**  Then the reverend one, well pleased, replied to Vaiśravaṇa: I have been honored as is fitting; I shall now depart, O lord of wealth.

**13.20.27**  I am pleased, and all things here befit you, O lord of riches. By your grace, my lord, and by the charge of the high-souled great sage, I depart today; may you flourish and prosper.

**13.20.28**  Then the reverend one, going forth, journeyed on facing northward, and traversed all the golden heights — Kailāsa and Mandara.

**13.20.29**  Passing beyond those great mountains, he made reverent circuit of the supreme abode of the Kirātas, bowing with his head; and descending to the earth, he became then purified in soul.

**13.20.30**  Having circled the mountain thrice and turned to face north, he went on over level ground, gladness leading him onward.

**13.20.31**  Then he beheld another lovely tract of forest, furnished with roots and fruits of every season and with birds, adorned here and there with delightful woodland glades.

**13.20.32**  There the reverend one beheld a divine hermitage-ground, and golden crags of manifold form, jewel-bedecked, and lotus-pools set into a soil of gems.

**13.20.33**  Many other charming things besides he beheld; and the mind of the great sage, his soul refined, took deep delight.

**13.20.34**  There he saw a divine golden mansion, wrought all of jewels, of wondrous aspect, surpassing even the dwelling of the Wealth-giver.

**13.20.35**  There stood great palaces of many kinds, like mountains, and lovely sky-borne chariots, and gems of every sort.

**13.20.36**  The river Mandākinī was strewn with mandāra blossoms, and there were self-luminous jewels, and the ground was adorned with diamonds.

**13.20.37**  On every side it was encompassed by mansions of many kinds, with archways of variegated gems, festooned with nets of pearls and decked with jewels and precious stones, ravishing to mind and eye, lovely and auspicious.

**13.20.38**  The sage looked all about and saw delight on every hand; then a thought arose in him: Where might my lodging be?

**13.20.39**  Then, going up close to the gateway and standing there, he said: Let those who are within grant leave to me, a guest who has arrived.

**13.20.40**  Then forth from that house came maidens, attended one upon another — seven maidens, O lord, of varied form, all of them ravishing.

**13.20.41**  Whichever maiden he looked upon, that one stole away his heart; he could not hold his mind steady, and it began to sink within him.

**13.20.42**  Then resolve arose in that wise brahman; and the fair women said to him: Let the reverend one enter.

**13.20.43**  And filled with wonder both at those lovely women and at the mansion itself, the twice-born one entered the house.

**13.20.44**  There he beheld a woman bowed with age, clad in spotless garments, aged, seated upon a couch, and decked with every ornament.

**13.20.45**  And when he had greeted her with "Hail," that woman answered him then, and rising before the brahman, she said: Be seated.

**13.20.46**  Aṣṭāvakra said: Let all of them go to their own quarters; let one well-discerning and well-composed attend upon me; let the rest depart at their pleasure.

**13.20.47**  Then those maidens, having circled the sage in reverence, went forth from that house; but the aged one remained behind.

**13.20.48**  Then, lying down upon the shining bed, he said to her: Do you too take your rest, good lady, for the night is wearing away.

**13.20.49**  Being thus addressed by the brahman in talk, she lay down upon a second bed there, divine and of great splendor.

**13.20.50**  Then she, her limbs trembling, pleading the cold as her pretext, climbed up onto the great sage's bed.

**13.20.51**  "Welcome — let welcome be yours," the reverend one said to her; and she clasped the sage in her two arms with affection, O bull among men.

**13.20.52**  But seeing the sage unmoved, like a post or a wall, she grew distressed, and entered into talk with the sage.

**13.20.53**  Brahman, women have no power over desire, nor restraint before a man; bewildered with longing am I — accept me who seek you in love.

**13.20.54**  Be glad, O sage among brahmans; unite yourself with me; embrace me, brahman — I am sorely afflicted with desire for you.

**13.20.55**  For this, O righteous one, is honored as the fruit of your austerity, sought from the mere sight of you — accept me who give myself to you.

**13.20.56**  This mansion and this forest, and whatever else you see — over all of it your lordship extends, and over me as well, beyond doubt.

**13.20.57**  I shall fulfill every desire; take your delight together with me, O brahman, in this lovely forest that yields the fruit of all desires.

**13.20.58**  I shall be wholly yours, and you shall take delight with me, enjoying all the pleasures, both those that are divine and those that are mortal.

**13.20.59**  For there is no higher aim for women than union with a man; this indeed is our supreme fruit.

**13.20.60**  Women act by their own will, driven on by the god of love; even going their way over coals of well-heated dust, they are not burned.

**13.20.61**  Aṣṭāvakra said: I would never, good lady, approach another man's wife; the touching of another's wife is condemned in the treatises of dharma.

**13.20.62**  Know me, good lady, to be one who wishes to marry — by truth I swear it; I am untutored in the pleasures of sense, for offspring is begotten for the sake of dharma.

**13.20.63**  Thus, through sons, shall I attain the higher worlds — of this there is no doubt. Understand righteousness, good lady, and understanding it, desist.

**13.20.64**  The woman said: Not the Wind, not Fire, not Varuṇa, nor any of the other gods, O brāhmaṇa, are as dear to women as is desire; for women are creatures given over to pleasure.

**13.20.65**  Scarcely one woman in a thousand is found here who is restrained; and among a hundred thousand, only here and there is one devoted to her husband.

**13.20.66**  They heed neither father nor lineage nor mother, neither brothers nor husband, neither sons nor brothers-in-law.

**13.20.67**  Sporting in their wantonness, they destroy their families as the great rivers wear away their banks; and Prajāpati declared that such failings dwell within women of weak mind.

**13.20.68**  Bhīṣma said: Then the sage, with collected mind, answered that woman: "As you please, be seated; or tell me—what is the task you would have done?"

**13.20.69**  The woman replied: "Lord, in due place and time you shall see. Dwell here a while, O greatly wise one; when your purpose is accomplished, you shall depart."

**13.20.70**  The brāhmaṇa-seer then said to her, "So be it," O Yudhiṣṭhira—"I shall dwell here as long as it pleases you; of that there is no doubt."

**13.20.71**  Then the seer, gazing upon that woman bowed down with age, fell into deep reflection and became as one consumed with care.

**13.20.72**  Whatever limb of hers that bull among brāhmaṇas looked upon, there his gaze found no delight, overcome by her ruined form.

**13.20.73**  "Surely this is the deity of this house, disfigured by some curse; yet it would not be fitting for me to seek out the cause of it in haste."

**13.20.74**  As he was thus absorbed in thought, longing to know the truth of the matter, the remainder of that day passed away while his mind was troubled.

**13.20.75**  Then that woman said: "Lord, behold the form of the sun joined with the clouds of twilight. What shall be made ready for you?"

**13.20.76**  He then said to that woman: "Bring water here for bathing; then, restrained in speech and with senses controlled, I shall attend upon the twilight rite."

**13.21.1**  Bhīṣma said: Then that woman, saying to the brāhmaṇa, "So be it," took up celestial oil and brought to him a bathing-cloth.

**13.21.2**  And, granted leave by that great-souled sage, the woman anointed all his limbs with the oil.

**13.21.3**  Gently rubbed down, he went into the bathing-chamber; and the seer then took his place upon a fine new seat richly adorned.

**13.21.4**  And when he was seated upon that goodly seat, she bathed the seer slowly, with a gentle hand, and performed for the sage the celestial rite duly, with every attendance.

**13.21.5**  By that pleasantly warm water and by the soothing touch of her hand, that man of great vows did not perceive that the whole night had passed away.

**13.21.6**  Then the sage, rising up in utter amazement, beheld the sun risen in the sky in the eastern quarter.

**13.21.7**  This thought came to him: "Is this a delusion, or is it the truth?" Then, having worshipped the thousand-rayed one, he said to her, "What shall I do?"

**13.21.8**  She set before the seer food that was like the taste of nectar; and by reason of the sweetness of that food he could not make an end of it. So the rest of the day passed away, and the twilight came again.

**13.21.9**  Then that woman urged the lord, saying, "Let us sleep," upon celestial couches there made ready, one for him and one for her.

**13.21.10**  Aṣṭāvakra said: "No, good lady; my mind does not cling to another man's wife. Rise up, good lady—blessings upon you—go to sleep, and desist."

**13.21.11**  Bhīṣma said: She, thus turned back by the brāhmaṇa's firmness, said to him, "I am my own mistress; there is no deceiving of dharma in this for you."

**13.21.12**  Aṣṭāvakra said: "Women have no independence; a woman is never her own mistress. This is the doctrine of Prajāpati: a woman is not entitled to independence."

**13.21.13**  The woman said: "Desire torments me, O brāhmaṇa; behold too my devotion. You will incur unrighteousness, O brāhmaṇa, in that you will not welcome me."

**13.21.14**  Aṣṭāvakra said: "Faults that are born within carry a man off wherever they will once they arise; but I am ever master of myself through firmness. Go, good lady, to your own couch."

**13.21.15**  The woman said: "With my head I bow, O brāhmaṇa; deign to show me grace. To me who am falling to the ground, be my refuge, O sinless one."

**13.21.16**  "But if you see a fault arising in approaching another man's wife, then this day I make a gift of myself: take my hand, O brāhmaṇa."

**13.21.17**  "And no fault shall there be—this I tell you in truth. Know me to be my own mistress; whatever unrighteousness there be, let it rest upon me."

**13.21.18**  Aṣṭāvakra said: "How are you your own mistress, good lady? Tell me the reason for this. There is no woman in the world who is entitled to independence."

**13.21.19**  "In childhood the father protects her, in youth the husband, and in old age the sons; a woman is not entitled to independence."

**13.21.20**  The woman said: "Mine is the chastity of girlhood; I am yet a maiden, without doubt. Harbor no misgiving, O brāhmaṇa; do not cast away your faith in me."

**13.21.21**  Aṣṭāvakra said: "As it is for me, so it is for you; as it is for you, so for me. Let me probe this: is this hindrance to the seer real, or what?

**13.21.22**  "For this is a thing of the utmost wonder. What course would be best for me? This maiden, decked in celestial ornaments and garments, has come before me."

**13.21.23**  "But how was her surpassing beauty aged before, and how again has she now this very day the form of a maiden? What can be the answer to this?"

**13.21.24**  "Yet so far as my strength of resolve avails, I shall in no wise swerve; for swerving I deem not good. By steadfastness thus do I prevail."

**13.22.1**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: How was it that the woman did not fear the curse of one so resplendent? And how did the venerable one desist? Tell me this, I pray.

**13.22.2**  Bhīṣma said: Aṣṭāvakra questioned her: "How is it that you change your form? You must speak no falsehood; tell me, out of regard for a brāhmaṇa."

**13.22.3**  The woman said: "This desire of mine is as boundless as heaven and earth, O best of brāhmaṇas. Listen attentively to all of it, O you of truthful valor."

**13.22.4**  "Know me to be the Northern Quarter. The fickleness of women has been shown to you; and by your not swerving, the heavenly worlds have been won by you, O you whose valor is truth."

**13.22.5**  "This testing was set in motion by me to make you steadfast, O sinless one—for even in aged women the fever of desire still torments."

**13.22.6**  "The Grandsire is pleased with you this day, and so are the gods together with Vāsava. And as for the purpose for which you, venerable one, have come here—

**13.22.7**  "sent by that brāhmaṇa, the father of the maiden, O bull among the twice-born, to make the instruction known to you—all of that has been accomplished by me."

**13.22.8**  "Safe shall you go to your home, and weariness shall not come upon you. You shall win that maiden, O brāhmaṇa, and she shall bear you sons."

**13.22.9**  "You questioned me out of desire, and so the answer was uttered—an answer that can never be gainsaid by all the three worlds together."

**13.22.10**  "Go now, your good work done. Or is there aught else you wish to hear, that I may tell it truly, O seer among brāhmaṇas, Aṣṭāvakra?"

**13.22.11**  "I have been entreated by the seer on your behalf, O bull among the twice-born; and to do him honor these words of mine were spoken to you."

**13.22.12**  Having heard her words, the brāhmaṇa stood with palms joined; and, taking leave of her, he made his way back to his own home.

**13.22.13**  Having come home and rested, and having honored his kinsfolk, he went duly to that brāhmaṇa, O delight of the Kurus.

**13.22.14**  And being questioned by that brāhmaṇa, "Has this token been seen?", the brāhmaṇa then spoke to the brāhmaṇa with a heart well pleased:

**13.22.15**  "Granted leave by you, I set out for Gandhamādana; and in the region to the north of it I beheld that mighty deity."

**13.22.16**  "And, granted leave by her, with you too made known to her, and having been told her saying, I have come home, my lord."

**13.22.17**  Then the brāhmaṇa said to him: "Receive my daughter, when star and lunar day are in conjunction; for you are a most worthy recipient."

**13.22.18**  Bhīṣma said: Aṣṭāvakra, saying "So be it," and accepting that maiden, O lord—he of the highest righteousness—was then filled with joy.

**13.22.19**  Having received that maiden as his most beautiful wife, he dwelt there gladly in his own hermitage, his fever of doubt now gone.

**13.23.1**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: Whom, O best of the Bhāratas, do the brāhmaṇas declare to be from of old a worthy recipient—the brāhmaṇa who bears the outward marks, or the brāhmaṇa without them?

**13.23.2**  Bhīṣma said: To one who keeps to his proper conduct, whether he bears the marks or not, a gift should be given, O great king; for both of these are men of austerity.

**13.23.3**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: When a man, purified by the highest faith, presents to a twice-born the offering to the gods, the offering to the ancestors, and gifts, what fault could there be, O Grandsire?

**13.23.4**  Bhīṣma said: A man purified by faith, my son, even though he be hard to discipline, becomes pure in every way, without doubt—how much more, then, do you, O lord of the earth.

**13.23.5**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: In rites to the gods a man should never examine the brāhmaṇa; but in the giving of offerings to the ancestors, the wise hold that the brāhmaṇa is to be examined.

**13.23.6**  Bhīṣma said: It is not the brāhmaṇa who brings the offering to fulfillment; it succeeds by the gods' ordinance. By the grace of the gods the sacrificers obtain their fruit, without doubt.

**13.23.7**  The brāhmaṇas, O best of the Bhāratas, are ever expounders of the sacred word; thus did the wise Mārkaṇḍeya declare of old here among the worlds.

**13.23.8**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: Whether a man be a stranger or a learned one, or a kinsman, or an ascetic, or one given to sacrifice—how is it that such a one becomes a worthy recipient?

**13.23.9**  Bhīṣma said: Wellborn, performing his rites, learned in the Veda, compassionate, modest, upright, truthful—such a one is a worthy recipient; and the first three among these qualities are foremost.

**13.23.10**  On this point hear from me, O Pārtha, the judgment of four glorious beings—of the Earth, of Kāśyapa, of Agni, and of Mārkaṇḍeya.

**13.23.11**  The Earth said: As a clod of earth cast into the great ocean swiftly dissolves away, so all ill conduct is dissolved away by the recitation of the threefold Veda.

**13.23.12**  Kāśyapa said: All the Vedas together with their six limbs, the Sāṃkhya, the Purāṇa, and birth in a noble line—none of these, all of them together, become a refuge for the man who is bereft of good character, O king.

**13.23.13**  Agni said: He who, learned in the texts and accounting himself a sage, destroys the renown of others by his learning—by that, O brāhmaṇa, he commits the slaying of a brāhmaṇa, and his heavenly worlds come to an end.

**13.23.14**  Mārkaṇḍeya said: A thousand horse-sacrifices and truth were weighed in the balance; and I do not find that the one would attain even to half of that truth.

**13.23.15**  Bhīṣma said: Having spoken thus, those four of boundless splendor swiftly departed—the Earth, Kāśyapa, Agni, and the long-lived scion of Bhṛgu.

**13.23.16**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: When brāhmaṇas in the world who keep their vows eat the sacrificial offering, that offering eaten for the sake of a brāhmaṇa—how does it become a meritorious deed?

**13.23.17**  Bhīṣma said: Those brāhmaṇas, O king of kings, learned to the end of the Veda, who, being invited, eat for the sake of a brāhmaṇa—they become fallen from their vows.

**13.23.18**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: The wise call dharma many-sided and of many doors. What in it may be held as certain? Tell me that, O Grandsire.

**13.23.19**  Bhīṣma said: Non-injury, truth, freedom from anger, compassion, self-restraint, and uprightness—this, O king of kings, is the certain mark of dharma.

**13.23.20**  But those who go about this earth praising dharma while not practicing that dharma, devoted to confusion of duties, O lord—

**13.23.21**  he who gives to them a jewel, or gold, or a cow, or horses—for ten years he feeds upon filth, lodged in hell.

**13.23.22**  Of the meda outcastes, of the pulkasas, and likewise of those who dwell at the cremation-ground, the rite performed is as good as unperformed, since they babble out of passion and delusion.

**13.23.23**  And those fools who give the Vaiśvadeva offering to a brāhmaṇa who is a student of the sacred word—nay, O king of kings, they go to enjoy worlds of ill.

**13.23.24**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: What is the highest form of chastity, what the highest mark of dharma, and what the most excellent purity? Tell me that, O Grandsire.

**13.23.25**  Bhīṣma said: Chastity is the highest course, dear son, and the renunciation of honey and meat; dharma abides within bounds, and tranquillity is the mark of purity.

**13.23.26**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: At what time should one pursue dharma, at what time pursue wealth, and at what time enjoy pleasure? Tell me this, grandfather.

**13.23.27**  Bhīṣma said: In the early hours let him attend to wealth, then immediately after to dharma; afterward let him attend to pleasure, yet never give himself over to attachment.

**13.23.28**  Let him hold the brāhmaṇas in honour and revere his elders; gentle toward all beings, soft of nature, and kindly in speech.

**13.23.29**  Falsehood in the exercise of office, slander carried to the king, and deceit practised against one's teacher—each of these is equal to the slaying of a brāhmaṇa.

**13.23.30**  Let him not strike at kings, nor likewise slay a cow; he who indulges in either of these does what is equal to the killing of an embryo.

**13.23.31**  Let him never abandon the sacred fire, nor forsake the Vedas, nor revile a brāhmaṇa—for that too is equal to the slaying of a brāhmaṇa.

**13.23.32**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: What kind of brāhmaṇas are the virtuous ones, gifts to whom bear great fruit, and of what kind are those whose food may be eaten? Tell me this, grandfather.

**13.23.33**  Bhīṣma said: Free from anger, devoted to dharma, ever truthful, delighting in self-restraint—such are the virtuous brāhmaṇas; a gift given to them bears great fruit.

**13.23.34**  Free from conceit, all-enduring, having perceived the truth, their senses subdued, friendly and devoted to the welfare of all beings—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

**13.23.35**  Free from greed, pure, learned, modest, truthful in speech, and intent upon their own duty—a gift given to such men bears great fruit.

**13.23.36**  That bull among the twice-born who has studied the four Vedas with their auxiliary sciences, and who has turned away from the six base occupations—him the seers know to be a worthy recipient.

**13.23.37**  Those who are endowed with such qualities—a gift given to them bears great fruit; the giver to one worthy by his merits gains a thousandfold reward.

**13.23.38**  Endowed with wisdom and sacred learning, with right conduct and good character, a single bull among the twice-born can in this world deliver an entire lineage.

**13.23.39**  Let him bestow upon such a one a cow, a horse, wealth, or food, and other goods besides; then in the life beyond he shall not grieve.

**13.23.40**  Even one foremost among the twice-born can in this world deliver a whole lineage—how much more, then, a single soul? Therefore let one seek out a worthy recipient.

**13.23.41**  And having heard of a brāhmaṇa endowed with virtue and esteemed by the good, let him summon him from afar for the rite and honour him in every way.

**13.24.1**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: Concerning the time of the śrāddha, concerning the offering to the gods, and concerning dharma as well, grandfather, I wish to hear from you what has been ordained by the divine seers.

**13.24.2**  Bhīṣma said: Let him perform the offering to the gods in the forenoon, but the rite for the ancestors in the afternoon, accomplished in auspicious observances, having performed his purifications, and diligent.

**13.24.3**  But to men he should give at midday, as is fitting; a gift bestowed out of its proper time—that portion they know to belong to the rākṣasas.

**13.24.4**  What has been stepped over, what has been licked, what has been done amid strife, and what has been looked upon by women in their courses—that portion they know to belong to the rākṣasas.

**13.24.5**  What is eaten amid clamour, and what is eaten by one who keeps no vows, O Bhārata, and what has been touched by a dog—that portion they know to belong to the rākṣasas.

**13.24.6**  Food into which a hair or an insect has fallen, upon which one has sneezed, which dogs have gazed upon, over which there has been weeping, or which has been shaken about—that portion they know to belong to the rākṣasas.

**13.24.7**  What is eaten without the sacred syllable Oṃ, and what is eaten with a weapon at hand, O Bhārata, and what is eaten by an evil-souled man—that portion they know to belong to the rākṣasas.

**13.24.8**  What is eaten that has been left over by another, and what may have already been partaken of—at the rite for the gods or for the ancestors alike, that portion they ever know to belong to the rākṣasas.

**13.24.9**  What is reviled and condemned, what is served amid wrath, whether at the rite for the gods or for the ancestors—that portion they know to belong to the rākṣasas.

**13.24.10**  A śrāddha that is served wanting in sacred chants and wanting in proper rites by the three varṇas, O best of men—that portion they know to belong to the rākṣasas.

**13.24.11**  Whatever is served without the oblation of clarified butter, and what is eaten by men of evil conduct—that portion they know to belong to the rākṣasas.

**13.24.12**  Those portions that are declared to belong to the rākṣasas have now been told, O bull of the Bhāratas; henceforth hear the examination of the brāhmaṇa upon the giving away of the gift.

**13.24.13**  All those brāhmaṇas who are fallen, and likewise the dull-witted and the mad—at the rite for the gods or for the ancestors, O king, they deserve no invitation.

**13.24.14**  The man afflicted with white leprosy, the leper, the eunuch, he who is wasted by consumption, the epileptic, and the blind, O king, deserve no such honour.

**13.24.15**  Physicians, temple priests who serve images for hire, those who keep vows to no purpose, and sellers of the soma—at a śrāddha they deserve no invitation.

**13.24.16**  Singers and dancers, acrobats and players of instruments, reciters of tales and prize-fighters, O king, deserve no invitation.

**13.24.17**  Those who officiate at the sacrifices of the base-born, and those who instruct the base-born, and likewise the pupils of the base-born, O king, deserve no invitation.

**13.24.18**  The brāhmaṇa who hires another's sacred service and he who is so hired, O Bhārata—neither of these two deserves the śrāddha, for both are sellers of sacred knowledge.

**13.24.19**  A brāhmaṇa who has been made the leader at the marriage of a man of lower varṇa—though he be versed in all the sciences, O king, he deserves no invitation.

**13.24.20**  Those brāhmaṇas who keep no sacred fires, and those who bear forth the dead for hire, and thieves and the fallen, O king, deserve no invitation.

**13.24.21**  Those of unknown ancestry, and those born of a guild's promiscuous union, O Bhārata, and the sons born of an appointed daughter—at a śrāddha they deserve no invitation.

**13.24.22**  The maker of debts, O king, and the twice-born who lives by usury, and he whose livelihood is the selling of living creatures, O king, deserve no invitation.

**13.24.23**  Those who were once women, and the makers of arrow-shafts, all of them, O bull of the Bhāratas, and brāhmaṇas who do not chant the sāvitrī—at a śrāddha they deserve no invitation.

**13.24.24**  The brāhmaṇas who are debarred from the śrāddha and the offering to the gods have been named, O bull of the Bhāratas; now hear again, of giver and receiver alike, who are worthy of favour.

**13.24.25**  Those who have fulfilled their vows and are endowed with virtues—even if they be tillers of the soil—if they know the sāvitrī and perform the rites, they, O king, are fit to be invited.

**13.24.26**  Even a well-born twice-born who follows the kṣatriya's dharma in battle one may invite; but a trader, dear son, one should never appoint at the śrāddhas.

**13.24.27**  The brāhmaṇa who maintains the agnihotra fire, who dwells in the village, who is no thief and is mindful of guests—he, O king, is fit to be invited.

**13.24.28**  He who chants the sāvitrī at the three junctures of the day, O bull of the Bhāratas, who lives by alms and performs the rites—he, O king, is fit to be invited.

**13.24.29**  He who rises with the sun and rests at its setting, and likewise rests at its setting and rises with it, who does no harm and has but few faults—he, O king, is fit to be invited.

**13.24.30**  The brāhmaṇa free from guile and free from idle cavil, O bull of the Bhāratas, possessed of full awareness and living by alms—he, O king, is fit to be invited.

**13.24.31**  One who was vowless, a gambler, a thief, a seller of living creatures, and a trader, but who afterward has drunk the soma—he, O king, is fit to be invited.

**13.24.32**  One who first earned his wealth by the harsh labours of tillage, and who afterward becomes hospitable to all guests—he, O king, is fit to be invited.

**13.24.33**  Wealth got by the selling of sacred knowledge, wealth earned by a woman, and wealth gained through unmanliness—these are not to be given to the ancestors and the gods.

**13.24.34**  When the concluding rite is being performed, the twice-born who does not utter what is fitting, O bull of the Bhāratas—his transgression is as the falsehood that loses a cow.

**13.24.35**  The brāhmaṇa is the right occasion for the śrāddha; fit also are curds and clarified butter when they come to hand, the waning of the moon, and the flesh of forest game, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

**13.24.36**  At the conclusion of a brāhmaṇa's śrāddha, let the word svadhā be well pronounced; for a kṣatriya, too, let him then say, "May the ancestors be pleased."

**13.24.37**  At the conclusion of a vaiśya's śrāddha rite, O Bhārata, the word "imperishable" is to be spoken; and for a śūdra, "well-being," O Bhārata.

**13.24.38**  In the offering to the gods, the proclamation of an auspicious day is ordained for the brāhmaṇa; this same proclamation, without the syllable Oṃ, is ordained for the kṣatriya; and for the vaiśya it is to be spoken thus: "May the deities be pleased."

**13.24.39**  Hear now the due sequence of the rites and their prescribed performance—all the sacraments beginning with the birth-rite among the three varṇas, O Bhārata; for the brāhmaṇa and the kṣatriya they are enjoined with sacred chants, and so too for the vaiśya, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

**13.24.40**  For the brāhmaṇa the girdle is of muñja grass, for the kṣatriya it is of bowstring fibre, and for the vaiśya it is of balbaja grass—such is the law, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

**13.24.41**  Hear now, of the giver and the receiver alike, these their dharma and their transgression: for the brāhmaṇa, the sin in falsehood is declared to bear the name of a grievous fault; for the kṣatriya it is held to be fourfold, and for the vaiśya eightfold.

**13.24.42**  A brāhmaṇa, if invited beforehand by another brāhmaṇa, should not eat elsewhere; for the younger man who does so incurs a guilt equal to the slaughter of an animal.

**13.24.43**  But if, being invited, he should eat at the homes of a kṣatriya or a vaiśya, the younger man thereby incurs half the share of the guilt of slaying an animal.

**13.24.44**  The brāhmaṇa who eats at the rite for the gods or for the ancestors, in the houses of brāhmaṇas and the rest, while yet unbathed, O king—his transgression is as the falsehood that loses a cow.

**13.24.45**  The brāhmaṇa who, while in a state of impurity, eats in the houses of brāhmaṇas and the rest, knowingly and out of greed, O king—his transgression is as the falsehood that loses a cow.

**13.24.46**  He who would seek food in return for food, and who invites another merely for the sake of his own rite, O Bhārata, O lord of kings—his transgression is reckoned to be a falsehood.

**13.24.47**  Those wanting in the Vedas, in vows, and in good conduct, who are served as if entitled to the sacred chants by the three varṇas, O Yudhiṣṭhira—in their case the transgression is as the falsehood that loses a cow.

**13.24.48**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: Of that which is given at the rite for the ancestors or for the gods, grandfather, I wish to hear in whom a gift bestowed bears great fruit.

**13.24.49**  Bhīṣma said: Those whose wives await the leavings and remnants of the meal as tillers await a good rain—feed them, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

**13.24.50**  Those steadfast in good conduct, O king, who are lean and whose means are meagre, and who come as suppliants—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

**13.24.51**  Those who are devoted to you, who dwell in your house, O king, whose wealth and whose refuge lie in you, and who come as suppliants in their need—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

**13.24.52**  Those who, distressed by fear of thieves or of enemies, O Yudhiṣṭhira, come as suppliants desiring to eat—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

**13.24.53**  The young students who beg on behalf of a guileless brāhmaṇa, one who has shaped his soul by living on gleaned alms—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

**13.24.54**  Those brāhmaṇas who, robbed of their goods and bereft of their wives in the ruin of a land, come seeking aid—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

**13.24.55**  Those brāhmaṇas observing vows and firm in their restraints, esteemed for their sacred learning, who desire help for the completion of those vows—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

**13.24.56**  Those who have never strayed from the dharmas into the doctrines of heretics, whose vital strength is wasted and whose wealth is meagre—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

**13.24.57**  Those who, though blameless, have been stripped of all their possessions by the powerful, and who long for a meal of food—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

**13.24.58**  The ascetics steadfast in austerity, and those of them who wander seeking alms, who as suppliants desire some little thing—a gift given to them bears great fruit.

**13.24.59**  The rule of great fruit in giving you have now heard, O bull of the Bhāratas; now hear that by which men go to hell, and likewise to heaven.

**13.24.60**  Save for the sake of one's teacher or to save a life, O Yudhiṣṭhira, those who utter falsehood—they indeed are bound for hell.

**13.24.61**  Those who carry off the wives of others, who lay hands upon the wives of others, and who procure the wives of others—they indeed are bound for hell.

**13.24.62**  Those who seize away the goods of others, who destroy the goods of others, and who are informers against others—they indeed are bound for hell.

**13.24.63**  The men who are destroyers of watering-sheds, of assembly halls, of bridges and causeways, and of houses, O Bhārata—they are bound for hell.

**13.24.64**  Those men who deceive a helpless woman, a child, an old person, one in fear, or one given to austerity — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

**13.24.65**  Those who cut off a man's livelihood, his home, his wife, his friend, or his very hope, O Bhārata — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

**13.24.66**  Informers, breakers of alliances, those who live by another's labor, and the ungrateful toward their friends — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

**13.24.67**  Heretics, defilers, those who violate covenants, and those who have fallen back from their vows — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

**13.24.68**  Those who, by sowing discord, draw away one who has placed his hope in them, who has served them, given his devotion, and spent his toil for them — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

**13.24.69**  Those who eat before their wives, their servants, and their guests have eaten, and who have let the worship of the fathers and the gods lapse — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

**13.24.70**  Sellers of the Vedas, defilers of the Vedas, and those who commit the Vedas to writing — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

**13.24.71**  Those men who stand outside the four stages of life, outside the revealed scripture, and who live by forbidden acts — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

**13.24.72**  Dealers in hair, O king, dealers in poison, and dealers in milk — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

**13.24.73**  Those who, O Yudhiṣṭhira, slip in to obstruct the affairs of brāhmaṇas, of cattle, and of maidens — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

**13.24.74**  Sellers of weapons, O Yudhiṣṭhira, and the makers of barbed darts and of bows — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

**13.24.75**  Those who block the road with spikes, with stakes, or with pits, O bull of the Bhāratas — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

**13.24.76**  Those who abandon their teachers, their servants, and their devoted dependents when these are helpless, O bull of the Bhāratas — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

**13.24.77**  Those who break in beasts before their time, who pierce their noses, and who keep cattle in bondage — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

**13.24.78**  Those who fail to protect, who gain their wealth by fraud, who are intent on exacting the sixth-part tribute, and who, though able, give nothing — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

**13.24.79**  Those who, once their purpose is served, abandon the patient, the self-controlled, and the wise who have long dwelt with them — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

**13.24.80**  Those men who eat first, without first giving to the young, the old, and the servants — they, indeed, are bound for hell.

**13.24.81**  These the ancient seers beheld and declared to be bound for hell. Now I shall tell you, O bull of the Bhāratas, of those who share in the world of heaven.

**13.24.82**  In all undertakings that begin with rites to the gods, O Bhārata, an affront committed against a brāhmaṇa destroys one's sons and all one's cattle entirely.

**13.24.83**  Those men who, O Yudhiṣṭhira, follow the way of dharma through giving, through austerity, and through truth — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.84**  Those who, having gained sacred learning through service and austerity, O Bhārata, feel no craving to accept gifts — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.85**  Those for whose sake others are delivered from fear, from sin, from oppression, from poverty, and from the ravages of disease — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.86**  The forbearing and the steadfast, those ever roused to acts of dharma, and those devoted to auspicious conduct — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.87**  Those who have turned away from honey and flesh, from the wives of others, and from intoxicating drink — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.88**  The founders of hermitages, of families, of regions, and of cities, O Bhārata — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.89**  Those who give garments and ornaments, food, drink, and victuals, and who provide for whole households — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.90**  Those who have ceased from all harm, who endure all things, and who become a refuge for all — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.91**  Those who, masters of their senses, serve their mother and father, and bear affection toward their brothers — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.92**  Those who, though wealthy, strong, and in the bloom of youth, O Bhārata, yet remain steadfast and masters of their senses — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.93**  Those who remain affectionate even toward offenders, who are gentle, fond of their friends, and easy to win over — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.94**  Those men who feast thousands, who give to thousands, and who are the protectors of thousands — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.95**  The givers of gold and of cattle, O bull of the Bhāratas, and of carriages and draught-animals — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.96**  Those who give maidens in marriage, who give attendants and garments, O Yudhiṣṭhira — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.97**  Those who provide pleasure-grounds, resting-houses, gardens, wells, groves, and assembly-halls, and who build embankments — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.98**  Those who give dwellings, fields, and lodgings, O Bhārata, and whatever is asked of them — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.99**  Those men who, having themselves raised juices, seeds, and grain, O Yudhiṣṭhira, then give them away — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.100**  In whatever family they are born, men blessed with many sons and a span of a hundred years, full of compassion and having conquered their wrath — they are bound for heaven.

**13.24.101**  Thus has it been told, for the sake of the world beyond, regarding the rites to the gods and to the fathers, O Bhārata, and the dharma and adharma of giving, even as the ancient seers ordained them.

**13.25.1**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: This, O king, you ought to tell me truly, O Bhārata — by what act here, even without slaying, is the guilt of brahmin-murder incurred?

**13.25.2**  Bhīṣma said: That which I once asked of Vyāsa, having addressed him, O lord of kings, I shall now relate to you in full — listen here with single-minded attention.

**13.25.3**  You who are the fourth in descent from Vasiṣṭha — declare to me the truth, O sage: by what act here, even without slaying, is the guilt of brahmin-murder incurred?

**13.25.4**  Thus questioned, O great king, the son born of Parāśara's body, skilled in dharma, spoke without doubt and beyond all dispute.

**13.25.5**  He who himself summons a brāhmaṇa of meager livelihood to receive alms, and afterward says, 'There is nothing' — know that man to be a slayer of a brāhmaṇa.

**13.25.6**  The man of evil mind who robs of his livelihood a learned and impartial brāhmaṇa here, O Bhārata — know that man to be a slayer of a brāhmaṇa.

**13.25.7**  He who, O lord of the earth, raises an obstacle to the water sought by a herd of cattle tormented by thirst — know that man to be a slayer of a brāhmaṇa.

**13.25.8**  He who, in his ignorance, reviles the established sacred lore or the scripture rightly composed by the sages — know that man to be a slayer of a brāhmaṇa.

**13.25.9**  He who does not bestow his own daughter, endowed with beauty and grown to maturity, upon a worthy suitor — know that man to be a slayer of a brāhmaṇa.

**13.25.10**  The deluded man, devoted to unrighteousness, who falsely inflicts upon the twice-born a grief that pierces to the quick — know that man to be a slayer of a brāhmaṇa.

**13.25.11**  He who carries off the whole property of one bereft of sight, of a cripple, or of a simpleton — know that man to be a slayer of a brāhmaṇa.

**13.25.12**  He who in his folly sets loose fire upon a hermitage, a forest, a village, or a town — know that man to be a slayer of a brāhmaṇa.

**13.26.1**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: The sight of the sacred fords is a blessing, and bathing in them too, O bull of the Bhāratas; and hearing of them as well, O greatly wise one — I wish to hear of them truly.

**13.26.2**  Those holy fords that are upon the earth, O bull of the Bhāratas, you ought to tell me of them; I shall listen, intent and self-restrained, O lord.

**13.26.3**  Bhīṣma said: This lineage of the sacred fords, declared by Aṅgiras, O one of great splendor, you ought to hear — blessings be upon you; you shall attain the highest dharma.

**13.26.4**  Approaching the brāhmaṇa, the great sage Aṅgiras, who had gone to the grove of austerities, Gautama of rigid vows questioned him, O hero.

**13.26.5**  I have, O blessed one, a certain doubt concerning the dharma of the sacred fords. All of it I wish to hear; declare it to me, O great sage.

**13.26.6**  What fruit accrues from touching the waters at those fords, O sage, in the life beyond, O greatly wise one? Tell it to me just as it is.

**13.26.7**  Aṅgiras said: He who for seven days plunges into the Candrabhāgā and the wave-garlanded Vitastā, fasting and free of all sense of possession, becomes like unto a sage.

**13.26.8**  The rivers that, in the region of Kāśmīra, fall into the great river — coming to those streams of the Sindhu, the man of virtuous conduct attains heaven.

**13.26.9**  Having plunged into Puṣkara, Prabhāsa, Naimiṣa, the ocean-waters, the Devikā, the Indramārga, and the Svarṇabindu, a man is awakened set upon a celestial chariot, hymned by the apsarases.

**13.26.10**  Having stirred the waters of Hiraṇyabindu and, self-controlled, reverently saluted the Kuśeśaya, he attains godhead, and his sin is washed away.

**13.26.11**  Reaching the Indratoyā near Gandhamādana, and the Karatoyā among the Kuraṅgas, the man who has fasted three nights and plunges in, restrained and pure, gains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice.

**13.26.12**  Having bathed at the Gate of the Gaṅgā, at Kuśāvarta, at Bilvaka, at Mount Nemi, and at Kanakhala, a man, his sins shaken off, goes to heaven.

**13.26.13**  Touching the waters at the lake Apāṃ Hrada, a chaste man who has conquered wrath, true to his word and harmless to all, gains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice.

**13.26.14**  Where the Bhāgīrathī Gaṅgā turns toward the northern quarter, at the abode of Maheśvara, the man who is consecrated there, fasting for a whole month, beholds the gods themselves.

**13.26.15**  At Saptagaṅga, at Trigaṅga, and at the Indramārga, the man who offers libations to the fathers gains the nectar of immortality to taste, when he is born again.

**13.26.16**  Touching the waters at Mahāśrama, the pure man devoted to the fire-offering, fasting for a whole month, attains perfection in that month.

**13.26.17**  Touching the waters at the Great Lake on Bhṛgutuṅga, the man free of greed, having fasted three nights, is released from the guilt of brahmin-murder.

**13.26.18**  Touching the waters at the Kanyākūpa and making his offering of water in the Balākā, a man wins renown among the gods and shines forth in glory.

**13.26.19**  Touching the waters at Deśakāla and likewise in the lake Sundarikā, a man gains from the Aśvins beauty and brilliance of form when he passes to the other world.

**13.26.20**  Touching the waters of the Mahāgaṅgā, and likewise at Kṛttikā and Aṅgāraka, a man who fasts for a single fortnight, made spotless, attains heaven.

**13.26.21**  Touching the waters at Vaimānika and likewise at the hermitage of Kiṅkiṇīkā, in the celestial dwelling of the apsarases, a man is honored and roams there at will.

**13.26.22**  Reaching the hermitage of Kālikā and making his offering of water in the Vipāśā, a chaste man who has conquered wrath is freed, after three nights, from the round of rebirth.

**13.26.23**  He who bathes at the hermitage of the Kṛttikās and offers libations to the fathers, having gladdened Mahādeva, made spotless, attains heaven.

**13.26.24**  Touching the waters at Mahāpura, a man who has fasted three nights casts off all fear of moving creatures, of unmoving things, and of men.

**13.26.25**  Having bathed in the Devadāru grove, his sins shaken off, and made his offering of water, the pure man who has fasted seven nights attains the world of the gods.

**13.26.26**  At Kauśanta, at Kuśastamba, at Droṇaśarmapada, and bathing at Āpaḥprapatana, a man is waited upon by the throngs of apsarases.

**13.26.27**  Plunging, while fasting, into Citrakūṭa, into Janasthāna, and into the waters of the Mandākinī, a man attains the royal fortune of a king.

**13.26.28**  Having gone to the hermitage of Śyāmā, and dwelling there and bathing, after spending three sets of three nights in succession, a man may dwell in the city of the gandharvas.

**13.26.29**  Touching the waters at Ramaṇyā and likewise at Gandhatārikā, a man who fasts for a whole month gains the power of vanishing from sight.

**13.26.30**  Reaching the Gate of the Kauśikī, a man free of greed who feeds on air alone ascends to heaven after twenty-one nights.

**13.26.31**  He who bathes in the Mataṅga pool attains perfection in a single night; for he passes through the eternal, supportless, blinding darkness.

**13.26.32**  He who, with senses subdued, touches the waters at Naimiṣa and at the Svargatīrtha, and offers libations there for a month, wins the fruit of the Puruṣamedha sacrifice.

**13.26.33**  Touching the waters of the Gaṅgā-pool and likewise of the Utpalāvana, and offering libations there for a month, a man obtains the merit of the Horse Sacrifice.

**13.26.34**  At the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā, and upon Mount Kālaṃjara, touching the Ṣaṣṭi pool—no other gift surpasses what is gained there.

**13.26.35**  Ten thousand sacred fords, and thirty million others besides, all gather at Prayāga in the month of Māgha, O bull of the Bhāratas.

**13.26.36**  He who, restrained and firm in his vows, bathes at Prayāga during the month of Māgha, O best of the Bhāratas, becomes spotless and attains heaven.

**13.26.37**  Touching the waters at the Marudgaṇa, pure at the hermitage of the Fathers, and at the ford of Vaivasvata, a man himself becomes as holy as a sacred ford.

**13.26.38**  So too, having gone to Brahmaśiras and offered libations in the Bhāgīrathī, fasting for one month, a man attains the world of Soma.

**13.26.39**  A man who bathes at Kapotaka and offers libations at Aṣṭāvakra, fasting for twelve days, wins the fruit of the Naramedha sacrifice.

**13.26.40**  By visiting Muñjapṛṣṭha and Gayā, Nirṛti and the mountain of the gods, and thirdly the Krauñcapādī, even the slaying of a brāhmaṇa is purged away.

**13.26.41**  Touching the waters at Kalaśī, and often at the Vedī, bathing at the city of Agni and offering libations at Viśālā, and touching the waters of the Devahrada, a man shines forth, having become one with Brahman.

**13.26.42**  Having resorted to Purāpavartana, the Nandā, and the Mahānandā, the self-controlled and harmless man is waited upon by the apsarases in the grove of Nandana.

**13.26.43**  He who, well-composed, goes there at the conjunction of Urvaśī and the Kṛttikā stars, and bathes in due form in the Lauhitya, wins the fruit of the Puṇḍarīka sacrifice.

**13.26.44**  Touching the waters of the Rāma-pool and offering libations at Viśālā, fasting for twelve days, a man is wholly freed from defilement.
