**13.81.22**  Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, those auspicious cows, tender with compassion, having taken counsel together, all spoke to Śrī, O lord of men.

**13.81.23**  You must surely be honoured by us, O glorious one; dwell within our dung and urine, for this is holy in us, O auspicious one.

**13.81.24**  Śrī said: Happily have you shown me grace, full of favour. So be it; blessings upon you. I am honoured, O bestowers of happiness.

**13.81.25**  Bhīṣma said: Having thus made her compact with the cows, O Bhārata, Śrī vanished then and there, even as they looked on.

**13.81.26**  Thus, my son, has the greatness of cow-dung been recounted to you; and now hear further of the greatness of the cows as I tell it.

**13.82.1**  Bhīṣma said: Those who bestow cows, and those who eat only what remains after the oblation, possess the merit of sacrificial rites and sacrifices perpetually, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

**13.82.2**  Without curds and clarified butter no sacrifice can proceed; therein lies the sacrificial essence of a sacrifice, and herein its very root is seen.

**13.82.3**  Of all gifts whatsoever, the gift of cows is extolled; the cows are most excellent and pure, and this is the supreme means of purification.

**13.82.4**  For prosperity let one serve them, and for peace as well — those whose milk, curds, and clarified butter release one from all sin.

**13.82.5**  The cows are declared the supreme splendour in this world and the next; there is nothing more purifying than cows, O bull among men.

**13.82.6**  On this too they recount an ancient tale — a colloquy between the Grandsire and Indra, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

**13.82.7**  When the daityas had been vanquished and Śakra was lord of the three worlds, all creatures throve, devoted to truth and dharma.

**13.82.8**  Then the sages with the gandharvas, the kiṃnaras, serpents, and rākṣasas, the gods, asuras, and suparṇas, and the lords of creatures — once upon a time, O Kauravya, they waited upon the Grandsire.

**13.82.9**  Nārada and Parvata, Viśvāvasu, Hāhā, and Hūhū, singing in divine melodies, waited upon that Lord.

**13.82.10**  There the wind wafted celestial flowers, and the seasons too brought fragrant blossoms each in turn.

**13.82.11**  In that gathering of the gods, that assembly of all beings, resounding with celestial instruments and thronged with divine women and cāraṇas, Indra, having saluted and bowed to the Lord of gods, asked him:

**13.82.12**  O blessed Grandsire, wherefore is the world of cows set above that of the gods, the lords of the worlds? This I wish to know.

**13.82.13**  What austerity or chastity, O Lord, was performed by the cows here, that they dwell in joy, free of passion, above the gods?

**13.82.14**  Then Brahmā said to Śakra, the slayer of Bala: The cows have ever been slighted by you, O slayer of Bala.

**13.82.15**  Because of this you do not know the greatness of these cows; hear it, O lord. Learn the supreme power and majesty of cattle, O bull among the gods.

**13.82.16**  Cows are declared to be a limb of sacrifice, indeed the very sacrifice itself, O Vāsava; and without them no sacrifice could ever proceed at all.

**13.82.17**  They sustain living beings with their milk and with the oblation; and their offspring too apply themselves to the labor of the plow.

**13.82.18**  They bring forth grains and seeds of many kinds; from these the sacrifices proceed, and the offerings to the gods and to the ancestors in every form.

**13.82.19**  Milk, curds, and clarified butter—holy are these cows, O lord of the gods; and tormented by hunger and thirst they bear burdens of every kind.

**13.82.20**  By their toil they sustain the sages here and all living beings as well, O Vāsava; drawing their loads with guileless hearts, and by their meritorious deeds, they dwell forever above even us.

**13.82.21**  This, O Śakra, is the reason I have now told you why the abode of cattle lies above even the gods, O lord of a hundred sacrifices.

**13.82.22**  For these cows are both granted by boon and themselves bestowers of boons, O Vāsava—daughters of Surabhī, doers of holy deeds, purifying, and marked with auspicious signs.

**13.82.23**  And for what reason the daughters of Surabhī attained the rank of cattle, O best of the gods—hear that too in full as I tell it, O slayer of Bala.

**13.82.24**  Of old, in the age of the gods, dear one, when the great-souled lords of the Daityas were ruling the three worlds, Viṣṇu entered the womb.

**13.82.25**  While Aditi was practicing fearsome and most difficult austerity, standing ever upon a single foot for the sake of a son, O best of the immortals—

**13.82.26**  and seeing that great goddess engaged in mighty austerity, the goddess who was Dakṣa's daughter, Surabhī by name,

**13.82.27**  in gladness, devoted to dharma, performed a fearsome austerity upon the lovely peak of Kailāsa, frequented by gods and Gandharvas.

**13.82.28**  Established in supreme yoga, she stood upon a single foot for ten thousand years and ten hundred years besides.

**13.82.29**  Scorched by the heat of her austerity, the gods together with the sages and the great serpents went there with me and waited upon that auspicious one.

**13.82.30**  Then I spoke there to that goddess girt with austerity: 'For what purpose, O goddess, do you practice this fearsome austerity, O blameless one?'

**13.82.31**  'I am pleased with you, O fortunate one, by this austerity, O lovely one; choose a boon, O goddess, for I am ready to grant it'—so said Brahmā, O Purandara.

**13.82.32**  Surabhī said: By a boon, O blessed one, my purpose is fulfilled, O grandsire of the worlds; this very thing is my boon today—that you are pleased with me, O sinless one.

**13.82.33**  Brahmā said: To the goddess Surabhī, who spoke thus, O lord of the thirty gods, I made reply—learn now what I said, O king of the gods, O consort of Śacī.

**13.82.34**  'By your freedom from greed and desire, O goddess, and by your holy austerity, I am well pleased; therefore I grant you the boon of immortality.'

**13.82.35**  'Above even the three worlds shall you dwell, and by my favor that place shall become renowned as the World of Cattle, Goloka.'

**13.82.36**  'And your sons, doing their work among men, and all your daughters too shall dwell there, O fortunate one.'

**13.82.37**  'Whatever enjoyments, divine and human, you conceive in your mind, and whatever happiness of heaven there is, O goddess—all that shall be yours, O auspicious one.'

**13.82.38**  Her worlds, O thousand-eyed one, are furnished with every desire; there death does not advance, nor old age, nor fire; no misery and nothing inauspicious is found there, O Vāsava.

**13.82.39**  There are divine forests there, and divine dwellings, and well-appointed celestial chariots that go where one wishes, O Vāsava.

**13.82.40**  By holy vows of many kinds, by frequenting sacred fords, by great austerity, and by good works, Goloka can be attained, O lotus-eyed one.

**13.82.41**  All this I have declared to you, O Śakra, who asked of it; you must show no contempt for cattle, O slayer of foes.

**13.82.42**  Bhīṣma said: Having heard this, the thousand-eyed one ever honored cattle and always held them in high esteem, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

**13.82.43**  All this I have told you, purifying and of great splendor; the supremely holy and highest greatness of cattle has been proclaimed, O tiger among men—a thing that destroys all sins.

**13.82.44**  Whoever, with collected mind, recounts this always to the brāhmaṇas—at the offerings to gods and ancestors, at sacrifices, and at the rites for the fathers—an imperishable reward fulfilling every desire awaits his ancestors.

**13.82.45**  The man devoted to cattle obtains whatever he desires; and women too who are devoted to cattle attain their wishes.

**13.82.46**  He who longs for a son obtains a son; the maiden gains a husband; he who seeks wealth gains riches; he who seeks dharma attains dharma.

**13.82.47**  He who seeks knowledge attains knowledge; he who seeks happiness attains happiness; for him who is devoted to cattle nothing is hard to win, O descendant of Bharata.

**13.83.1**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: The grandsire has declared this—that the gift of cattle is unsurpassed, and especially so for kings who keep their gaze upon dharma.

**13.83.2**  For kingship is unceasing sorrow, and the orders of life are very hard to know; with a great retinue comes grief, hard to bear for those whose souls are unperfected; and most often no auspicious destiny is found for kings.

**13.83.3**  They are surely purified herein who bestow the gift of land; and the duties you have already related to me before, O joy of the Kurus.

**13.83.4**  Just so the gift of cattle was extolled by you, as it was shown of old by King Nṛga and by the sage Nāciketa.

**13.83.5**  And in the Vedas and the Upaniṣads, in all rites the sacrificial fee is enjoined, and in all sacrifices: land, cattle, and gold.

**13.83.6**  Therein the supreme scriptural teaching is that gold is the fitting fee; this I wish to hear, O grandsire, exactly as it is.

**13.83.7**  What is gold, how did it come to be, in what age, and of what nature? What is its gift, what is its fruit, and why is it called the highest?

**13.83.8**  Why do the wise honor the gift of gold, and why is it commended as the fee in the rites of sacrifice?

**13.83.9**  And why is gold the most purifying—above land and above cattle—and supreme as a sacrificial fee? Tell me this, O grandsire.

**13.83.10**  Bhīṣma said: Listen attentively, O king, to the full account of its many causes—the origin of gold and what I myself have experienced.

**13.83.11**  My father, the greatly resplendent Śaṃtanu, had passed away; wishing to perform his śrāddha rite, I came to the Gate of Gaṅgā.

**13.83.12**  Having arrived there, my son, I began the śrāddha rite for my father, and my mother Jāhnavī then lent me her aid.

**13.83.13**  Then, having seated before me many sages perfected in austerity, I began the rites, beginning with the offering of water.

**13.83.14**  Having completed that preliminary rite as prescribed, with collected mind I set about offering the funeral oblation rightly, in due order.

**13.83.15**  Then, breaking through that arrangement of darbha grass, an arm rose up, adorned with a lovely armlet and with pendent ornaments, O lord of peoples.

**13.83.16**  Seeing it risen up, I fell into utter astonishment, thinking, 'It is my father in person, come to receive the offering,' O bull of the Bhāratas.

**13.83.17**  Then my reason returned to me, and reflecting upon the scriptures I thought: 'This rule is not enjoined in the Vedas—that the offering be placed into a hand'; and this conviction arose in me, O lord.

**13.83.18**  'A man's fathers, being hidden from sight, do not anywhere receive it directly; it is thus enjoined that the rice-ball be offered upon the kuśa grass.'

**13.83.19**  Then, disregarding the appearance of my father's hand, mindful of the subtle rule on the authority of scripture, O king—

**13.83.20**  I offered all of it upon the darbha grass, O bull of the Bhāratas, following the path of scripture; know this, O bull among men.

**13.83.21**  Thereupon that arm of my father vanished, O ruler of men; and then the fathers showed themselves to me at the close of a dream.

**13.83.22**  And being well pleased they said to me: 'We are pleased, O bull of the Bhāratas, by this discernment of yours, in that you are not led astray from dharma.'

**13.83.23**  'For by making scripture your authority herein, O king, you have honored—as the great sages do—the self, dharma, sacred learning, the Vedas, and the fathers.'

**13.83.24**  'The grandsire Brahmā himself, the teachers, and Prajāpati have been upheld as authority, and the established order has not been shaken.'

**13.83.25**  'This rite has been rightly begun by you today, O bull of the Bhāratas; but for the sake of land and cattle, let gold be given.'

**13.83.26**  'Thus shall we, and dharma, and all our forefathers be purified; for that is the highest purification.'

**13.83.27**  'Those who bestow gold carry across ten ancestors before them and ten descendants after'—thus did my fathers speak to me.

**13.83.28**  Then, awakened in astonishment, O king, O lord of peoples, I set my mind upon the gift of gold, O best of the Bhāratas.

**13.83.29**  Hear too this ancient tale, O king, concerning the son of Jamadagni, O mighty one—a tale that bestows fortune and long life.

**13.83.30**  By Rāma, the son of Jamadagni, filled with fierce wrath, the earth was made bereft of warriors thrice seven times of old.

**13.83.31**  Then, having conquered the whole earth, the lotus-eyed hero Rāma performed a sacrifice honored by brāhmaṇas and kṣatriyas alike.

**13.83.32**  A horse-sacrifice, O great king, furnished with every desired thing, purifying to all beings and enhancing splendor and luster.

**13.83.33**  Though already free of sin, that resplendent son of Jamadagni did not, even by the fruit of that sacrifice, reach lightness in his own esteem.

**13.83.34**  Having worshipped with that most excellent, fee-laden sacrifice, the great-souled scion of Bhṛgu questioned the sages and the gods, who were learned in scripture.

**13.83.35**  'Let it be told, O greatly fortunate ones, what is the supreme purification for men engaged in dread and violent deeds'—so spoke he in whom compassion had arisen.

**13.83.36**  Vasiṣṭha said: They who give gold bestow the very gods; for Agni is all the gods, and gold is of that same essence.

**13.83.37**  Therefore by him who gives gold all the gods are given, O tiger among men; for they know of nothing higher than this.

**13.83.38**  And learn yet further the greatness of gold as I tell it, O sage among brāhmaṇas, O best of all who bear weapons.

**13.83.39**  This I heard of old in the ancient lore, O joy of the Bhṛgus, as the Prajāpati Manu, the self-existent, related it.

**13.83.40**  It concerns the trident-bearing lord, the great-souled Rudra, upon the most excellent mountain Himavat, O upholder of the Bhṛgu line.

**13.83.41**  When the wedding of the goddess Rudrāṇī had been accomplished, O joy of the Bhṛgus, and the great-souled lord came together with the goddess, then all the gods, deeply agitated, approached the lord.

**13.83.42**  Having propitiated with bowed heads the seated Mahādeva and the boon-granting goddess Umā, they all spoke to Rudra, O upholder of the Bhṛgus.

**13.83.43**  'This union of yours with the goddess, O sinless god—of you, an ascetic, with her, an ascetic; of you, supremely fiery, with her, the fiery one—O god, your fire is unfailing, and so too is this goddess Umā.'

**13.83.44**  'The offspring of you two, O god, will be mighty, O lord; surely it will leave nothing remaining in the three worlds.'

**13.83.45**  'Therefore to these gods who bow before you, O broad-eyed one, grant a boon, O lord of the worlds, out of desire for the welfare of the three worlds: for the sake of progeny, restrain your blazing, supreme seed.'

**13.83.46**  As they spoke thus, the blessed lord whose banner bears the bull replied to those gods, O sage among brāhmaṇas: 'So be it.'

**13.83.47**  Having said this, the bull-borne lord drew his seed upward; and from that time forth he became one whose seed flows upward.

**13.83.48**  Then Rudrāṇī, enraged that the begetting of offspring had thus been cut off, spoke to the gods, in her womanly nature, harsh words.

**13.83.49**  "Because my husband, who longed for offspring, has been turned from his purpose, therefore all of you gods shall be without progeny.

**13.83.50**  Since the cutting off of my offspring has been wrought by you this day, therefore, O sky-rangers, none of you shall have progeny."

**13.83.51**  But Pāvaka was not present there at the time of the curse, O scion of Bhṛgu; and so, by the goddess's curse, the gods became without offspring.

**13.83.52**  Rudra, meanwhile, held back that incomparable seed; yet something of it spilled forth from him and fell there upon the earth.

**13.83.53**  That fell then into the fire and grew, a thing of wondrous likeness; radiance mingled with radiance, and so came to share a single source.

**13.83.54**  At this very time the gods, with Śakra at their head, were grievously tormented by an asura named Tāraka.

**13.83.55**  The Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Maruts, and the two Aśvins, and all the Sādhyas, were terrified by the prowess of that descendant of Diti.

**13.83.56**  For the abodes of the gods, their celestial chariots and cities, and the hermitages of the sages too were seized by the asuras.

**13.83.57**  All of them, downcast in heart—the gods and the sages alike—went for refuge to the god Brahmā, the undecaying lord.

**13.84.1**  The gods said: "An asura named Tāraka, to whom you granted a boon, O Lord, afflicts the gods and the sages; let his slaying be ordained.

**13.84.2**  From him terror has arisen for us, O Grandsire; save us, O god, for we have no other refuge."

**13.84.3**  Brahmā said: "I am equal toward all beings, and I take no pleasure in unrighteousness; let Tāraka, the oppressor of the hosts of gods and sages, be slain swiftly.

**13.84.4**  The Vedas and the laws of dharma must not go to ruin, O best of gods; this matter has already been provided for by me—let your fever pass away.

**13.84.5**  The gods said: "By the granting of your boon, O blessed one, the son of Diti is proud of his strength; he cannot be slain by the gods—how then shall he be brought to an end?

**13.84.6**  For he obtained from you, O Grandsire, the boon: 'May I be slayable neither by the gods, nor by the asuras, nor by the rākṣasas.'

**13.84.7**  And the gods were cursed by Rudrāṇī, when the cutting off of her offspring was wrought of old: 'You shall have no progeny,' O lord of all the worlds."

**13.84.8**  Brahmā said: "Hutāśana was not present there at the time of the curse, O best of gods; he shall beget offspring for the slaying of the foes of the Thirty.

**13.84.9**  That offspring, surpassing all—gods, dānavas, and rākṣasas, men and gandharvas, nāgas and birds—

**13.84.10**  with a weapon of unfailing aim, with his spear, shall slay him from whom your terror has arisen, and whatever other foes of the gods there be.

**13.84.11**  For the eternal Resolve is named Kāma; and the seed of Rudra spilled forth and fell into the fire.

**13.84.12**  That radiance, become a mighty being, like a second Fire, Agni shall bring to birth in the Gaṅgā for the slaying of the foes of the gods.

**13.84.13**  He, the eater of oblations, did not incur that curse, for he had vanished at the time; therefore, O gods, the son of Pāvaka shall arise as the remover of your fear.

**13.84.14**  Let the Burning One be sought out, then, and appointed this day to the task; the means of Tāraka's slaying has been told you by me, O sinless ones.

**13.84.15**  For curses do not prevail over the radiance of the radiant; lesser powers, when they meet a greater power, become powerless indeed.

**13.84.16**  Kāma, who is delight in resolve, the most ancient Fire, could slay even the unslayable, the granters of boons, and the ascetics.

**13.84.17**  He is the lord of the world, indefinable, all-pervading, the source of all being, the one who dwells in the hearts of all creatures, the eldest, a lord mightier even than Rudra.

**13.84.18**  Let him be sought out swiftly, Hutāśana, that mass of radiance; that god shall fulfill the desire that lies in your hearts."

**13.84.19**  Having heard this speech of the great-souled one, the gods then went forth, their resolve made firm, searching for Vibhāvasu.

**13.84.20**  Then the sages, together with the gods, searched through the three worlds, longing for the sight of Vahni, all with their minds fixed upon him.

**13.84.21**  Endowed with the highest austerity, glorious, renowned throughout the worlds, the perfected ones all ranged across the worlds, O scion of Bhṛgu; yet they did not find Hutāśana, who had vanished, withdrawn into himself.

**13.84.22**  Then to those who were stricken with terror and yearning for the sight of Agni, a frog, a water-dweller, weary in spirit and scorched by the radiance of Agni, rose up from the depths of the nether region and spoke to the gods:

**13.84.23**  "In the depths of the nether region, O gods, dwells Agni, O lord; I have come here driven by the burning that springs from Pāvaka.

**13.84.24**  He, the blessed Havyavāhana, lies asleep in the water, O gods; mingling the waters with his radiance, he has scorched us by it.

**13.84.25**  If the sight of him, of Vibhāvasu, is your wish, O gods, go to him there, if you have business with Vahni.

**13.84.26**  Let it be gone to; as for us, we shall make our escape from the fear of Agni, O gods." Having said only this, the frog hastily entered the water.

**13.84.27**  But Hutāśana perceived the frog's treachery, and, coming upon him, cursed him: "You shall know no flavors."

**13.84.28**  Having bound the frog with that curse, the all-pervading Pāvaka went elsewhere to dwell, and did not show himself to the gods.

**13.84.29**  But the gods bestowed a favor upon the frogs, O scion of Bhṛgu; hear it all from me as I tell it, O mighty-armed one.

**13.84.30**  The gods said: "Though tongueless and cut off from the knowledge of flavors by Agni's curse, you shall utter speech of many kinds.

**13.84.31**  Even when you dwell in holes, foodless and senseless, even when lifeless and dried up, the earth shall sustain you; and you shall roam abroad even in the darkness-shrouded night."

**13.84.32**  Having spoken thus to them, the gods then ranged once more over this earth for the sake of the Burning One, yet they did not find Hutāśana.

**13.84.33**  Then a certain elephant, like unto the elephant of the king of the gods, said this to them, O scion of Bhṛgu: "Agni dwells within the aśvattha tree."

**13.84.34**  The Burning One, overcome with wrath, cursed all the elephants: "Your tongue shall be turned backward," O scion of Bhṛgu.

**13.84.35**  Having said this, Agni, betrayed by the elephant, came forth from the aśvattha; then Vahni entered the womb of the śamī tree, desiring to sleep.

**13.84.36**  Hear now the favor that the gods, whose valor is truth, bestowed, well pleased, upon the elephants, O lord, O best of Bhṛgu's line.

**13.84.37**  The gods said: "Even with your backward-turned tongue you shall take all your food, and you shall utter a voice aloud, with unarticulated sound." Having said this, the dwellers of heaven once more went in pursuit of Agni.

**13.84.38**  And Agni, having come forth from the aśvattha, had then entered the womb of the śamī; betrayed by a parrot, O brāhmaṇa, the gods rushed upon him.

**13.84.39**  But Agni cursed the parrot: "You shall be bereft of speech"; and the eater of oblations then turned that one's tongue backward too.

**13.84.40**  But the gods, seeing the Burning One, spoke to the parrot, filled with compassion: "You shall not, O bird, be wholly deprived of speech.

**13.84.41**  Though your tongue is turned backward, your speech shall be lovely—soft, indistinct, and wondrous, like that of a grown person who yet speaks as a child."

**13.84.42**  Having said this, and beholding Vahni within the womb of the śamī, the gods made that very tree his holy abode for all sacred rites.

**13.84.43**  From that time forth Agni is found within the wombs of the śamī, and men too followed this means for the kindling of fire.

**13.84.44**  Those waters in the nether region that were mingled with Citrabhānu, O Bhārgava, release their heat through the springs of the mountains, scorched as they were by the radiance of Pāvaka, who lay couched within them.

**13.84.45**  Then Agni, seeing the gods, became troubled, and Pāvaka asked them thus: "What is the purpose of your coming?"

**13.84.46**  All the wise ones and those supreme sages said to him: "We would appoint you to a task; you ought to perform it; and when it is done, a great benefit shall accrue to you as well."

**13.84.47**  Agni said: "Tell me what your task is; I shall do it all, O gods; for I am yours to command—let there be no hesitation in you over this."

**13.84.48**  The gods said: "An asura named Tāraka, made proud by Brahmā's boon, oppresses us by his might; let his slaying be ordained.

**13.84.49**  Save these hosts of gods, dear one, and the hosts of the Prajāpatis, and the greatly blessed sages too, O Pāvaka.

**13.84.50**  Beget an offspring endowed with radiance, a great hero, O lord, who shall destroy the fear we have from that asura, O Havyavāhana.

**13.84.51**  For us, cursed by the great Goddess, there is no other refuge than your valor; therefore deliver us from this peril."

**13.84.52**  Thus addressed, the blessed bearer of oblations to gods and ancestors said "So be it," and that one hard to assail went then toward the Gaṅgā, the daughter of Bhagīratha.

**13.84.53**  He mingled with her, and an embryo formed within her then; and that embryo grew, as the fire whose path is black grows in dry brushwood.

**13.84.54**  By the radiance of that embryo Gaṅgā, her senses overwhelmed, came to a fierce burning, and she could not endure it.

**13.84.55**  When the embryo, charged with radiance, had been placed by the Burning One in Gaṅgā, a certain asura let loose a terrible roar.

**13.84.56**  At that vast roar, fallen upon her unawares, Gaṅgā—her eyes wide with terror and rolling, her gaze swimming, her senses gone—was unable to hold the embryo within herself.

**13.84.57**  Then Jāhnavī, her limbs encompassed by radiance and trembling, overborne by the embryo, spoke these words, O brāhmaṇa: "I am not able, O blessed one, to bear up this radiance of yours.

**13.84.58**  I am bewildered, and by it I have been made most ill at ease; I am overwhelmed, O blessed one, and my own radiance is lost, O sinless one.

**13.84.59**  I am not able to hold this embryo, O best of those that burn; I shall release it out of distress, and in no wise out of any wish to do so.

**13.84.60**  There is no touch of inclination in my heart, O god Vibhāvasu; for a bond formed in time of distress, even the subtlest, is no true bond, O greatly resplendent one.

**13.84.61**  Whatever here is endowed with merit, or otherwise, O Hutāśana, I deem that to rest in you alone, and the merit and demerit of it to be wholly yours."

**13.84.62**  Then Vahni said to her: "Let it be borne, let this embryo be borne, charged with my radiance, the source of great and meritorious fruit.

**13.84.63**  For you are able to bear and to sustain the whole earth; there is nothing beyond your power, save the holding of my seed."

**13.84.64**  Though held back by Vahni and by the gods, that best of rivers then cast off the embryo upon Meru, the noblest of mountains.

**13.84.65**  Though capable of bearing it, overborne by the radiance of Rudra, she was then unable to sustain that embryo by her strength.

**13.84.66**  Having cast off in distress that embryo, bright as the blazing Vaiśvānara, Agni then showed himself to Gaṅgā, O scion of Bhṛgu, and asked that best of rivers: "Is the embryo a happy birth?

**13.84.67**  Of what hue, O goddess, and of what form does it appear? And with what radiance is it endowed? Tell me all of this."

**13.84.68**  Gaṅgā said: "That embryo is of golden form, in radiance like to yourself, O Anala—of fair gold, spotless, blazing; and it lit up the mountain.

**13.84.69**  It is cool as pools intermingled with lotuses and blue water-lilies; and its fragrance is equal to that of the kadamba blossoms, O best of those that burn.

**13.84.70**  By the radiance of that embryo, as by the rays of the sun-maker, whatever substance was touched, upon the earth or in the mountains, all of that was seen on every side to have turned to gold.

**13.84.71**  He coursed over the mountains, the rivers, and the springs, and with his radiance he set ablaze the three worlds, all that moves and all that is still.

**13.84.72**  Of such a form, O bearer of oblations, is that lordly son of yours, equal to the sun and to Vaiśvānara, and in his loveliness like a second moon. Having spoken thus, the goddess vanished then and there.

**13.84.73**  And the radiant Pāvaka too, having accomplished the purpose of the dwellers in heaven, then went to the region he desired, O delight of Bhṛgu's line.

**13.84.74**  For these qualities of his deeds, the name of Agni is sung throughout the world as Hiraṇyaretas, 'he whose seed is gold,' by the seers and by the wise; and the goddess Earth from that time was renowned as Vasumatī, 'she who holds the treasure.'

**13.84.75**  But that embryo of mighty splendor, son of Gaṅgā and offspring of Pāvaka, having reached the celestial thicket of reeds, grew up, a wonder to behold.

**13.84.76**  The Kṛttikās beheld him, his luster like the newly risen sun, and conceiving tenderness for that child, they nourished him with the flowing of their breasts.

**13.84.77**  Thereupon that one of supreme radiance attained the name Kārttikeya; from his having been let fall he gained the name Skanda, and from his dwelling in a hidden place he became Guha.

**13.84.78**  Thus did gold come to be, the offspring of Jātavedas; and of it the Jāmbūnada gold is the finest, an ornament even of the gods.

**13.84.79**  And from that time onward this gold has been called jātarūpa, 'born of his form'; for the gold itself is the lord Agni, the master, the Lord of Creatures.

**13.84.80**  For gold is the purest of all pure things, O best of the twice-born; and jātarūpa is declared to have the very nature of Agni and Soma.

**13.84.81**  It is the most excellent of jewels, the most excellent of ornaments, the purest of pure things, and the most auspicious of all that is auspicious.

**13.85.1**  Vasiṣṭha said: Moreover, O Rāma, of old I heard this revelation of Brahman, what befell concerning the Grandsire Brahmā, the Supreme Self.

**13.85.2**  My son, of the great god who bore the form of Varuṇa, in the sovereign domain of Varuṇa, O Rāma, in the lordship of Rudra the Ruler, O mighty one—

**13.85.3**  there came all the sages, and the gods with Agni at their head, and all the members of the sacrifice, and the Vaṣaṭ-call itself embodied.

**13.85.4**  And the Sāman chants embodied, and the Yajus verses by the thousand, and the Ṛgveda came there, adorned with its word-order and its sequence of recitation.

**13.85.5**  The marks of grammar, the accents, the chant-syllables, the etymology, and the divisions of tone, and the syllable Oṃ dwelt there, and likewise restraint and free recitation as his two eyes.

**13.85.6**  The Vedas with their Upaniṣads, the sacred lore, and the Sāvitrī as well—the past, the present, and the future the lord Śiva upheld, himself then offering the self into the self, O mighty one.

**13.85.7**  And the wives of the gods, and the maidens, and the mothers of the gods came there together at that time, O upholder of the line of Bhṛgu.

**13.85.8**  Delighted, they came to the sacrifice of the great-souled Paśupati, of Varuṇa; but when the Self-existent beheld them, his seed fell upon the earth.

**13.85.9**  From the spilling of that seed Pūṣan gathered up the dust from the ground and cast it with both his hands into that very oblation-eating fire.

**13.85.10**  Then, when that long sacrificial session was under way with its fire ablaze, as Brahmā was offering oblation, a manifestation came forth there.

**13.85.11**  And taking up with the offering-ladle that seed the moment it was shed, he offered it as one offers clarified butter, and with sacred formulas, O delight of Bhṛgu.

**13.85.12**  Thereupon that mighty one brought forth the host of beings; and from that fiery essence there was born in the worlds all that is fiery in nature.

**13.85.13**  From darkness come the states marked by darkness; goodness too is pervasive, and both alike; the fiery essence is forever endowed with quality, and within darkness lies the ether.

**13.85.14**  And so in all beings there is goodness, fiery energy, and darkness; but when the seed was offered into that fire, three beings came forth, O mighty one.

**13.85.15**  They were men endowed with bodily form, endowed with the qualities arising at their birth: from the very crackling 'bhṛg' came Bhṛgu first, and from the embers came Aṅgiras into being.

**13.85.16**  And from his dwelling upon the embers another came to be, named Kavi; since Bhṛgu arose together with the flames, he is therefore remembered as Bhṛgu.

**13.85.17**  From the rays of light arose Marīci, and from Marīci came Kaśyapa; from the embers came Aṅgiras, my son, and the Vālakhilyas from the heap of stones; and they say, O mighty one, that Atri was born here, and so he is called Atri, 'born just here.'

**13.85.18**  Likewise from the scatterings of ash arose the Vaikhānasas, equal to the host of Brahman-seers, longing for the merits of austerity and sacred learning; and from his unheard-of essence arose the two Aśvins, esteemed for their beauty.

**13.85.19**  The remaining Lords of Creatures were born from his channels; the seers were born from the pores of his skin, and from his sweat came the meters, which have the nature of his impurity.

**13.85.20**  For this reason the seers, endowed with sacred learning, declare on the authority of the Vedas that all the deities are Agni.

**13.85.21**  The kinds of kindling-wood are his months; the exudations are called his fortnights; the days and nights and moments are his bile, and the light is that of Varuṇa.

**13.85.22**  The red they call Raudra, Rudra's own; from the red, gold is held to arise; this is to be understood as belonging to Mitra, and from the smoke the Vasus are remembered to spring.

**13.85.23**  His flames are the Rudras and likewise the Ādityas of great splendor; and so too are his embers declared to be those that stand upon the fire-altars set in the sky.

**13.85.24**  He is the primeval Lord of the world, that supreme Brahman, that abiding one; they call it the granter of every desire, and there he bore the oblation aloft.

**13.85.25**  Then the great god Varuṇa, the Supreme Self, spoke: 'This celestial sacrificial session is mine, and here I am the householder.'

**13.85.26**  'Those three first offspring are mine, of that there is no doubt—know this, O sky-goers; for they are the fruit of my sacrifice.'

**13.85.27**  Agni said: Born from my limbs and brought forth by resort to me, those offspring are mine alone; for Varuṇa is one who has lost mastery of himself.

**13.85.28**  Then spoke Brahmā, the teacher of the worlds, the Grandsire of the worlds: 'Those offspring are mine alone, for it was my seed that was offered.'

**13.85.29**  'I am the utterer of the sacred formula and the offerer of the seed; his is the fruit whose seed it is, if the seed be held the cause.'

**13.85.30**  Then the hosts of gods, approaching the Grandsire, spoke, all of them with palms joined together and bowing low with their heads in salutation.

**13.85.31**  'We all, O lord, and the world with all that moves and is still, are entirely your offspring; therefore let Agni Vibhāvasu and the lord god Varuṇa each obtain the desire he longs for.'

**13.85.32**  And Varuṇa, by his nature the lord of the water-creatures, born of Brahmā, took first as his offspring Bhṛgu, who shone with the splendor of the sun.

**13.85.33**  The Lord assigned Aṅgiras to Agni for the sake of his offspring; and the Grandsire, knower of the truth, took Kavi for his own offspring.

**13.85.34**  Thus Bhṛgu was renowned as Varuṇa's, a doer of the work of begetting; the glorious Aṅgiras as Agni's; and Kavi, of great renown, as Brahmā's. The lines of Bhṛgu and of Aṅgiras in the world bear the mark of the world's continuance.

**13.85.35**  These three are all foremost among the twice-born, Lords of Creatures; understand that all this lineage is theirs.

**13.85.36**  Bhṛgu had seven sons, equal to Bhṛgu in their qualities: Cyavana and Vajraśīrṣa, and Śuci, and Aurva likewise.

**13.85.37**  Śukra and Vareṇya the mighty, and Savana—these are the seven, all Bhārgavas, all of Varuṇa's line, in whose lineage you too belong.

**13.85.38**  And Aṅgiras had eight sons; they too are declared to be of Varuṇa's line: Bṛhaspati and Utathya, and Vayasya, and Śānti.

**13.85.39**  Ghora, Virūpa, Saṃvarta, and Sudhanvan, remembered as the eighth—these eight, all born of Agni, are devoted to knowledge and free from affliction.

**13.85.40**  The sons of Kavi, who is Brahmā's, are also declared to be of Varuṇa's line: eight of them, endowed with the qualities arising at their birth, knowers of Brahman, blessed.

**13.85.41**  Kavi and Kāvya and Viṣṇu, and the wise Uśanas likewise, and Bhṛgu, and Virajas, and Kāśī, and Ugra the knower of dharma.

**13.85.42**  These are the eight sons of Kavi; by them the whole world is spread out; for these are Lords of Creatures, by whom these creatures came to be.

**13.85.43**  Thus the world is forever filled by the offspring and descendants of Aṅgiras and of Kavi, and by those born in the line of Bhṛgu, O tiger among Bhṛgu's race.

**13.85.44**  And Varuṇa, the mighty Lord, took first, O brāhmaṇa—Kavi, my son, and Bhṛgu as well; therefore those two are remembered as belonging to Varuṇa.

**13.85.45**  The crested god, the oblation-eater, took Aṅgiras; therefore all who are of his line are to be known as descendants of Aṅgiras.

**13.85.46**  Brahmā the Grandsire was of old propitiated by the deities, who said: 'These lords of the world will carry us across through their progeny.'

**13.85.47**  'All of them are Lords of Creatures, all of them are surpassing ascetics; by your grace they will carry this everlasting world across.'

**13.85.48**  'And likewise may they be founders of lineages, enhancers of your splendor, all knowers of the Veda, and masters of speech.'

**13.85.49**  'Holding to the side of the gods, gentle, sprung from the Lord of Creatures, these great seers attain austerity and the highest practice of chastity.'

**13.85.50**  'For all of us, and these too, are your offspring alone, O lord; for you are the maker of the gods and of the brāhmaṇas, O Grandsire.'

**13.85.51**  'Setting Marīci at the head, and all the Bhārgavas too—regarding them as our offspring, we ask your pardon, O Grandsire.'

**13.85.52**  'In this very form they will beget creatures, and will establish themselves anew at the beginning and the end of each age.'

**13.85.53**  Thus did this come to pass of old at the sacrifice of that great-souled one, the best of the gods, at the world's beginning, as he bore the form of Varuṇa.

**13.85.54**  Agni, Brahmā, Paśupati, Śarva, Rudra, the Lord of Creatures—this is the settled tradition: that gold is indeed the offspring of Agni.

**13.85.55**  And in the absence of fire, those who know the authorities place gold in the stead of fire upon the altars, O son of Jamadagni, on the showing of the Vedic revelation.

**13.85.56**  One offers oblation to the fire in a tuft of kuśa grass, with gold set there; and when the oblation is made, the Lord deems delight-giving prosperity to abide therein.

**13.85.57**  Therefore we have heard that all the deities have Agni as their highest; for Agni was brought forth from Brahmā, and from Agni in turn came gold.

**13.85.58**  Therefore those who, beholding dharma, give gold—they give all the deities together: so have we heard.

**13.85.59**  And for him, free of darkness, going to the supreme goal, there are worlds; in the world of heaven he would be consecrated to the kingship over kings, O Bhārgava.

**13.85.60**  He who, when the rising of the sun has come, gives gold accompanied by rite and sacred formula—he wards off the evil dream.

**13.85.61**  He who gives the moment the sun has risen, his evil is shaken off; for one who gives gold at midday, it destroys the evil that is yet to come.

**13.85.62**  He of steadfast vow who gives gold at the evening twilight attains to dwelling in the same world as Brahmā, Vāyu, Agni, and Soma.

**13.85.63**  And in the worlds where Indra dwells he gains a blessed standing; having won renown in this world, his evil stilled, he rejoices.

**13.85.64**  Thereafter he comes to be peerless forever in the other worlds; his movement is unobstructed, and he becomes one who goes wherever he wills.

**13.85.65**  And he does not fall away from those worlds, but enjoys the great reward forever; having given imperishable gold, he attains the most abundant worlds.

**13.85.66**  But he who, having kindled the fire toward the rising of the sun, should give with a vow in view—he attains all his desires.

**13.85.67**  That gift they call Agni himself, the bringer of happiness; endowed with whatever excellence is desired, it is remembered as setting all good things in motion.

**13.85.68**  Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed by Vasiṣṭha, the valorous son of Jamadagni gave gold to the brāhmaṇas and was released from his sin.

**13.85.69**  All this have I declared to you, O lord of the earth—the fruit of the giving of gold, and its peerless origin from Agni.

**13.85.70**  Therefore do you too bestow abundant gold upon the brāhmaṇas; by giving gold, O king, you shall be released from all sin.

**13.86.1**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: The grandsire has set forth here at length, according to the ordinances, the virtues of the gift of gold as attested by the scriptures.

**13.86.2**  But touching the cause of the origin of gold that has been declared here—how did Tāraka meet his death? That tell me.

**13.86.3**  He was said to be unslayable by the gods, O lord of the earth; yet his death has not been recounted by you here in full.

**13.86.4**  This I wish to hear from you, O upholder of the Kuru line—the slaying of Tāraka in its entirety; for great is my curiosity.

**13.86.5**  Bhīṣma said: Their endeavour having failed, O king of kings, the gods and the sages alike urged the Kṛttikās to undertake the rearing of the child.

**13.86.6**  For not one among the goddesses was able by her own might to bear that embryo of Agni, the knower of all that is born.

**13.86.7**  Then Pāvaka, the purifier, was pleased with those six for their bearing of the embryo, by reason of his own outpoured splendour and supreme potency.

**13.86.8**  Those six Kṛttikās nourished the embryo of Jātavedas; into their six channels was the whole splendour of Agni deposited, O lord.

**13.86.9**  Then, their limbs wholly compassed about by the splendour of that growing and high-souled boy, they could find ease nowhere.

**13.86.10**  Then, their limbs encompassed by that splendour, when the appointed time was come, all those Kṛttikās gave birth to the embryo together, O bull among men.

**13.86.11**  Then the Earth received that embryo, which from its six seats had come into oneness, near the city of Kāntī.

**13.86.12**  That embryo, of celestial form, blazing, bright as Pāvaka, having reached a divine thicket of reeds, grew up, fair to behold.

**13.86.13**  The Kṛttikās beheld that child, splendid as fire; and tenderness arising, out of affection they nourished him with the flowing of their milk.

**13.86.14**  He became Kārttikeya throughout the three worlds, with all that moves and is unmoving; from his being poured forth he attained the state of Skanda, and from dwelling in a covert he became Guha.

**13.86.15**  Then the three-and-thirty gods, and the quarters with their guardian lords, Rudra and Dhātṛ and Viṣṇu, Yajña, Pūṣan, Aryaman, Bhaga,

**13.86.16**  Aṃśa and Mitra and the Sādhyas, the Vasus, Vāsava, the two Aśvins, the Waters, Vāyu, the Sky, the Moon, the lunar mansions, the planets, the Sun—

**13.86.17**  and other separate beings, those that are offered in oblation to the gods, came there to behold that prince, the son of the flaming one; and the sages praised him, and the Gandharvas likewise sang.

**13.86.18**  That prince of six faces and twice-six eyes, dear to the twice-born, broad-shouldered, twelve-armed, with the lustre of Fire and the Sun,

**13.86.19**  as he lay couched within the reed-clump—beholding him, the gods together with the sages won the highest joy, and deemed the Asura already slain.

**13.86.20**  Then the gods, every one of them, did all that was pleasing to him, and to him at his play they gave playthings and flocks of birds.

**13.86.21**  Suparṇa gave him for his vehicle a peacock with bright-hued plumage, and the Rākṣasas gave him both a boar and a buffalo.

**13.86.22**  Varuṇa himself bestowed a cock resembling fire; the Moon gave a ram, and the Sun a radiant splendour.

**13.86.23**  And the goddess, mother of cattle, gave kine by hundreds of thousands; Agni gave a goat endowed with good qualities, and Ilā much fruit and flower.

**13.86.24**  Sudhanvan gave a cart and a chariot with measureless pole; Varuṇa gave auspicious celestial serpents of his own kind; and Surendra gave lions and tigers and panthers and other fanged beasts.

**13.86.25**  and many fearsome beasts of prey, and parasols of various kinds; and hosts of Rākṣasas and Asuras there were who followed that lord.

**13.86.26**  But beholding him as he grew, Tāraka sought by many devices to slay him, yet he could not slay that mighty one.

**13.86.27**  The gods, having honoured the dweller in the covert with the office of commander, told him of that outrage which Tāraka had wrought.

**13.86.28**  Then Guha, grown to full strength, of mighty valour, the lordly commander of the divine host, slew the Dānava Tāraka with his unfailing spear.

**13.86.29**  When the Asura had been slain by that prince as though in sport, Surendra was once more established as lord upon the kingdom of the gods.

**13.86.30**  Then valorous Skanda shone forth as commander, the lord and protector of the gods, and a doer of what was dear to Śaṃkara.

**13.86.31**  This same blessed one of golden form, the son of Pāvaka, ever a youth, attained to the generalship of the gods.

**13.86.32**  Therefore gold is held auspicious, an imperishable and excellent jewel, born together with Kārttikeya, deemed the supreme splendour of Fire.

**13.86.33**  Thus did Vasiṣṭha relate to Rāma of old, O Kaurava; therefore strive after the giving of gold, O ruler of men.

**13.86.34**  For Rāma, having given gold, was freed of all his sins, and won in heaven a high place hard for men to attain.

**13.87.1**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: The duty of the four orders, O righteous one, has been declared by you, O sinless lord; even so now declare to me in full the rite of the śrāddha, O king.

**13.87.2**  Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīṣma the son of Śāntanu then set about to expound this whole rite of the śrāddha.

**13.87.3**  Bhīṣma said: Hearken attentively, O king, to this auspicious ordinance of the śrāddha—wealth-giving, fame-bestowing, conducive to offspring, the sacrifice to the fathers, O scorcher of foes.

**13.87.4**  By gods, Asuras, and men, by Gandharvas, serpents, and Rākṣasas, by Piśācas and Kiṃnaras, the fathers are ever to be honoured.

**13.87.5**  Having first honoured the fathers, men afterward satisfy the gods; therefore with all endeavour should a man honour them ever.

**13.87.6**  The śrāddha of the fathers, O great king, is called the anvāhārya; and its performance with flesh, by ordinance, was the rite first appointed.

**13.87.7**  On all days are the fathers gladdened by the śrāddhas performed; yet I shall declare to you, for each lunar day, the merits and demerits of each.

**13.87.8**  On whatsoever days the śrāddhas, when performed, yield what fruit, O sinless one—all this I shall duly recount; learn it of me.

**13.87.9**  Worshipping the fathers on the first lunar day, a man obtains in his own house women fair-formed, bearing comely offspring, lovely to look upon, and rich in children.

**13.87.10**  On the second are born daughters; on the third, panegyrists; on the fourth there come to be in the house many small cattle.

**13.87.11**  On the fifth, to those who perform it, O king, are born many sons; and men who perform it on the sixth come to share in radiance.

**13.87.12**  He who performs the śrāddha on the seventh becomes a sharer in the harvest, O king; performing it on the eighth, a man obtains gain in trade.

**13.87.13**  To him who performs the śrāddha on the ninth come single-hooved beasts in plenty; and to him who performs the śrāddhas on the tenth, the kine increase.

**13.87.14**  A man who performs it on the eleventh becomes a sharer in base metals, O king; and sons radiant with sacred lore are born within his house.

**13.87.15**  To him who strives at the rite on the twelfth there is ever seen abundant silver of varied kind, and gold delightful to the mind.

**13.87.16**  Performing the śrāddha on the thirteenth, a man becomes foremost among his kinsmen; yet inevitably the young men of his house come to die.

**13.87.17**  A man who performs the śrāddha on the fourteenth becomes a partaker in battle; but offering on the new-moon day, he obtains all his desires.

**13.87.18**  In the dark fortnight, beginning with the tenth and excepting the fourteenth, the lunar days are commended for the rite of the śrāddha—not so are the others.

**13.87.19**  And even as the latter fortnight is held superior to the former, so for the śrāddha is the afternoon superior to the forenoon.

**13.88.1**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: What gift made to the fathers becomes imperishable, O lord? What oblation avails for a long season, and what conduces to endlessness?

**13.88.2**  Bhīṣma said: The oblations in the rite of the śrāddha that the knowers of the śrāddha know—hear of me those that fulfil desire, and their fruit, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

**13.88.3**  With sesame, with rice and barley, with beans, with water, and with roots and fruits—by the śrāddha so offered the fathers are gladdened for a month, O king.

**13.88.4**  A śrāddha abounding in sesame is imperishable, Manu declared; and among all things that may be eaten, sesame is held to hold the foremost place.

**13.88.5**  With fishes the satisfaction of the host of fathers lasts two months; with mutton, men say, three months; and with hare's flesh, four months.

**13.88.6**  With goat's flesh the fathers are gladdened five months, O king; with boar's flesh six months; and seven months with the flesh of fowl.

**13.88.7**  Eight months with the flesh of the spotted deer, and nine indeed with that of the ruru deer; and with the flesh of the gavaya the satisfaction lasts ten months.

**13.88.8**  With buffalo's flesh the fathers' contentment lasts eleven months; but when the śrāddha is offered with cow's milk and the like, it is said here to last a full year.

**13.88.9**  As with the produce of the cow, so likewise is it with milk-rice joined with clarified butter; and with the flesh of the vādhrīṇasa the satisfaction lasts twelve years.

**13.88.10**  Rhinoceros-flesh given at the offering to the fathers avails for endlessness; and the kālaśāka herb, and red goat, are said likewise to conduce to endlessness.

**13.88.11**  And here too they sing verses sung by the fathers, O Yudhiṣṭhira; the blessed Sanatkumāra of old spoke them unto me.

**13.88.12**  "May there be born in our line one who would offer us, on the thirteenth day, under the asterism Maghā, in the sun's southern course, milk-rice joined with clarified butter;

**13.88.13**  or with goat's flesh, or with red goat, under those very Maghās, one of steadfast vows, duly fanned with the ear-fan amid the shadows of elephants."

**13.88.14**  Many sons should be desired, that even one of them might journey to Gayā, where stands renowned throughout the worlds that fig-tree which makes the offering imperishable.

**13.88.15**  Water, root, fruit, flesh, or food given at the offering to the fathers—whatsoever is mingled with honey conduces to endlessness.

**13.89.1**  Bhīṣma said: The śrāddhas that Yama declared to Śaśabindu—hear of me those that fulfil desire, severally under each lunar mansion.

**13.89.2**  The man who should ever perform the śrāddha under the conjunction of the Kṛttikās, having set up the sacred fires, would sacrifice with offspring and free of fever.

**13.89.3**  He who longs for offspring should offer under Rohiṇī; he who longs for vigour, under the lordly deer-mansion; but a man giving the śrāddha under Ārdrā becomes one of cruel deeds.

**13.89.4**  A man performing the śrāddha under Punarvasu becomes a sharer in the harvest; and one who longs for nourishment should strive at the śrāddha under Puṣya.

**13.89.5**  Giving the śrāddha under Āśleṣā, a man begets heroic sons; and offering the śrāddha under the Maghās, he becomes foremost among his kinsmen.

**13.89.6**  Giving the śrāddha under the Phalgunīs, the giver becomes blessed with fortune; under the Uttaras he becomes a sharer in offspring, and under Hasta a sharer in fruit.

**13.89.7**  Giving the śrāddha under Citrā, he obtains comely sons; worshipping the fathers under the conjunction of Svāti, he lives by trade.

**13.89.8**  A man striving at the rite to the fathers under the Viśākhās becomes rich in sons; and performing it under the Anurādhās, he sets in motion the wheel of empire.

**13.89.9**  A man, O foremost of the Kuru line, going with faith and self-restraint before him, attains to sovereignty by making the offering under Jyeṣṭhā.

**13.89.10**  Under Mūla he should attain health, and under the Aṣāḍhās fame unsurpassed; and under the Uttarāṣāḍhās, freed of sorrow, he would range the earth.

**13.89.11**  Performing the śrāddha under Abhijit, he would obtain the highest knowledge; and giving the śrāddha under Śravaṇa, he would go after death to the supreme course.

**13.89.12**  He who performs the śrāddha under Dhaniṣṭhā becomes a sharer in kingdoms and meets with no calamity; performing it under the lunar mansion of Varuṇa, a man attains success in the healing art.

**13.89.13**  Performing it under the Pūrva-Proṣṭhapadā stars, he gains goats and sheep in abundance; performing it under the Uttarā stars, he gains cattle by the thousand.

**13.89.14**  Resorting to Revatī, he gains wealth wrought of much silver; under Aśvayuj he obtains horses, and under the Bharaṇī stars the highest length of life.

**13.89.15**  Having heard this ordinance of the śrāddha, Śaśabindu acted accordingly; without hardship he conquered the earth, and he ruled it.

**13.90.1**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: To brāhmaṇas of what sort should the śrāddha-offering be given, O grandsire? O tiger of the Kurus, you ought to expound this to me.

**13.90.2**  Bhīṣma said: A kṣatriya versed in the law of giving should not scrutinize brāhmaṇas in rites for the gods; but in the rite for the ancestors, scrutiny is held to be proper.

**13.90.3**  The deities here honor the offering by their divine splendor when they draw near; therefore a man should have the offering given to all the gods alike.

**13.90.4**  But at the śrāddha, O great king, the wise man should examine the brāhmaṇas by their family, character, age, and form, by their learning and noble birth.

**13.90.5**  Of these, some are defilers of the row and others are sanctifiers of the row; those who are unworthy of the row, O king, I shall now name—hear of them.

**13.90.6**  The gambler, the slayer of an embryo, the consumptive, the cattle-herder, the misshapen, the village drudge, the usurer, the professional singer, the seller of every kind of ware,

**13.90.7**  the house-burner, the poisoner, the eater of food in a vessel of adultery's child, the seller of soma, the seafarer, the king's servant, the oil-presser, the forger of false coin,

**13.90.8**  he who quarrels with his father, he in whose house there is a paramour, the man falsely accused, the thief, and he who lives by a manual craft,

**13.90.9**  the maker of festival days, the informer, the betrayer of friends, the adulterer, the teacher of those without vows, and likewise the renegade who turns his back on his own kindred,

**13.90.10**  he who roams about with dogs, he who has been bitten by a dog, he who marries before an elder brother, the man of diseased skin, the defiler of his teacher's bed, the actor-dancer, the temple-priest who lives off idols, and he who lives by reading the stars—

**13.90.11**  these one should know to be unworthy of the row, the basest of the twice-born, together with those of little wit who give instruction to śūdras.

**13.90.12**  A one-eyed man defiles sixty, a eunuch a hundred, O king; and a man with white leprosy, when seated in the row, defiles as far as his eye can reach.

**13.90.13**  What is eaten with the head wrapped, what is eaten facing south, and what is eaten while still shod—all this one should know to belong to the demons.

**13.90.14**  What is given grudgingly and what is given without faith—all this Brahmā has apportioned as the share of the lord of the asuras.

**13.90.15**  Dogs and defilers of the row should by no means look upon the offering; therefore one should give it in an enclosed place and scatter sesame seeds around it.

**13.90.16**  When the sesame offering is omitted, the flesh-eating fiends, the hosts driven by wrath, the yātudhānas, and the piśācas plunder that oblation.

**13.90.17**  For as long as one unfit for the row gazes upon those eating in the row, so long does he strip the foolish giver of his reward.

**13.90.18**  But these, O best of the Bhāratas, are to be known as sanctifiers of the row; those who are such I shall now declare—examine these brāhmaṇas here.

**13.90.19**  Brāhmaṇas who have completed their study of the Veda and their vows of the bath are, every one, worthy of the row; and those whom I shall name as worthy should be known as sanctifiers of the row.

**13.90.20**  He who has thrice kindled the Nāciketa fire, the keeper of the five fires, the knower of the Trisuparṇa hymn, the master of the six Vedāṅgas, he born of a line of brahma-given marriages, the chanter of the Sāman, the singer of the Jyeṣṭha-sāman,

**13.90.21**  he who is obedient to his mother and father, the learned man of ten generations of Veda-knowers, and he who always approaches his lawful wives only in their season—such a brāhmaṇa, accomplished in Veda, learning, and vow, indeed purifies the row.

**13.90.22**  The student of the Atharvaśiras, the chaste one of restrained vows, the speaker of truth, he of righteous conduct, and he who is devoted to his own appointed duty—

**13.90.23**  and those who have toiled in ritual bathing at holy fords, and who have been bathed in the final ablution of sacrifices accompanied by their proper mantras—

**13.90.24**  those free of anger, free of fickleness, patient, self-controlled, masters of their senses, and devoted to the welfare of all beings—these one should invite to the śrāddhas; what is given to them is imperishable, for these indeed are sanctifiers of the row.

**13.90.25**  These others too, O great king, are to be known as sanctifiers of the row: the ascetics who know the law of liberation, the men of yoga of well-practiced vows,

**13.90.26**  those who, intent and pure, recite the ancient lore to the best of the twice-born, those who are versed in commentary, and those who delight in grammar,

**13.90.27**  those who study the Purāṇa and the treatises on dharma as well, and who, having studied them duly and rightly, act according to their precepts,

**13.90.28**  he who has dwelt completely in his teacher's household, the speaker of truth, the giver of a thousand gifts, the foremost in all the Vedas and in all the recitations—

**13.90.29**  as far as these gaze upon the row, so far do they purify it; and because of this purifying of the row, each is called a sanctifier of the row.

**13.90.30**  Even a single such man, born of a line of brahma-given marriages, can sanctify the offering from a distance of two and a half krośas—so the knowers of Brahman declare.

**13.90.31**  If one who is neither officiating priest nor teacher takes the foremost seat unauthorized by the officiants, he carries off, along with the row, only ill-deserved demerit.

**13.90.32**  But if he is a knower of the Veda, free of all the faults of the row, and is not a fallen man, O king, then he is indeed a sanctifier of the row.

**13.90.33**  Therefore with all care one should examine and invite brāhmaṇas devoted to their own duties, self-controlled, well-born, and deeply learned.

**13.90.34**  He whose śrāddhas and oblations are devoted chiefly to friends gratifies neither the ancestors nor the gods, and he does not attain to heaven.

**13.90.35**  He who turns the śrāddha into a gathering of friends does not travel by the path of the gods; like a fig loosed from its stalk, the man who befriends at the śrāddha falls away from the world of heaven.

**13.90.36**  Therefore the performer of the śrāddha should not honor a friend with it; let him give his friends wealth to win their goodwill instead. Whom he regards as neither foe nor friend, that neutral man let him feed at the rites for gods and ancestors.

**13.90.37**  As seed sown in barren ground does not sprout, and the sower of it gains no return on his seed, so the śrāddha eaten by the unworthy yields its fruit neither here nor hereafter.

**13.90.38**  For a brāhmaṇa who has not studied dies down like a fire of straw; to him the śrāddha should not be given, for no oblation is poured upon ashes.

**13.90.39**  The mere feeding of friends is a fee fit for piśācas; it reaches neither the gods nor the ancestors. Drained of merit, it wanders here below, like a cow within the stable that has lost its calf.

**13.90.40**  As clarified butter poured upon a fire that has died reaches neither the gods nor the ancestors, so too is what is given to dancing and to singing, and the fee one bestows upon one who knows no sacred verse.

**13.90.41**  The fee given to one who knows no sacred verse destroys them both and nourishes neither; deadly and contemptible, in its falling it casts the departed of such men down from the path of the gods.

**13.90.42**  Those who ever observe the discipline of the seers, O Yudhiṣṭhira, steadfast and knowers of all dharma—the gods know such brāhmaṇas to be true.

**13.90.43**  The seers are to be understood as devoted to recitation, devoted to knowledge, devoted to austerity, and devoted to ritual action, O Bhārata.

**13.90.44**  The ancestral offerings are to be entrusted to those devoted to knowledge, O Bhārata; and among them, whatever brāhmaṇas there be who revile no one—those are the most excellent.

**13.90.45**  But those who revile others in their chatter—one should not feed them at the śrāddhas; for brāhmaṇas reviled, O king, can destroy a family through three generations.

**13.90.46**  The word of the Vaikhānasa seers is heard, O king: from afar should one examine the brāhmaṇas who have mastered the Veda, and whether they be dear or hateful, in them should one set the śrāddha.

**13.90.47**  Though a man should feed a thousand thousands of men who know no sacred verse, a single knower of the mantras, when pleased, outweighs them all, O Bhārata.

**13.91.1**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: By whom was the śrāddha first conceived, at what time, and of what nature? In the age of Bhṛgu and Aṅgiras, by which of the two sages was it ordained?

**13.91.2**  What things are to be shunned in the śrāddhas, and what roots and fruits, and what kind of grain is to be avoided? Tell me this, O grandsire.

**13.91.3**  Bhīṣma said: How the śrāddha came into being, at what time, of what nature, and by whom it was conceived—hear this from me, O lord of men.

**13.91.4**  There was Atri, son of the Self-existent, O Kauravya, a supreme seer of mighty splendor; in his line, O great king, was born he remembered as Dattātreya.

**13.91.5**  Dattātreya had a son named Nimi, rich in austerity; and to Nimi there was born a son named Śrīmān, endowed with glory.

**13.91.6**  At the close of a full thousand years, having performed hard austerities, his being overtaken by the law of time, he came to his death.

**13.91.7**  But Nimi, having performed the purifications by the rite ordained, fell into bitter grief, wholly given over to sorrow for his son.

**13.91.8**  Then, having made the funeral offerings on the fourteenth day, the great-minded one, brooding upon that very grief, awoke at the close of night.

**13.91.9**  As he awoke, his self veiled by grief, having drawn his mind back from the objects of sense, his understanding ranged far and wide.

**13.91.10**  Then, composed in mind, he pondered the ordinance of the śrāddha—what foods, what roots, and what fruits had been dear to his son,

**13.91.11**  and whatever others were prescribed, and whatever were beloved of him—all these the man rich in austerity determined in his mind.

**13.91.12**  On the night of the new moon, O greatly wise one, having summoned brāhmaṇas and honored them, he himself fashioned all the seats of grass coiled toward the right.

**13.91.13**  Then he brought forward seven brāhmaṇas together to the meal, and the lord gave them food of wild millet, with everything save salt.

**13.91.14**  Then darbha grasses, their tips pointing south, were laid upon the seats and at the feet of the brāhmaṇas who were partaking of the food.

**13.91.15**  And having set the darbhas with their tips toward the south, well-disciplined and pure, he offered the rice-ball to Śrīmān, pronouncing his name and lineage.

**13.91.16**  Having done this, that best of sages, tormented by great remorse at the confounding of dharma he had wrought, fell to thinking:

**13.91.17**  "What is this I have performed, never done by the sages before? How may the brāhmaṇas not consume me with their curse?"

**13.91.18**  Then he called to mind the founder of his own line; and no sooner was he thought upon than Atri, rich in austerity, came near.

**13.91.19**  Then Atri, seeing him so wasted with sorrow for his son, the imperishable one comforted him deeply with kindly words:

**13.91.20**  "O Nimi, this rite for the ancestors has been conceived by you, O man of austerity. Let no fear be yours: this dharma was foreseen of old by Brahmā himself.

**13.91.21**  This dharma, ordained by the Self-existent, has been conceived by you; for save the Self-existent, who else could have set forth this ordinance of the śrāddha?

**13.91.22**  And I shall declare to you further the most excellent ordinance of the śrāddha, ordained by the Self-existent, O son; perform it, and mark my words.

**13.91.23**  Having first performed the fire-rite with its proper mantras, O man of austerity, then ever offer to Aryaman, to Soma, and to Varuṇa;

**13.91.24**  and to those All-gods who ever range together with the ancestors—for them the shares were appointed by the Self-existent himself.

**13.91.25**  And here the Earth is to be praised, she who upholds the offering—called the Vaiṣṇavī, the Kāśyapī, and likewise the Imperishable.

**13.91.26**  And at the bringing of water, the all-pervading Varuṇa is to be praised; thereafter Agni and Soma are here to be gratified, O sinless one.

**13.91.27**  The gods named the Fathers were indeed fashioned by the Self-existent, those drinkers of vapor of exceeding blessedness; for them the shares were apportioned.

**13.91.28**  Honored by the śrāddha, they are released from sin; the ancestral line is sevenfold, as foreseen of old by the Self-existent.

**13.91.29**  And the All-gods, fire-faced, were reckoned of old; I shall declare the names of those great-souled ones who are worthy of a share.

**13.91.30**  Sahas, Kṛti, Vipāpman, Puṇyakṛt, and Pāvana likewise; Grāmaṇi, Kṣema, Samūha, and Divyasānu as well.

**13.91.31**  Vivasvat, Vīryavat, Hrīmat, Kīrtimat, and Kṛta; Vipūrva, Somapūrva, and Sūryaśrī — so they are named.

**13.91.32**  Somapa, Sūryasāvitra, Dattātman, Puṣkarīyaka; Uṣṇīnābha, Nabhoda, Viśvāyu, and Dīpti too.

**13.91.33**  Camūhara and Suveṣa, Vyomāri, Śaṃkara, Bhava; Īśa, Kartṛ, Kṛti, Dakṣa, Bhuvana, and Divyakarmakṛt.

**13.91.34**  Gaṇita and Pañcavīrya, Āditya, and Raśmimat; Saptakṛt, Somavarcas, Viśvakṛt, and Kavi too.

**13.91.35**  Anugoptṛ and Sugoptṛ, Naptṛ, and Īśvara; Jitātman, Munivīrya, Dīptaloman, and Bhayaṃkara.

**13.91.36**  Atikarman and Pratīta, Pradātṛ, and Aṃśumat; Śailābha, Paramakrodhin, Dhīroṣṇi, and Bhūpati.

**13.91.37**  Srajin, Vajrin, and Varin — these are the eternal Viśvedevas, the greatly blessed ones, now celebrated, who move within the range of time's course.

**13.91.38**  Among grains, kodrava and pulaka are unfit for the śrāddha rite; among condiments, asafoetida; among vegetables, the onion and the garlic.

**13.91.39**  The onion, the drumstick plant, the carrot and their kind, the gourd-fruit and the bottle-gourd, and black salt as well.

**13.91.40**  The flesh of the domestic boar, and whatever has not been consecrated, black cumin, biḍa salt, and the slow-ripening melon, sprouted shoots and the like, and water-chestnuts — these too are to be shunned here.

**13.91.41**  One should avoid all manufactured salt, and likewise the fruit of the rose-apple; and at śrāddha rites one should reject whatever has been sneezed or wept upon.

**13.91.42**  At an offering of food, of oblations to the gods or to the fathers, the sight of a dog is to be deplored; neither the fathers nor the gods take pleasure in such an oblation.

**13.91.43**  When the offering of food is set forth, the Caṇḍāla and the dog-eater must be kept away, as must the wearer of ochre robes, the leper, the outcaste, and even the slayer of a brahmin.

**13.91.44**  A brahmin of mixed birth, and a kinsman who has fallen from his estate — these the wise must exclude when the offering of food is set forth.

**13.91.45**  Having thus spoken of old to the sage born of his own line, the venerable Atri, rich in austerity, departed to the divine assembly hall of the Grandfather.

**13.92.1**  Bhīṣma said: When the rite had been set in motion in this manner, all the great sages performed the sacrifices to the fathers with action prescribed by ordinance.

**13.92.2**  The sages, ever devoted to dharma, having made their food-offerings, performed too the libation of water from sacred fords, steadfast in their vows.

**13.92.3**  Gratified by the offerings of food given by the four orders, O Bhārata, the fathers and the gods could not, however, digest the food.

**13.92.4**  Stricken by indigestion, those gods together with the fathers, oppressed by the offered food, betook themselves to Soma.

**13.92.5**  Reaching Soma, the fathers, afflicted with indigestion, said: "We are tormented by the offered food; let some remedy be devised for us in this matter."

**13.92.6**  Then Soma answered them: "If you desire a remedy, O gods, go to the abode of the Self-Existent; he will ordain what is best for you."

**13.92.7**  At Soma's word, those gods together with the fathers, O Bhārata, approached the Grandfather, who was seated upon the peak of Meru.

**13.92.8**  The fathers said: "By the offered food, O Lord, we are sorely tormented. Show us your grace, O God; let some remedy be ordained for us."

**13.92.9**  Hearing these words of theirs, the Self-Existent spoke thus: "Here at my side is Fire; he will ordain what is best for you."

**13.92.10**  Agni said: "Together, dear ones, we shall eat when the offering of food is set forth, and along with me you shall digest the food — of this there is no doubt."

**13.92.11**  Hearing this, the fathers were thereupon freed of their distress; and for this very reason, O king, the foremost portion is given to Agni.

**13.92.12**  When the offering is made with Agni first, O bull among men, the brahma-rākṣasas do not defile that offering, and the demons turn away when the god of radiant light is present.

**13.92.13**  First one should offer the rice-ball to the father, then to the grandfather, and then to the great-grandfather: this is held to be the ordinance of the śrāddha.

**13.92.14**  At the śrāddha, with collected mind, one should recite the Sāvitrī over each rice-ball; one should say "to Soma," and likewise "to him attended by the fathers."

**13.92.15**  A woman in her courses, or one maimed in her ears, should not attend at the offering; nor are those of another lineage to be admitted.

**13.92.16**  While crossing a body of water, one should call to mind the grandfathers; and upon reaching a river, one should perform the rice-ball offering and libation to the fathers.

**13.92.17**  First having made the water-libation to those born of one's own line, one should then offer a handful of water to the company of friends and kinsmen.

**13.92.18**  When one crosses the water yoked to a pair of dappled oxen, the fathers indeed long for him, and as he climbs aboard the boat; ever upon the boat those who know offer the water-libation with collected minds.

**13.92.19**  In the half-month of the dark fortnight one should make the food-offerings; for nourishment, long life, vigor, and prosperity attend upon him who is devoted to the fathers.

**13.92.20**  The Grandfather, Pulastya, Vasiṣṭha, and Pulaha, Aṅgiras, Kratu, and the great sage Kaśyapa — these, O best of the Kuru line, are remembered as the mighty lords of yoga.

**13.92.21**  These too are the fathers, O king; this is the supreme ordinance of the śrāddha. The departed, bound to the rice-ball offerings, are by that act set free.

**13.92.22**  Thus, O best of men, has the origin of the śrāddha, as it was first set forth, been declared to you according to tradition. Of the gift of charity I shall now speak hereafter.

**13.93.1**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: If the twice-born, bound by their vows, eat the oblation — food given out of desire to please the brahmins — how can this be, O grandfather?

**13.93.2**  Bhīṣma said: Those bound by vows not enjoined in the Veda, if they eat, are merely doers of their duty; but those who eat while under vows enjoined in the Veda, O Yudhiṣṭhira, have broken their vow.

**13.93.3**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: That fasting which the common folk here call austerity — is this indeed austerity, or might true austerity be something else?

**13.93.4**  Bhīṣma said: The fasting for a month or half a month that people deem austerity — he who thereby injures his own constitution is neither an ascetic nor a knower of dharma.

**13.93.5**  The very perfection of renunciation is taught to be the highest austerity; one may be ever a faster and likewise ever a celibate.

**13.93.6**  A brahmin may be ever a sage, and ever may he sacrifice to the gods, though he be a householder devoted to dharma, and ever wakeful, O Bhārata.

**13.93.7**  He may be ever an eater of ambrosia, and ever may he be pure; ever a speaker of truth he may be, and ever may he be self-restrained.

**13.93.8**  He may be ever an eater of the remnants, and ever loving toward his guests; ever an abstainer from flesh he may be, and ever may he be pure.

**13.93.9**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: How may one be ever a faster and a celibate, O king? And how may one be an eater of the remnants, and how a lover of guests?

**13.93.10**  Bhīṣma said: He who does not eat again in between the evening meal and the morning meal becomes ever a faster.

**13.93.11**  Approaching his wife only in her season, a man becomes ever a celibate; and a man given to charity becomes ever a speaker of truth.

**13.93.12**  By not eating flesh in vain, one becomes an abstainer from flesh; by giving in charity, one becomes pure; and even sleeping by day, one remains free of sleep.

**13.93.13**  The man who ever eats only after his dependents and guests have eaten — know, O Yudhiṣṭhira, that he eats nothing but ambrosia.

**13.93.14**  The man who does not eat while the brahmins have not yet eaten — by that very abstinence heaven is won by him.

**13.93.15**  He who eats what is left over after the gods, the fathers, his dependents, and his guests — him they call an eater of the remnants.

**13.93.16**  For such men, boundless worlds in the abode of Brahmā are remembered, attended by Apsarases and Gandharvas, O lord of men.

**13.93.17**  Together with the deities, the guests, and the fathers they feast, and they take delight with their sons and grandsons; theirs is a course beyond all surpassing.

**13.94.1**  Yudhiṣṭhira said: Men bestow various gifts upon the brahmins; between the giver and the receiver, which is the more excellent, O grandfather?

**13.94.2**  Bhīṣma said: The twice-born who accepts a gift from a virtuous man, or likewise from one who is not virtuous, incurs little fault if the giver is endowed with merit, but he sinks down if the giver is devoid of it.

**13.94.3**  On this point, too, they recount this ancient tale, the dialogue between Vṛṣādarbhi and the Seven Sages, O Bhārata.

**13.94.4**  Kaśyapa, Atri, and Vasiṣṭha, then Bharadvāja and Gautama, Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, and the virtuous Arundhatī as well.

**13.94.5**  Now Gaṇḍā was the serving-maid of all of them, and the Śūdra Paśusakha was her husband.

**13.94.6**  All of them, performing austerities, of old wandered over this earth, striving through meditation toward the eternal world of Brahmā.

**13.94.7**  Then there came a great drought, O delight of the Kurus, in which this world was reduced to a hard struggle for life and gripped by hunger.

**13.94.8**  And once, of old, at a certain sacrifice, the son of Śibi, the patron of the rite, gave his own son to the officiating priests as a sacrificial fee.

**13.94.9**  At that time, O lord, that short-lived boy came to the end ordained by fate; and they, scorched by hunger, surrounded him and stood near.

**13.94.10**  Then, seeing the patron's son bereft of life, those most excellent sages, tormented by hunger, set to cooking him in a pot, O Bhārata.

**13.94.11**  In this world of mortals where there was nothing to eat, those ascetics, seeking to preserve their own lives, fell into a wretched mode of living for the sake of food.

**13.94.12**  Now the lord of the earth, the Śaibya king Vṛṣādarbhi, roaming along the road, beheld them cooking, sorely afflicted.

**13.94.13**  Vṛṣādarbhi said: Accepting a gift brings deliverance; it is indeed a nourishment for those who receive. Hear, O you rich in austerity, what wealth is to be found with me.

**13.94.14**  Dear to me indeed is the brahmin who asks; I would give you a thousand she-mules, each one with its sire and brought to birth, all of them swift-going and white of coat.

**13.94.15**  Bulls that sustain a family, by the hundred upon hundred, draught-oxen fair and fit for the yoke I would give you wholly, broad and well-fed bearers of the earth, and as many milch-cows, choice young heifers, gentle of disposition.

**13.94.16**  Choice villages, rice and barley and savory things, and other jewels hard to obtain — what shall I give? Do not turn your minds to forbidden food; for your nourishment, what shall I bestow upon you?

**13.94.17**  The sages said: O king, a gift from a king is sweet to the taste as honey, yet like poison. Knowing this, why do you set temptation before us?

**13.94.18**  The warrior-order leans upon the brahmin as upon a deity; for this brahmin, made spotless by austerity and well pleased, gives pleasure to the gods themselves.

**13.94.19**  Sometimes the austerity of a brahmin is born here in but a single day; and a king's gift, once received, would burn that away as a forest fire consumes.

**13.94.20**  "May welfare, along with your giving, be ever yours, O king; let all be given to those who seek it" — having so spoken, they then departed.

**13.94.21**  That flesh of theirs, wise as they were, remained even yet uncooked; and so, abandoning it, they all went off into the forest, still longing for food.
